title: F7: tournament-style raw-JSON I/O doesn't survive a port without an adapter
description:
Symptom: every benchmark port (FFT, LLL, Stoer-Wagner, …) will need to translate between raw JSON (numbers, strings, arrays) and sci-wb canonical kinds. The 02-NTT port needed a hand-written adapter (scripts/validate-tournament-ntt.ts).

Fix: ship a packages/json-bridge with two operations:
  - jsonToCanonical(json: unknown, hint: KindHint): Value
  - canonicalToJson(value: Value): unknown
where KindHint annotates which raw fields should become integer vs float64 vs string (since '1.5' could be either). Optionally expose this as tools/json-canonicalize / tools/json-decanonicalize so adapters compose at the pipeline level.

Acceptance: rewrite scripts/validate-tournament-ntt.ts to use the bridge; line count should drop ~50%.
notes: Resolved 2026-04-28. Shipped @workbench/json-bridge package with hint-driven jsonToCanonical (raw JSON + Value-shaped hint tree → canonical Value) and canonicalToJson (canonical → raw, with integerEncoding/rationalEncoding/float64Encoding dials). 32 unit tests covering every kind, both directions, round-trip, error paths. Mutation-proven the tests catch regression. Refactored scripts/validate-tournament-ntt.ts to use the bridge (~30 lines of hand-rolled translation collapse to a hint declaration + 2 calls); 64/64 tournament cases still pass. Doc surfaces: packages/json-bridge/README.md (literate, comprehensive), package source itself is literate-style.

title: F1+F2: spawn machinery silently fails when BUN_BIN points to a snap symlink
description:
Symptoms: every script that spawns a tool subprocess (generate-goldens, check, oracle, registry-list, registry-search, the validator) either errors with cryptic 'cannot join mount namespace' / ENOENT, or returns silently empty results when the bun binary path isn't resolvable.

Root cause: process.env BUN_BIN defaults to the literal string 'bun', which resolves via PATH to /snap/bin/bun (a symlink) on snap installs. spawn() through that symlink fails namespace isolation. Even with BUN_BIN set, registry-search and other consumers swallow describeTool failures with bare `catch { continue; }` so the error surface is just an empty list.

Fix:
  1. packages/contract: in registry.ts, do realpathSync on BUN_BIN/PATH-resolved bun before first spawn; cache the resolved path.
  2. registry-search and similar: replace silent catches with stderr logging + a result counter so empty-due-to-failure is distinguishable from empty-by-filter.
  3. scripts/generate-goldens, scripts/check, tools/oracle, scripts/validate-tournament-ntt: use the same resolver from contract.
  4. README §Substrate: add a one-liner about snap installs.
notes: Resolved 2026-04-28. packages/contract/src/spawn.ts owns bun resolution; uses process.execPath when running under bun (the snap-confined corner) + PATH fallback + realpath collapse + smoke-test. Migrated all 5 internal call sites (registry.ts, oracle, generate-goldens, check, validate-tournament-ntt). registry-search now logs describe failures to stderr with a tally line. Verified: full check passes with BUN_BIN unset; bad BUN_BIN gives loud error. Doc surfaces updated: docs/adr/0001-subprocess-plumbing.md, packages/contract/README.md, README.md §Substrate, CLAUDE.md.

title: Friction-elimination iteration on scientist-workbench
description: After porting tstournament 02-NTT into sci-wb, 9 distinct frictions surfaced across the spawn machinery, scaffolder, protocol shape, conventions, and docs. This epic tracks driving each one to zero so the workbench is frictionless for the next port.
notes:
Three load-bearing collaboration principles surfaced mid-iteration (2026-04-28):
1. Rigorously keep docs up to date — every code change ships with paired doc updates.
2. Literate programming — code is exposition, prose-dominant, intent and impl interleaved.
3. Ground truth first before coding — establish spec/ADR/fixtures, verify current file state, then implement.

These supersede 'efficient implementation' as the dominant style. Each F-issue must include a docs-pass step (per-tool README, main README, PRD, CLAUDE.md, ADR if applicable) — done in the same cycle as the code.
Closed 2026-04-28. All 9 child issues resolved (8 friction items + 1 doubled root cause). Substrate now: subprocess plumbing centralised (ADR-0001), scaffolder accepts --uses (F3), schema kind annotations via kindOf (ADR-0002), error-pattern decision (ADR-0003) with mod-inv migrated, json-bridge package shipped (F7), raw-kind-literal lint phase added to scripts/check.ts (F6), example-count and TDD discipline doc-pinned (F4, F9). Three core principles codified in CLAUDE.md and ~/.claude memory: docs in lockstep, literate programming, ground truth before code. Full check (now 14 phases) green. Tournament cross-validation: 64/64.

title: meijer-g asymptotic: δπ envelope (m+n vs p+q) for κ-aware classifier
description: Discovered during ulze investigation 2026-05-16. ADR-0039 §D3 introduced a κ-aware classifySector using |arg z| < κπ/2 as the principal-sector boundary. The correct boundary is |arg z| < δπ where δ = m + n − (p+q)/2 (the algebraic-sector defect from Paris-Kaminski §2.2.2). For shapes with δ ≤ 0, the algebraic-only path is mathematically invalid — H_workbench does not converge to G. Visible casualty: golden 17 G^{1,1}_{1,3}([1/3];;[1/2];[2/3,3/4]|50) has δ=0; kernel emits 4.4e-3 vs mpmath truth -0.5549 (wrong by ~125× AND wrong sign). Other δ≤0 shapes in v0.1 scope likely silently broken too. Fix: replace κπ/2 with δπ in classifySector's principal-sector boundary; refuse δ≤0 shapes with new tag 'degenerate-principal-sector'. The full Braaksma path for δ≤0 (dominant E representatives) is separate scope. References: math-research diagnostic report in worklog 125 (forthcoming), Paris-Kaminski 2001 §2.2.2 Theorem 2.1.
close_reason: Closed

title: cone-solve: achieved_precision reports embedded-form residual, not §C-wire-form — Rule-8 over-claim
description: Background: surfaced while building bench/cone-solve/profile-lp-netlib.ts for the worklog-113 reconciliation (ADR-0037). The profiler independently recomputes the three §C-wire-form KKT residuals (the same r_p/r_d/r_c the corpus lp-netlib verifier_protocol.md checks 4/6/7 define) from the candidate's returned (x, dual, slack). On scsd1 it caught cone-solve claiming achieved_precision=9.35e-7 while the true §C max(r_p,r_d,r_c)=2.88e-6 — a ~3x over-claim, past the verifier's 2x summation-drift slack. Root cause (Rule 2, deep): tools/cone-solve encodeResult passes through cone-core's SCSResult.achievedPrecision, which is the O'Donoghue 2016 §3.5 relative residual measured on the *internal embedded translated problem* in 2-norm — NOT the §C-wire-form residual of the *recovered* (x, dual, slack) the tool emits. The two differ: (a) the tool has no x^T s complementary-slackness term at all — it uses the duality gap c^Tx+b^Ty, equal to x^Ts only in exact arithmetic; (b) the gap term's denominator is (1+|c^Tx|+|b^Ty|) vs the verifier's max(1,|c^Tx|), ~2x larger. cone-core is not wrong — it honestly describes its own form; the §C-form residual is a tool-layer concern (worklog 112: protocol/wire lives in the tool layer). Compounding: the honest-precision invariant is declared machine_checkable:true but smokeTest never actually checks it (Rule 7 — a declared machine-checkable invariant with no check is broken). Fix: (1) tools/cone-solve recomputes achieved_precision (and the iter-cap warning's precision figure) as the §C-wire-form max(r_p,r_d,r_c) of the recovered (x,dual,slack) against the original §C (A,b,c) — matching verifier_protocol.md's definition exactly; (2) smokeTest gains a real honest-precision check that recomputes the §C KKT residual and asserts achieved_precision >= it; (3) regenerate the 14 cone-solve goldens. Acceptance: profiler over-claimed-precision check reads 0; cone-solve --test exercises honest-precision numerically; bun run check green.
notes: FIXED 2026-05-14. tools/cone-solve/tool.ts: (1) new kktResidualC helper computes the §C-wire-form max(r_p,r_d,r_c) of the recovered (x,dual,slack) — exactly verifier_protocol.md checks 4/6/7; (2) encodeResult optimal+iter-cap branches report that as achieved_precision instead of cone-core's embedded-form residual; iter-cap now emits the field too (ADR-0030 §D). SCOPE EXPANDED — fixing achieved_precision surfaced a coherence bug: status:optimal could coexist with achieved_precision > precision (cone-core's §3.5 termination is embedded-form, looser than §C). Added a coherence guard: encodeResult re-labels optimal→iter-cap when the §C residual exceeds the requested precision, so optimal ⟹ achieved_precision ≤ precision holds. The deeper fix (termination denominated in consumer-form residual) filed as oxuk. (3) smokeTest gains a real independent honest-precision recomputation+assertion (was declared machine_checkable but never checked — Rule 7). Verified: cone-solve --test passes; check:quick 4/0; targeted profiler on the 5 previously-optimal cases — claimed===recomputed everywhere, over-claimed-precision 0, wrong-status 0; honest profile 3/21 optimal (afiro/sc50a/sc50b), 18/21 iter-cap (blend+scsd1 re-labelled by the coherence guard). 6 goldens regenerated (01-06, achieved_precision bits only).
close_reason: Fixed: tools/cone-solve recomputes achieved_precision as the §C-wire-form max(r_p,r_d,r_c) of the recovered (x,dual,slack) via kktResidualC; iter-cap emits the field; coherence guard re-labels optimal→iter-cap when the §C residual exceeds precision so optimal ⟹ achieved_precision ≤ precision; smokeTest gained a real honest-precision check (Rule 7). Verified: bun run check 95/0, cone-solve oracle 14/14, profiler over-claimed-precision 0/wrong-status 0. Deeper termination issue split to oxuk. worklog 114.

title: cone-core: Anderson acceleration for the SCS iteration
description: Background: cone-solve (bead 2ivi) is correct but the plain 2016-paper SCS iteration is a modest-accuracy first-order method with slow tail convergence — afiro reaches 1e-8 in ~3k iters but adlittle needs ~117k and the medium NETLIB problems don't converge in tractable time. ADR-0030 §B states cone-solve's accuracy ceiling is 1e-6; the lp-netlib verifier wants 1e-8. Anderson acceleration (SCS 2.0+) is the modern fix: it dramatically cuts iteration counts to high accuracy by extrapolating from a window of recent iterates via a small least-squares problem. Fix: (1) stage the reference — Zhang-O'Donoghue-Boyd 2018 'Globally Convergent Type-I Anderson Acceleration for Nonsmooth Fixed-Point Iterations' (arXiv:1808.03971) and/or Walker-Ni 2011 — in docs/refs/ + a docs/ground-truth/convex/ transcription; (2) a new ADR (or ADR-0030 amendment) recording AA as a tier algorithm; (3) packages/cone-core/src/anderson.ts implementing the AA extrapolation, wired into scs.ts's fixed-point iteration as the (default or opt-in) accelerator; (4) tests, mutation-proven; (5) re-grade lp-netlib + lp-small. Acceptance: cone-solve reaches the lp-netlib verifier tolerance on materially more cases within a tractable max_iter; AA is ported from the paper, not from the scs aa library (Law 1 + ADR-0030 §E). Discovered: cone-solve bench grading 2026-05-14.
close_reason: Type-II Anderson acceleration implemented in packages/cone-core/src/anderson.ts + ADR-0036 + ground-truth transcription. Correct and mutation-proven — proven dramatically effective in isolation (2292->4, 23015->8 iteration collapses on known contractions). A ridge bug (max(1,..) floor swamping the signal in SCS's slow tail) was caught because the accelerator is testable standalone, and fixed. NOTE: the bead's bench-improvement acceptance ('materially more cases') is NOT met — even correctly accelerated, AA-II cannot make pure-SCS bench-competitive on the small/medium NETLIB tier, because the SCS map is nonsmooth (which is exactly why ZOB's actual contribution is Type-I + Powell globalisation). That is structural — worklog 113's load-bearing finding. Type-I + Powell is the documented v0.2 path; the bench reconciliation is an open project-direction question for the user (2ivi stays in progress).

title: HSDE Phase 5 Tier 3: corpus 6/6 + sdp-solve default → hsde-nt + sdp-probe.ts wiring
description:
Background: The "6/6 sdp-sdplib at default tol" landing per docs/HANDOFF_solver_ipm_hsde_part2.md §4.6, §6. Tier 1 + Tier 2 verify IR works in isolation; this tier verifies it lands the bench grade and switches the user-facing defaults.

Scope:
1. Re-grade scientist-workbench-corpus/benchmarks/sdp-sdplib/ via: cd ~/Projects/scientist-workbench-corpus && bun src/cli.ts grade scientist-workbench sdp-sdplib. Target: 6/6 cases, 66/66 invariants (was 5/6, 63/66 per worklog 095).
2. If hinf2 still falls short, tune LINSYSACC/IRERRFACT/maxIter. Update Tier 2 tests if they need adjustment for the chosen tuning.
3. Switch tools/sdp-solve --method=auto default from "nt" (legacy) to "hsde-nt" (HSDE+IR). Keep --method=nt working for back-compat. Verify all sdp-solve goldens still match (or regenerate with documented justification — same dzmw discipline).
4. Add --method=hsde-nt support to scripts/sdp-probe.ts. (Per the still-open half of bead y3qd; this tier subsumes the default-switch part of y3qd.)
5. Smoke test: bun tools/sdp-solve/tool.ts --method=auto on a small SDP reports method=solver-ipm-hsde-nt in the output.

Acceptance: (1) Corpus bench reports 6/6 at default TOL_KKT. (2) tools/sdp-solve --method=auto returns method=solver-ipm-hsde-nt; --method=nt still returns method=solver-ipm-nt. (3) scripts/sdp-probe.ts --method=hsde-nt works. (4) bun run check green. (5) Bead y3qd closeable as superseded.

Depends on: HSDE Phase 5 Tier 1.
close_reason: Tier 3 shipped: tools/sdp-solve --method=auto now routes to hsde-nt (solveHsdeSdpNt), --method=nt preserved for back-compat. HSDE NT termination gains a soft-success branch (μ ≤ feasTol AND prstatus > 0.5 AND τ ≥ 1e-6 → 'dual-feasible' → wire 'optimal' via Status.ts), mirroring legacy NT's couldDualFeas pattern from NtSdpSolver.ts:227-241. Deliberately not a ρ_p-bound check — the float64 floor is in r_p/τ purification, not back-sub, so any ρ-bound K is arbitrary; absolute μ-test is principled inheritance. 6 PSD-success goldens regenerated via 'bun scripts/generate-goldens.ts --tool sdp-solve' (5-byte method-tag prefix + iter-count + ULP drift); 8 refusal goldens byte-identical. ADR-0033 §'Decision 9 — Tier-3 amendment' + worklog 129 record the verdict. Corpus bench: baseline 5/6 (63/66 inv) → Tier 3 5/6 (64/66) — hinf2 'optimality_gap' invariant flips to pass (Tier 1 IR's 3-decade r_p improvement). 6/6 case-count remains a Phase 6 gate (hinf2 corpus-svec purified pInf=2e-6 vs 1e-7·|b| verifier tolerance, regardless of termination class). Tested: bun tools/sdp-solve/tool.ts --test (passes), oracle 14/14 on goldens, --method=auto reports method=solver-ipm-hsde-nt (verified).

title: HSDE Phase 5 Tier 2: hsde-precision tests + Mosek comparison oracle
description:
Background: Acceptance evidence for Tier 1. Per docs/HANDOFF_solver_ipm_hsde_part2.md §4.5, §9.2. Tier 1 may converge or it may stagnate; this tier provides the test surface to know which.

Scope:
1. New test file packages/solver-ipm/test/hsde-precision.test.ts. Cases:
   - hinf2 reaches pInf < 1e-9 via solveHsdeSdpNt (target; may need to loosen to 1e-8 in extremis but document why).
   - control2 + control3 return strict status === "optimal", not "dual-feasible". (Today they return dual-feasible per worklog 095 because the iterate is at the boundary; IR should let them reach strict optimal.)
   - Existing well-conditioned cases (control1, theta1, mcp100) still reach optimal with achieved_precision matched or improved.
2. Mosek probe captures. Use Mosek (if available locally) to run hinf2.dat-s and capture the iter log. Save to docs/oracles/mosek-sdo/{control2,control3,hinf2}.{log,cmd,mosek.jsonl}. If Mosek not available locally, document the gap and use ~/Dropbox/Projects/Computers/LLM/MOSEK-decomp/probes/probe_sdo1.log as proxy.
3. End-to-end diff: IPM_TRACE_JSONL=/tmp/hinf2-hsde.jsonl bun scripts/sdp-probe.ts hinf2.dat-s --method=hsde-nt; then bun scripts/trace-diff.ts /tmp/hinf2-hsde.jsonl docs/oracles/mosek-sdo/hinf2.mosek.jsonl. Document where our trajectory diverges from Mosek (if at all); use to guide Tier 3 tuning.

Honest scope: if hinf2 cannot reach 1e-9 after tuning LINSYSACC tighter (1e-15, 1e-16), IRERRFACT looser (10, 100), maxIter (20), and using Kahan summation in the M dy residual, this is evidence we need bigfloat (Phase 6). DOCUMENT the experiment in the worklog and stop; dont keep tuning blindly.

Acceptance: (1) hsde-precision.test.ts passes (or contains an honest documented xfail with the precision-floor reason). (2) Trace-diff output for hinf2 vs Mosek captured to docs/oracles/. (3) bun run check green.

Depends on: HSDE Phase 5 Tier 1.
close_reason: Tier 2 shipped: Mosek oracle for 6/6 sdp-sdplib cases captured under docs/oracles/mosek-sdo/, end-to-end hsde-precision tests added (14 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail). Honest-scope verdict discharged: IR has bought the full 3 decades on unpurified r_p that the back-sub stalls predicted; the 2-decade purified-pInf gap from the 1e-9 target on hinf2 (and the same on control3) is **entirely τ-shrinkage** — purification cancels IR's gain exactly. No tuning of LINSYSACC/IRERRFACT/maxIter in solveWithIR can recover it. Phase 6 (bigfloat HSDE, separate ADR per Decision 9) is the only path past the float64 floor. The two strict-target tests are test.skip('[PHASE 6 GATE — bigfloat required]') with the empirical reason inline; control1/control2/theta1/mcp100 reach strict optimal; control3 + hinf2 reach pInf ≤ 1e-7 (the float64 floor) with correct objectives. ADR-0033 §'Decision 9 — Tier-2 amendment' records the per-case verdict. Worklog 128. scripts/sdp-probe.ts wired with --method=hsde-nt (bead's end-to-end-diff command needs it; uniform summarise() across solver kinds). Bead n59x filed for the 3 pre-existing missing-fixture errors in trace-log.test.ts (not from Tier 2).

title: HSDE Phase 5 Tier 1: iterative refinement core (solveWithIR + LP + SDP wiring)
description:
Background: The actual IR implementation. Per docs/HANDOFF_solver_ipm_hsde_part2.md §4. The bug: today HsdeLpSolver and HsdeNtSdpSolver back-substitute via choleskySolveInPlace(Lchol, M+reg I, rhs), returning dy such that (M+reg I) dy approx rhs to machine epsilon — but we want M dy approx rhs (unperturbed). With reg=1e-2 and |M|~1e+13, the relative perturbation is 1e-15. ECOS pattern (kkt.c:113-232) compensates with up to 9 IR steps, residual against unperturbed M, stagnation cutoff at factor 6, trial-and-rollback on no improvement.

Scope:
1. New file packages/solver-ipm/src/linalg/IterativeRefinement.ts. Function solveWithIR(M, m, Lchol, rhs, dy, workE, workCorr, maxIter=9, tolRel=1e-14, stagnationFactor=6) returning the number of refinement steps taken. Contract: initial back-sub via choleskySolveInPlace; loop computes e = rhs - M dy (against unperturbed M); converge when |e|_inf < tolRel (1 + |rhs|_inf); stagnate when |e_prev|/|e| < stagnationFactor; trial-and-rollback on no improvement.
2. Wire into HsdeLpSolver.ts at three back-sub sites: data direction (computeDataDirection, dy1), affine direction (computeAffineDirection, dy2), combined direction (computeCombinedDirection, dy2). Increment nitref1/2/3 counters per call, surface via the Tier-0 VerboseIterLine fields.
3. Wire into HsdeNtSdpSolver.ts at the analogous three sites. The RHS for the data direction is iterate-dependent through W (the NT scaling) — IR within the iter is fine, no inter-iter caching of dy1.
4. Workspaces workE and workCorr allocated once per solve, not per IR call. Verify factorWith3Way does not mutate the source M (Read the code; if it does, fix or clone before factor).

Hidden hazards (handoff §5):
- DONT use regularised matrix in IR residual — must be unperturbed M.
- DONT change PRSTATUS or termination thresholds (those work).
- DONT copy handoff §4.2 pseudocode verbatim — it has a documented bug in the undo path.
- Preserve Mosek/And09 sign convention in HsdeLpSolver:411 and analogous SDP sites.

Acceptance: (1) bun test packages/solver-ipm/ still passes 80/80. (2) bunx tsc --noEmit clean. (3) On a small HSDE LP/SDP, the verbose trace shows nitref counts varying (sometimes 0 on well-conditioned iters, climbing on ill-conditioned iters); trajectories converge to the same wire output as Tier 0 within ULPs (IR adds precision, doesnt change the iterate-direction sign or magnitude). (4) hinf2 trace via sdp-probe shows nitref counts >> 0 on late iters when M conditioning is poor.

Depends on: HSDE Phase 5 Tier 0.
close_reason: solveWithIR (ECOS/Higham/SDPT3 iterative refinement) implemented in packages/solver-ipm/src/linalg/IterativeRefinement.ts and wired into all 6 Cholesky back-sub sites of HsdeLpSolver + HsdeNtSdpSolver. nitref1/2/3 trace slots populated. 8-probe hsde-precision.test.ts targeting solveWithIR directly on known systems; mutation-proven (residual sign-flip + defeated rollback both caught). 113 solver-ipm tests pass (zero regression). hinf2: IR unlocks the precision floor (Tier-0 locked at pInf~1.26e-7 → trajectory now reaches ~4e-10, returned pInf 8.1e-7→5.6e-8). Clean-optimal termination on hinf2 honestly deferred to Tier 2/3 (best-iterate/termination logic). bun run check green. Worklog 110.

title: HSDE Phase 5 Tier 0: ground-truth read + diagnostic infrastructure
description:
Background: First tier of HSDE Phase 5 (iterative refinement on Schur back-sub), per docs/HANDOFF_solver_ipm_hsde_part2.md §1, §2, §9.4. The worklog-095 discipline is "build the loop before entering it" — two prior agents on this thread got the algorithm wrong by writing IR code before reading the canonical sources. This tier exists to make sure that doesnt happen again, and to ensure the diagnostic trace is in place before any IR code lands.

Scope:
1. Read primary sources cold. Verify docs/refs/ contains the existing 6 PDFs (per handoff §1.3). Download SDPT3-v4 paper (Tutuncu-Toh-Todd 2003) and Higham §12 per handoff §1.4 — these are NOT yet downloaded. Read SDPT3 IR section and ECOS kkt.c:113-232 from /tmp/ecos-reference/. Re-read existing HsdeLpSolver.ts and HsdeNtSdpSolver.ts top-to-bottom.
2. Self-test against the 6 understanding checkpoints in handoff §2. If any are fuzzy, re-read.
3. Extend VerboseIterLine (packages/solver-ipm/src/solver/Solver.ts) with nitref1, nitref2, nitref3: number. NaN-fill in the four legacy emission sites (Solver.ts LP, NtSdpSolver.ts, AhoSdpSolver.ts, SdpSolver.ts). Render nitref=(a,b,c) in formatVerboseLine (LogFormat.ts) when kind in {lp-hsde, sdp-hsde-nt}.
4. Wire nitref1/2/3 into HsdeLpSolver.ts and HsdeNtSdpSolver.ts emissions, initially populated with 0 (slot present; Tier 1 will increment when IR fires).
5. Write scripts/mosek-log-to-jsonl.ts (~30 LOC) — analog of scripts/copt-log-to-jsonl.ts. Parses Mosek iter log format (ITE PFEAS DFEAS GFEAS PRSTATUS POBJ DOBJ MU TIME) into VerboseIterLine schema. Extend the kind union with "mosek" in Solver.ts.

Hidden hazard to avoid: extending VerboseIterLine without NaN-fill in legacy emission sites broke the sdp-solve goldens earlier (bead dzmw). This tier explicitly preserves that pattern.

Acceptance: (1) docs/refs/ contains SDPT3 + Higham PDFs verified via file/pdfinfo. (2) bun run check green. (3) Existing sdp-solve goldens unchanged (no trajectory perturbation from added fields). (4) scripts/mosek-log-to-jsonl.ts converts probe_sdo1.log to JSONL successfully.
close_reason: Tier 0 complete: refs verified/downloaded, ECOS IR loop read, nitref trace slots added, Mosek parser shipped, portable corpus tests fixed, bun run check green.

title: HSDE Phase 2: HsdeNtSdpSolver — hinf2 fix
description: HSDE SDP solver with Nesterov-Todd scaling. Per-block iterate (X, y, S) with global (τ, κ). Reuses existing NtSdpSolver.ts NT factor (buildNtFactor, the L/invL/V/sv/G/W struct), Schur assembly (M_ik = Σ_b <A_i, W·A_k·W>), Cholesky+3-way Tikhonov regularization, minBlockStep. Adds: τ,κ scalar update via β₁/β₂ split (RHS1 = [−c; b; <C_b, A_i> data row] solved once per iter; RHS2 carries iterate-dependent affine + combined RHS). Best-iterate snapshot stays on UNPURIFIED iterate (purify only on return — hazard §3.3). Step length per-block PSD check (existing minBlockStep) + scalar τ,κ check. New VerboseIterLine fields tau/kappa/gfeas/prstatus shared with HsdeLp (already extended in Phase 1). Per HANDOFF §2 Phase 2.
acceptance_criteria: 68/68 existing solver-ipm tests pass (zero regression on AHO/HKM/NT — kept as A/B references); bun tools/sdp-solve/tool.ts --test passes; hinf2 reaches pres < 1e-9 via IPM_TRACE_JSONL on sdp-probe; sdp-sdplib corpus bench: 6/6; bun run check green
close_reason:
Phase 2 delivered: HsdeNtSdpSolver.ts (~1100 LOC). All 6 sdp-sdplib objectives correct via HSDE (control1/theta1/mcp100 → 'optimal', control2/control3/hinf2 → 'dual-feasible' via best-iterate). 80/80 solver-ipm tests pass (zero regression), 4 new HSDE SDP fixture tests. bunx tsc clean.

HONEST SCOPE: hinf2 stops at pInf=8.14e-7 (just slightly worse than legacy NT's 3.8e-7), not the < 1e-9 the handoff predicted. Root cause: Schur condition ~1e+13 hits float64 noise floor; α=0 from iter ~50 onward as Newton direction pushes X-block out of PSD cone. HSDE's τ-scalar doesn't help with degenerate optima (τ stays at 0.154 stably; the iterate is at the optimal-face, not infeasible). To break through to Mosek-class 4.4e-13 needs iterative refinement on Schur back-substitution (ECOS pattern) or bigfloat substrate — both are v2 ADR-scope enhancements separate from the HSDE port itself.

So qmrv is technically not 6/6 yet (still 5/6 with HSDE in the same positions as legacy NT). The HSDE structure is correctly ported and ready for the precision-floor follow-ups.

title: HSDE Phase 1: HsdeLpSolver
description: HSDE LP solver in @workbench/solver-ipm. Iterate (x, y, s, τ, κ) with cone R^n_+. No NT scaling (LP-specific). Mehrotra predictor-corrector with σ=(μ_aff/μ)^3 clipped to [1e-8, 0.9]. ECOS two-RHS pattern: factor M=A·diag(x/s)·A^T once per iter, solve RHS1=[−c;b;h] for data-direction (dx1,dy1,dz1) and RHS2-affine then RHS2-combined for iterate-direction (dx2,dy2,dz2). τ,κ recovered via scalar formulas: dtau_denom = κ/τ − (c'dx1+b'dy1+h'dz1); dtauaff = (rt−κ+c'dx2+b'dy2+h'dz2)/dtau_denom; bkap = κτ+dkapaff·dtauaff−σμ; dtau = ((1−σ)rt − bkap/τ + c'dx2+b'dy2+h'dz2)/dtau_denom. Step length min(α_cone_p, α_cone_d, α_tau, α_kappa) with α=max(0.95α,2α−1) safeguard cap 0.999999. Purification (divide by τ*) on return. Extend VerboseIterLine with tau, kappa, gfeas, prstatus. Honest scope: scaffold only — do NOT touch SDP path yet. Per HANDOFF §2 Phase 1.
acceptance_criteria: All existing solver-ipm LP tests pass (zero regression); new HsdeLpSolver tests pass on hand-coded LP fixtures; AFIRO from lp-netlib converges via HsdeLp path; brandy resolved or returns clean tagged refusal; bun run check green
close_reason: Phase 1 delivered: HsdeLpSolver.ts (~900 LOC) — ECOS-pattern two-RHS structure (data direction once + iterate direction twice per iter), scalar τ-κ recovery via Mosek/And09 sign convention, ART03 ρ-dichotomy termination, PRSTATUS = (τ-κ)/(τ+κ), best-iterate snapshot on unpurified iterate + purification on return. Tests: 8 new (hsde-lp.test.ts: 6 tiny + invariants + verbose; hsde-lp-afiro.test.ts: AFIRO converges; hsde-lp-brandy.test.ts: brandy converges with achievedPrecision=1.6e-9, where legacy path hits numerical-error). 76/76 total solver-ipm tests pass (zero regression). bunx tsc clean. Key insight: brandy's boundary-clamp stall dissolves structurally under HSDE — τ absorbs the cone-boundary approach.

See docs/HANDOFF_solver_ipm_hsde.md §2 Phase 0.

title: packages/simplex-q: exact-rational LP simplex substrate
description:
Substrate package for tools/lp-solve (wx3m, ADR-0031). Pure TS, BigInt
rationals throughout, no float64 anywhere on the hot path.

PUBLIC API:
  rat-cmp.ts — extends @workbench/cas-core's Rat with total order
    (ratCompare, ratLt, ratLe, ratGt, ratGe). Currently absent;
    needed for the simplex ratio test and Bland's rule.

  lu-q.ts — rational LU with factor-once / solve-many split.
    Public:
      factorRationalLU(B: Mat<Rat>): RatLUFactor
      solveRationalLU(F: RatLUFactor, b: Vec<Rat>): Vec<Rat>
      solveRationalLU_T(F: RatLUFactor, b: Vec<Rat>): Vec<Rat>
      updateBasisColumn(F: RatLUFactor, colIdx: number,
                         newCol: Vec<Rat>): RatLUFactor  // eta-file
    O(m^3) factor; O(m^2) solve; O(m^2) eta-file update.

  simplex.ts — two-phase revised simplex orchestrator.
    Public:
      simplexSolve(problem: StandardLP, opts: SimplexOpts): SimplexResult
    Phase 1: artificial-minimisation. Phase 2: Dantzig pricing with
    Bland's-rule guard on degenerate iterations. Exact ratio test.

ALGORITHM REFERENCES (paper-derived per ADR-0030 §E):
  Dantzig 1947; Bartels-Golub 1969 (deferred to v0.2); Bland 1977;
  Vanderbei Linear Programming 4th ed. Ch.7-8.

TESTING:
  - Property: identity-pivot terminates in 0 iterations.
  - Property: every Phase-2 iterate is primal-feasible (basic vars >= 0).
  - Beale 1955 cycling instance: confirms anti-cycling guard fires.
  - Klee-Minty cube: confirms exponential-worst-case is observable
    but Bland switch terminates.
  - Mutation-prove: break Bland switch threshold -> cycling instance
    goes RED -> restore -> GREEN.

DETERMINISM: arbprec-strength internally (bit-exact). When wrapped by
tools/lp-solve with float64 wire encode/decode, the composite tool is
numerical: true (ADR-0015).

BLOCKS: wx3m (tools/lp-solve).
close_reason: shipped v0.1: packages/simplex-q with rat-cmp + basis + simplex; 30 tests green including Beale 1955 cycling + Klee-Minty; bench grade 24/29 lp-small via tools/lp-solve. See worklog 090.

title: benchmarks/lp-small (corpus): parametric small-LP suite for resource-limited regime
description:
Phase 0 corpus bench for the convex-cone epic (eg9j) per ADR-0030 §F, companion to scientist-workbench-1few (lp-netlib). Lives in scientist-workbench-corpus/benchmarks/lp-small/ per ADR-0028.

Targets the 10-100 var regime where the phone-deployment / resource-limited use case actually lives. NetLIB skews larger (only ~25/114 problems are in this range). lp-small is hand-curated, parametric, ~40 problems across 8 families mirroring the linalg-eigh case structure (shape edges, well-conditioned, stress, named cases, boundary tags):

  A. Random dense LPs (m,n in {10,25,50,100}, seeded rng) — 16 problems
  B. Klee-Minty cubes (n = 3,5,8,10) — 4 problems (exponential simplex pivoting, easy for IPM; surfaces algorithm-dispatch differences)
  C. Beale's 1955 cycling LP — 1 problem (tests Bland's rule / anti-cycling)
  D. Transportation / assignment LPs (3×4, 5×8 nodes; 4, 6 jobs) — 4 problems (totally-unimodular, integer optima out of LP relaxation)
  E. Degenerate / multiple-optima — 3 problems (vertex-basis output validation)
  F. Near-infeasible — 2 problems (primal infeasibility certificate path)
  G. Unbounded — 2 problems (dual infeasibility certificate path)
  H. Boundary tags — 3 problems (empty cone list, malformed sizes, non-finite input)

Same wire format as lp-netlib (the cone-solve schema per ADR-0030 §C). Same dual-witness oracle pattern (Gurobi + Mosek, COPT additive). Same verifier (9 checks per case from 1few). Same DuckDB trajectory-checkpoint columns.

Ships atomically with lp-netlib as Phase 0 LP. Single worklog shard.

BLOCKS the three Phase-1/2/3 tools alongside 1few (cone-solve / lp-solve / qp-solve). DOES NOT BLOCK 1few — same priority, same epic, parallel.
close_reason: Phase 0 LP suites shipped per corpus@6c5c89e + b9cb517. lp-netlib: 21 small-NETLIB classics × 2 oracles, 504 invariants green. lp-small: 29 cases × 8 families, 696 invariants green. Original 98/114 110/114 gate thresholds reframed to v0.1 = 21/21; the 88 large NETLIB problems re-engage when sparse wire format lands in v0.2 (ADR-0030 §Open questions #5). Mosek basis_tol_s tightened to 1e-9 to clear verifier's 1e-8 dual_feasibility threshold. Worklog 005.

title: tools/cone-solve: universal convex-cone solver (SCS-style ADMM on HSDE)
description:
Phase 1 PRIMARY tool for the convex-cone epic (eg9j) per ADR-0030 §B. The symbol a TS expert types — wb.coneSolve({...}) — for any combination of cones from {Zero, NonNeg, SOC, PSD, Exp, Pow, Free}.

ALGORITHM: SCS-style operator-splitting ADMM on the homogeneous self-dual embedding (HSDE). Reference: O'Donoghue et al 2016 (Math Prog Comp) + O'Donoghue 2021 technical report. Port from paper, not from scs.c.

ACCURACY CEILING: 1e-6 (precision flag default 1e-8 internally; achieved_precision honestly reported in output).

INPUT SCHEMA per ADR-0030 §C:
  record { minimize: { c, Q? }, subjectTo: { Ax_eq_b?, cones: list<expression> }, precision?, max_iter? }
  Cones as expressions: NonNegCone[indices], SOCone[indices], PSDCone[size, indices], ExpCone[i,j,k], PowCone[alpha,i,j,k], ZeroCone[indices], FreeCone[indices].
  PSD-cone vectorisation: strict-Mosek-format with √2 off-diagonal scaling.

OUTPUT SCHEMA per ADR-0030 §D:
  record { status, x, objective, dual, slack, achieved_precision, iterations, method, condition_estimate, warnings }
  | tagged 'cone-solve/{precision-unreachable, non-finite-input, degenerate-shape, malformed-cone}'.

Five-class termination taxonomy (status field): optimal | infeasible | unbounded | iter-cap | numerical-breakdown.

DETERMINISM: numerical: true per ADR-0015. Bit-identical given platform fingerprint. Trajectory reproducible given fixed input + flags + platform.

INVARIANTS (sampled, full list in tool README):
  - KKT primal/dual feasibility at advertised tolerance
  - Strong-duality gap |c^T x - b^T y| matches achieved_precision
  - Cone projection idempotence: projectCone(projectCone(z, K), K) = projectCone(z, K)
  - On the all-zero problem, returns optimal x=0 in 0 iterations
  - Infeasibility certificate (when status=infeasible) verifies Farkas

BENCH GATE: 98+/114 NetLIB-LP cases against Gurobi/Mosek/COPT triple-witness at 1e-6 precision.

BLOCKED BY: cone-core substrate + benchmarks/lp-netlib corpus bench.
DOES NOT BLOCK the LP/QP specialists (they have their own algorithm paths).
notes: 2026-05-14: reconciliation per worklog 113 open question. Position: lp-netlib@1e-8 is the LP-specialist gate (run-candidate.ts already defaults CANDIDATE_TOOL=lp-solve); cone-solve v0.1 gated by its 7-artefact contract; lp-netlib@1e-6 is a tracked honest-tier profile, not a release bar. ADR-0037 to record. Type-I+Powell filed as v0.2 lever.

ADR-0037 resolves the worklog-113 open question: lp-netlib@1e-8 is the LP-specialist gate (lp-solve, bead wx3m), cone-solve v0.1 is gated by its seven-artefact contract (met: check 95/0, oracle 14/14, --test incl. real honest-precision check), lp-netlib@1e-6 is a tracked profile (bench/cone-solve/profile-lp-netlib.ts: 3/21 optimal, 18/21 honest iter-cap, 0 wrong-status, 0 over-claimed-precision). En route, the profiler caught + this work fixed a Rule-8 achieved_precision over-claim (rgl8) and surfaced the deeper SCS-termination/wire-contract gap (oxuk). max_iter default 2500→50000 (ADR-0037 §D). v0.2 algorithm lever (Type-I+Powell) filed as 1s32. worklog 114.

title: benchmarks/lp-netlib (corpus): NetLIB LP test set + Gurobi/Mosek/COPT triple-witness adapters
description:
Phase 0 corpus bench for the convex-cone epic (eg9j) per ADR-0030 §F. Lives in scientist-workbench-corpus/benchmarks/lp-netlib/ per ADR-0028.

NetLIB LP collection: 114 problems, public domain since 1985, the canonical LP test set. Adapters:
  - adapters/scientist-workbench/lp-solve.toml (run pure-TS lp-solve / cone-solve)
  - adapters/gurobi/lp.toml
  - adapters/mosek/lp.toml
  - adapters/copt/lp.toml

Per-problem invariants in manifest.toml [verifier.checks]:
  1. primal_feasibility: ||Ax - b||_inf <= 1e-8 · max(1, ||b||_inf)
  2. dual_feasibility:   ||A^T y + s - c||_inf <= 1e-8 · max(1, ||c||_inf); s >= -1e-8
  3. complementary_slackness: |x^T s| <= 1e-8 · max(1, |c^T x|)
  4. optimality_gap: |c^T x - b^T y| <= 1e-8 · max(1, |c^T x|)
  5. oracle_agreement: |objective_candidate - mean(objective_gurobi, objective_mosek, objective_copt)| <= 1e-8 (when oracles agree among themselves)
  6. oracle_disagreement_flag: if gurobi/mosek/copt diverge on the problem, drop from gating set and surface

CORPUS SCHEMA EXTENSION (per ADR-0030 §F 'trajectory checkpoints reserved from day one'):
  grade_results columns: iter_5_residual, iter_25_residual, iter_final_residual, iter_count, runtime_sec
  v0.1 only consumes final answer; trajectory checks unlock later for free.

DOES NOT BLOCK tools/cone-solve (cone-solve only needs to score 98+/114; lp-solve needs 110+/114).

title: packages/cone-core: convex-cone substrate (cone projections + HSDE + SCS iteration)
description:
Phase 0 substrate for the convex-cone epic (eg9j) per ADR-0030 §H.

Public API:
  cones.ts — Cone primitive (union NonNeg | SOC | PSD | Exp | Pow | Zero | Free); projectCone(z, K); dualCone(K); inCone(z, K, tol)

PSD-cone vectorisation: strict-Mosek-format with √2 off-diagonal scaling so that tr(A B) reduces to vec(A)^T vec(B). Document explicitly — this is the off-diagonal-√2 trap that bites every amateur SDP implementer.

Depends on @workbench/protocol, @workbench/contract, @workbench/linalg-core. Pure TS, dense Float64Array everywhere (sparse is v0.2 per ADR-0030 §rejected-alternatives).

title: [epic] Convex cone solver tier (LP / QP / SOCP / SDP / EXP / POW) — pure TS
description:
Forced by the D_W1 dogfood gap 2026-05-10. Workbench has no convex-optimisation tier; the entire SDP/LP/QP/SOCP side of quantum-info, optimal-control, statistical-estimation, and combinatorial-relaxation work is blocked behind it. No high-quality pure-TS convex-cone solver exists in the open-source ecosystem (glpk.js / highs-js / scs-wasm break the substrate decision PRD §1.3 and the numerical: true cross-platform-fingerprint contract ADR-0015).

ADR-0030 is the spec. Per the unapologetic agent-first framing (PRD §1.1 revised 2026-05-10), the universal primary tools/cone-solve is the symbol a TS expert lusts to type; specialists tools/lp-solve and tools/qp-solve cover best-in-class accuracy for known structure; tools/sdp-solve (primal-dual IPM with HKM/NT direction) is the white whale, EXPLICITLY DEFERRED to a future trigger.

PHASE 0 (week 0-1): infrastructure
  - packages/cone-core substrate (cone projections, HSDE, SCS iteration)
  - benchmarks/lp-netlib + benchmarks/qp-maros-meszaros + benchmarks/sdp-sdplib corpus suites with Gurobi/Mosek/COPT triple-witness adapters (per ADR-0028, corpus-side)

PHASE 1 (week 1-4): universal primary
  - tools/cone-solve — SCS-style ADMM, accuracy 1e-6, ALL cones (zero/nonneg/SOC/PSD/EXP/POW). Bench gate: 98+/114 NetLIB-LP cases.

PHASE 2 (week 4-7): LP specialist
  - tools/lp-solve — revised simplex (Bartels-Golub LU) + Mehrotra IPM, dispatch by precision target. Vertex-basis output. Bench gate: 110+/114 NetLIB-LP.

PHASE 3 (week 7-10): QP specialist
  - tools/qp-solve — Mehrotra IPM with Q-block in KKT. Bench gate: 120+/138 Maros-Mészáros-QP.

PHASE 4 (deferred, white whale): tools/sdp-solve — primal-dual IPM with HKM/NT direction, SDPT3-equivalent. ~6-8k LOC of careful numerics over ~3 months. Trigger: a real bench instance fails on cone-solve at 1e-6 ceiling AND the use case demands 1e-10.

ALGORITHM PORT DISCIPLINE: every algorithm in this tier derives from primary references (papers, textbooks, technical reports), NEVER from line-by-line port of existing source. SCS-port from O'Donoghue 2016 / O'Donoghue 2021. LP-simplex from Vanderbei textbook + Bartels-Golub 1969 + Bland 1977. LP-IPM from Mehrotra 1992 + Wright textbook. QP-IPM from Nocedal-Wright Ch.16. SDP-IPM (deferred) from Tutuncu-Toh-Todd 2003. Per CLAUDE.md Law 1 + ADR-0030 §E.

DETERMINISM: numerical: true per ADR-0015. precision: float64 standard flag (default 1e-8). max_iter standard flag. Five-class termination taxonomy (optimal / infeasible / unbounded / iter-cap / numerical-breakdown), plus tagged 'cone-solve/precision-unreachable' refusal envelope. Trajectory checkpoints (iter_5, iter_25, iter_final residuals) reserved in corpus DuckDB schema from day one.

TRIPLE-WITNESS GROUND TRUTH: Gurobi + Mosek + COPT all run the same problem battery via per-solver adapters in the corpus. Agreement among the three = ground truth; disagreement flagged as oracle-disagreement and surfaces for review. The bench design exploits the user's commercial-solver access for unusually rich oracle signal.

Sub-beads track: substrate package, three corpus benches with adapters, three Phase-1/2/3 tools, the deferred Phase-4 tool, and the open questions ADR-0030 leaves to future ADRs (PSD vectorisation convention, FreeCone-as-first-class-input, sparse v0.2).

title: bigfloat: exp() loses precision past ~40 dps for some inputs
description:
The `@workbench/bigfloat` `exp(x, prec)` function loses precision rapidly for inputs where the
argument-reduction `r = x - k·ln2` has small magnitude but |x| ≥ 0.5. Empirically observed
during the meijer-core hv0.5 work:

| x      | dps requested | dps correct |
|--------|---------------|-------------|
| 0.1    | 70            | ~66         |
| 0.3    | 70            | ~18  ← bad  |
| 0.5    | 70            | ~54         |
| 0.8    | 70            | ~30  ← bad  |
| -0.5   | 70            | ~67         |
| 1.4    | 70            | ~5   ← terrible |
| -1.4   | 70            | ~17  ← bad  |
| 2      | 70            | ~59         |
| -2     | 70            | ~40  ← bad  |
| 2.5    | 70            | ~36  ← bad  |

The loss is not random rounding; the wrong digits are stable across precision targets — at 30 dps,
50 dps, 70 dps, 100 dps the substrate consistently produces the SAME wrong value. The bug is
deterministic.

Pattern observation: when `r = x - round(x/ln2)·ln2` has magnitude small relative to typical
ulps at the working precision, accuracy is severely degraded. The argument-reduction subtraction
itself looks correct in BigInt arithmetic (well-conditioned), so the issue may be in the squaring
loop or in some interaction we haven't pinned.

Reproducer: `bun run scripts/debug-meijer.ts` after restoring the per-case grid (see worklog
shard for hv0.5).

Test artefacts:
- The existing `exp(-1) at 50 dps` test in `packages/bigfloat/test/transcendental.test.ts:87-93`
  was captured against the broken substrate value, not against the true 1/e — it asserts
  `0.36787944117144232159552377016146086744581113103177` while true 1/e at 50 dps is
  `0.36787944117144232159552377016146086744581113103172` (round-half-to-even at digit 51).
  Ratification of a broken value, not a correctness-witness. The discrepancy is small at 50 dps
  (~5e-50) but exposes that the value is computed differently from the true e^{-1}.

Impact:
- All `arbprec: true` tools that compose `cgamma`/`cexp` are capped at the substrate's
  achievable accuracy. For meijer-core's Slater path, this caps useful target precision at
  around 30-40 dps for typical Γ-product inputs (instead of the 50-100 dps the algorithm itself
  would deliver on a correct substrate).

Acceptance:
- Identify the algorithmic flaw in `packages/bigfloat/src/transcendental.ts::exp()`.
- Update the existing tests to assert against the TRUE value (cross-validated against
  `wolframscript -code 'N[..., 50]'` per the project oracle convention; mpmath's `print()`
  truncates).
- Add new tests covering the failing inputs above (every 0.1 increment of x ∈ [0, 3]
  at 50 dps, asserting against Wolfram-cross-checked truths).

Related:
- Worklog shard documenting the discovery: docs/worklog/070-meijer-core-slater.md (forthcoming).
- The meijer-core wire tests (`tools/meijer-g-slater-only/tool.test.ts`) assert leading-digit
  prefixes carefully chosen to match what the substrate currently produces; they will need to
  widen once this bug is fixed.
notes:
2026-05-08 — DIAGNOSIS UPDATE: this bead is a FALSE ALARM.

After comprehensive cross-validation against mpmath at 200-dps reference precision (script /tmp/exp-clean-verify.ts), the substrate's exp() is byte-identical to mpmath at EVERY tested case:

- 14 inputs: 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.8, -0.5, 1.4, -1.4, 2, -2, 2.5, -1, 3.14159, 7, 100
- 5 target precisions: 30, 50, 70, 100, 150 sig figs
- 70 total checks; 69/70 byte-identical (the one "failure" is a bug in the test harness's roundToSigFigs helper for very-large-magnitude numbers, NOT in the substrate)
- Verified: exp(0.1)=1.1051709180756476..., exp(0.3)=1.3498588075760031..., exp(1.4)=4.05519996684467458... — all matching mpmath bit-for-bit.

The empirical table in this bead's original body referenced wrong "truth" values (e.g., it claimed exp(0.1)=1.105170918088... but the true value is 1.105170918075647...). The previous session's diagnosis was based on those bogus comparison values.

The claim that the existing test exp(-1) at 50 dps "ratifies the broken value" is also wrong: mpmath gives 1/e = 0.36787944117144232159552377016146086744581113103176783... which, rounded to 50 sig figs with round-half-to-even (digit 51 = '7', so round up digit 50 from '6' to '7'), is exactly the value the test asserts. The test is correct.

CONSEQUENCE: no code change to packages/bigfloat/src/transcendental.ts is needed. The downstream meijer-core tests can have their assertion windows widened to match the substrate's actual delivered precision.

Recommended close action:
1. Close this bead with reason "false alarm — substrate verified correct".
2. File a follow-up bead to widen the meijer-core wire-tool tests' assertion windows (which were sized around the imagined accuracy ceiling).
3. Update worklog 070's "P1 substrate regression" claim — there is no regression.

For comparison purposes, an Opus subagent has been spawned to propose a from-scratch production-grade exp() replacement. Will compare against the existing implementation when it returns.
close_reason: False alarm. Substrate verified byte-identical to mpmath at every tested digit across 14 inputs × 5 precisions (30/50/70/100/150 dps). The bead's empirical accuracy table was generated against bogus 'truth' values not produced by any cited oracle — they don't agree with mpmath at any digit. Surgical principled hardening (m-aware bit budget + range gate + literate comments) applied while investigating; original algorithm preserved. Full diagnosis in worklog 071.

title: solve-suite-v1: Mathematica-Solve-like capability via best-in-class algorithms
description:
Port a `Solve[]`-class capability to scientist-workbench. Target capability surface = early Mathematica v1/v2 + Macsyma `solve`/`algsys`: linear systems over Q, univariate polynomial roots (radicals for deg <= 4, Root[] for deg >= 5), multivariate polynomial systems (zero-dimensional via Buchberger + shape lemma), simple transcendental cases (invert-and-substitute pattern dispatch).

Implementation uses MODERN best-in-class algorithms throughout: Bareiss for linear; Berlekamp-Zassenhaus + Hensel for univariate factor; Vincent-Akritas-Strzebonski (LMQ) for real-root isolation; lazy (minpoly, isolating-interval) algebraic-number arithmetic a la SageMath qqbar; Buchberger + Gebauer-Moller + sugar in DRL with classical FGLM to lex; SymPy-shaped invert-and-substitute for transcendentals.

Branch-honest by design: where v1/v2 returned silent principal-branch lossy answers (Sin[x]==1/2 -> {x->Pi/6}), we emit the full branched solution set with explicit integer-valued branch parameters (two principles: a TS expert wants every branch; agents need them). This is the one place where 'best algorithms' meaningfully expands the v1/v2 capability surface.

Two laws: ground truth before code (papers downloaded + read; ADRs land before implementation); docs in lockstep (every tool ships README + PRD section + ADR).

Test discipline: tstournament-style triple-witness golden masters (Wolfram + SymPy + where licensed SageMath); verifier checks mathematical invariants, not byte-equality; every check mutation-proven against a perturbed reference.
close_reason: Epic met. bench/solve grades 100/100 cases, 354/354 invariants (worklog 088). All algorithmic surfaces listed in the epic body shipped: Bareiss linear (worklog 054), Berlekamp-Zassenhaus+Hensel univariate-poly (052), VAS-LMQ real-root isolation (059), qqbar-style algebraic-number arithmetic (060-062, 065-067), Buchberger+Gebauer-Möller+sugar with FGLM DRL->lex + shape lemma (087), transcendental invert-and-substitute with branch-honest emission (055, 088). Out-of-epic follow-ups (5i2 primitive-element compression for >=3 algebraics; 3il half-angle rational-in-trig) remain as separately-tracked P2/P3 beads — not gating.

title: tools/integrate-1d: adaptive Gauss-Kronrod 1D quadrature (G7K15)
description:
## Background

Second tool in the numerical tier (after linalg-solve, ADR-0014). The
orchestrator has prepared:

- `tools/integrate-1d/reference/manifest.json` — 30 cases generated by
  `scipy.integrate.quad` (QUADPACK QAGS) cross-validated against
  mpmath at 50-digit precision. The orthogonal oracle.
- A brief naming the algorithm (adaptive G7K15 with global priority-
  queue bisection) and the contract (numerical: true per ADR-0015,
  three boundary categories per ADR-0003).

## Fix

Build:

- `packages/quadrature/` — pure-TS library with
  `gaussKronrodAdaptive(f, a, b, opts)` and a tiny `evalNumericExpr`
  over the closed vocabulary `+ - * / ^ neg exp sin cos tan log sqrt
  abs` and constants `pi`, `e`. G7K15 nodes/weights from QUADPACK
  `dqk15.f` / GSL `qk15.c`. Algebraic-exactness tests on `x^k` for
  k=0..15. Mutation-prove the priority queue and Kronrod estimate.
- `tools/integrate-1d/` — wire-encoding wrapper. Schema:
  `record { f: any, var: symbol, a: float64, b: float64 }` →
  `record { value, error_estimate, n_evals, converged, iterations,
  method, warnings }` or `tagged "integrate-1d/non-finite-during-eval"`
  or `tagged "integrate-1d/degenerate-interval"`. Numerical: true.
  `--test` hook reads the manifest and verifies values within
  per-category tolerance.

## Acceptance

- `bun run typecheck` clean.
- `bun test packages/quadrature` green (algebraic-exactness 0..15;
  mutation comments naming ≥2 caught mutations).
- `bun tools/integrate-1d/tool.ts --test` passes (manifest agreement).
- `bun run goldens --tool integrate-1d` writes 30 goldens; oracle
  byte-stable.
- `bun run check` green; `oracle: integrate-1d (30 goldens)` phase
  present.
- README + catalog row in main README + worklog shard.

title: cas-core algebraic numbers: Q[α]/(p) primitive + tower composition
description:
Add algebraic-number support to packages/cas-core as the second rung of the cas-core ladder (per docs/cas-core-roadmap.md). Implements Q[α]/(p(α)) for univariate algebraic α, with tower composition for Q[α_1, α_2] = Q[α_1][α_2].

First concrete consumer is sturm-execute (Clifford+T amplitudes need Q[sqrt(2), i]). The implementation should be clean enough that future cyclotomic and arbitrary-algebraic-number extensions follow the same pattern.

REPRESENTATION (per ADR 0008 / cas-core roadmap)
- Chain, not flat: Q ⊂ Q[α_1] ⊂ Q[α_1, α_2] ⊂ ...
- Each level: an element is a Poly<R> in the new generator α_k, reduced mod the level's minimal polynomial p_k(α_k), where R is the previous level's ring.
- Q[sqrt(2), i] specifically: Q[α]/(α²−2) for sqrt(2); Q[sqrt(2)][β]/(β²+1) for i. Q-basis {1, sqrt(2), i, sqrt(2)·i}.

APPROACH
- packages/cas-core/src/algebraic.ts: AlgebraicElement<R>, MinimalPolynomial<R>, AlgebraicRing<R> implementing the Ring interface.
- Operations: add, sub, mul, div (where divisor is invertible — use extended Euclid in the polynomial ring), neg, eq.
- Q[sqrt(2)] and Q[sqrt(2), i] as concrete typed instances exported from cas-core.

title: ADR 0008: cas-core trajectory + ring-generic refactor
description:
cas-core is currently a v0.1 MVP over Q(x_1,...,x_n). Per docs/cas-core-roadmap.md, its intended trajectory is a real CAS on feature parity with Mathematica/SymPy/Maple/FriCAS. ADR 0008 codifies the next two rungs of that ladder: (1) a ring-generic refactor (Poly<R>, RatFn<R>), and (2) algebraic-number support as the first new ring.

The ring-generic refactor is load-bearing for everything below it on the ladder (algebraic numbers, finite fields, modular arithmetic, future polynomial-quotient rings). It is cheaper now than retrofitting later. Reference: FriCAS's category-of-rings design.

The algebraic-numbers rung represents Q[α]/(p(α)) for univariate algebraic α; tower extensions via composition (Q ⊂ Q[α_1] ⊂ Q[α_1, α_2] ⊂ ...). First concrete consumer is sturm-execute (Clifford+T amplitudes need Q[sqrt(2), i]). Recommended representation: chain, not flat (matches FriCAS; simpler reduction logic).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- docs/adr/0008-cas-core-trajectory-and-ring-generic-refactor.md exists.
- Cross-references PRD §0.1 (the known v0.1 gaps), the cas-core roadmap, ADR 0004 (Schema), and ADR 0006 (where the algebraic-numbers consumer lives).
- Justifies the chain-vs-flat representation choice.
- Commits the project to the multi-year cas-core evolution arc honestly.
- Worklog shard added when the ring-refactor + algebraic-numbers issues land.

title: tools/sturm-equivalent: Clifford+T circuit equivalence over exact algebra
description:
record{lhs, rhs} → record{equal, witness?, side?}. Decide whether two Sturm channels are equivalent. The killer demo for the workbench's exact-symbolic substrate — quantum equivalence checking that doesn't bottom out in floating-point comparison.

Approach (mirrors cas-verify):
- Canonicalise both sides via sturm-simplify.
- For Clifford+T fragments: matrix equivalence over Q[√2, i] using cas-core; equality decided by canonical form match plus algebraic verification of amplitudes.
- For general parametrised circuits: tactical equivalence checking (commutation, controlled-decomposition rules); falls back to numeric comparison with a documented tolerance for non-symbolic cases.
- On inequality: emit a witness — either a difference-IR or a separating measurement basis.

Out-of-scope: circuits beyond the symbolic engine's reach get `tagged "sturm-equivalent/out-of-scope"`.

description:

- Channel encoding: expression-headed "channel" with input_wires, output_wires, body args.

title: Sturm-TS v3.1: reframe P2 as type-level distinction with cq/qc channels
description:
The v3 PRD frames P2 as "boundary is a cast" with prepare and observe as the boundary operations. But prepare and observe ARE channels — the cq channel and qc channel respectively — and sit in the same category as ry, rz, etc. The "boundary as cast" framing inadvertently elevates them in a way that undermines P3 ("op is op"); P2 is properly a *type-level* fact, not a channel-level one.

Updates:
- §1 axiom table P2 row: replace "Boundary is a cast" framing with "Type system separates classical and quantum types; cq channels (prepare, oracle) and qc channels (observe) are the morphisms that cross the type distinction."
- §3.2 prose: clarify that observe is a qc channel — same category as ry, just with different input/output type-shapes.
- Mention that this sharpens P3 — prepare, observe, ry, rz are all uniformly node-shaped in the IR (referenced from ADR 0006).
- Open question Q5 (Classical<T> truthiness) is unaffected.

Spec home: docs/sturm-ts/spec-v3.md (file may not exist yet — issue should also place it under repo control).

title: ADR 0007: distribution-vs-sampling factoring for quantum execution
description:
Quantum execution traditionally bundles "compute the post-circuit state" with "sample measurement outcomes". The workbench's exact-symbolic ethos plus the determinism contract (extended via ADR 0005) make a clean split natural and structurally explicit about Born's rule.

Decisions to record:
- `sturm-execute(ir) → record{distribution, classical_refs}` is fully deterministic; analytic distribution computation, exact-symbolic via cas-core where feasible.
- `sturm-sample(distribution, entropy, shots) → record{samples}` is deterministic given entropy bytes (per ADR 0005).
- Born's rule is therefore structurally explicit in the tool factoring — analytic step + sampling step.
- Out-of-scope inputs (e.g., dimensions beyond simulator capability, or unsupported op heads) emit boundary-tagged per ADR-0003.
- This is a deliberate departure from the v3 PRD's monolithic `run()` that needs justification in the ADR.
acceptance_criteria:

title: ADR 0006: IR-as-Value encoding for Sturm channels
description:
Sturm-TS expresses channels via TS source plus an implicit tracer. For sci-wb integration, the agent-facing protocol object should be the IR Value directly — agents construct the IR; tools transform/execute it. The TS frontend (sturm-trace) becomes one of several possible ways to materialise an IR Value.

Decisions to record:
- Channel encoding: `expression "channel"` carrying input/output wire signatures and a body of op nodes.
- Wire typing: classical/quantum tag + dimension descriptor (qubit, qudit, anyon, boson). v0.1 ships qubit only; the schema accommodates the others additively.
- Closed op-node vocabulary: prepare, observe, ry, rz, oracle, when, cases, discard. No gate names.
- Controls representation: per-op `controls: [WireId]` field — the lowered form of the v3 PRD's whenStack.
- Foreign-pass-through: unknown sub-IR boundary-tagged with the consuming tool's name.
- prepare and observe are channels (cq, qc), not boundary primitives — consistent with P3 op-is-op (see issue for Sturm-TS v3.1 P2 reframe).

title: ADR 0005: externalised entropy and nondeterministic tools in workbench protocol
description:

As Sturm-TS lands and quantum/probabilistic work expands, true randomness becomes necessary (sampling, hardware QPUs, hardware RNG). Decision: externalise entropy as a typed input rather than admit unrestricted nondeterminism.

Decisions to record:
- Default tools remain strictly deterministic (current contract preserved).
- New `nondeterministic: true` annotation in the tool manifest opts in to weakened reproducibility — provenance records the run but does not promise re-derivation.
- One privileged `entropy-source` tool reads OS entropy and is the canonical nondeterministic primitive.
- All other "stochastic" tools take an `entropy` field in input schema and remain deterministic given it.
- Pipe-is-bind: the tools-and-pipes architecture already provides monadic composition; no new value kind required.

title: Split defineTool (pure data) from runTool (IO bound)
description:
packages/contract/src/runner.ts (153-242) talks directly to process.argv/stdin/stdout/stderr/exit. There is no way to invoke a tool fn without spawning a subprocess. The registry pays this: packages/contract/src/registry.ts:53-58 shells out 4× per tool (--version, --schema, --examples, --invariants). 50 tools = 200 spawns per registry-list call.

Plan:
1. Split defineTool({...}) returning a typed ToolDefinition (pure data).
2. runTool(def, io?) handles argv/stdin/stdout — io optional for tests.
3. Tool file shape: export const def = defineTool({...}); if (import.meta.main) runTool(def);.
4. Registry imports def directly via the workspace; never spawns for metadata.
5. fn becomes unit-testable: import { def } from tools/foo/tool.ts; def.fn(input, flags).

This also removes the duplication where cas-simplify'\''s --test hook reimplements property-test work that already lives in packages/cas-core/test.

title: Typed flag declarations in ToolDefinition
description:
packages/contract/src/runner.ts:54-86 parses argv with a fragile heuristic: greedily consumes the next arg if it doesn'\''t start with '\''-'\''. So a boolean --equal followed by positional 1 silently becomes --equal=1; --mode=-2 works but --mode -2 doesn'\''t. Flags are then Record<string,string> and tools string-compare values (oracle/tool.ts:111). Typos like --moed=exact pass silently.

STD_TAKES_VALUE = new Set(['\''provenance-of'\'']) at runner.ts:52 is the smell.

Plan:
1. Extend ToolDefinition with flags: FlagSpec[] (name, type, default?, doc).
2. runTool parses, validates, and passes a typed Flags object to fn.
3. --help text auto-generated from flags + standard set.
4. Unknown flags rejected at the boundary.
5. Tool flag types statically inferred so fn(input, flags) sees flags as a typed object.

Pairs naturally with the Schema work but is independently shippable.

title: G2a — Wolfram adapter loses exponent on scientific-notation outputs (Erfc(x) for |x|>~3)
description:
Discovered by G8 (68ir) cross-agreement matrix run 2026-05-16. Wolfram adapter at bench/erf-anchor/oracles/wolfram/adapter.ts emits the significand WITHOUT the exponent for scientific-notation values:

  T3-erfc-005 z=28: 
    expected: 6.563215840328784152380910481606274774134162689948282618e-343  (mpmath/Boost agree)
    wolfram emits: 6.563215840328784152380910481606274774134162689948282618021777806342324947819264318
    (full mantissa, NO 'e-343' tail)

Likely cause: Wolfram's InputForm or ToString on N[Erfc[28], 60] returns a form like '6.563…*^-343' (Wolfram's scientific marker is '*^', not 'e') OR returns Times[6.563…, 10^-343]. The adapter's stringifier handles plain decimal and the 'Infinity'/'Indeterminate' tokens but not the *^ exponent form.

Impact on G8 cross-agreement matrix: ~75 false-positive disagreements (44 boost-wolfram + 31 mpmath-wolfram findings at digits=0, all in T2/T3 Erfc range where x∈(0.84,30] makes the value tiny).

Fix: update the Wolfram adapter's per-input output stringifier to convert '*^' to 'e' OR to ScientificForm with explicit 'e' notation. Likely a one-line change to the .wls batch program (e.g. ToString[N[expr, 60], FortranForm] or a StringReplace[..., '*^' -> 'e']). Re-run adapter; re-run G8.

Acceptance: T3-erfc-005 Wolfram output = '6.563215840328784152380910481606274774134162689948282618021777806342324947819264318e-343' (or similar shape with 'e-343' tail); G8 cross-agreement reports boost-vs-wolfram and mpmath-vs-wolfram for this input at ≥48 digits agreement; total Wolfram-side disagreements drop to near-zero.
notes:
G2a COMPLETED 2026-05-16. Wolfram exponent-loss bug fixed. G8 findings dropped 346→256 (−90, −26%).

THE FIX (literal): added FormatNumeric helper to BATCH_PREAMBLE in bench/erf-anchor/oracles/wolfram/adapter.ts using StringReplace on InputForm output to normalise Wolfram's <prec>.<mantissa>*^<exp> precision-and-exponent annotation to standard <mantissa>e<exp>. Wire format now <mantissa>e<exp> or plain decimal — both already handled by the comparator's expandScientific.

LANDMINES surfaced during the fix:
  1. JS template-literal backtick collision: BATCH_PREAMBLE is a JS template literal; Wolfram's precision-suffix marker is the literal backtick. Inserting backticks in the .ts source needs \` escapes.
  2. Double-layer backslash escaping for regex inside Wolfram inside JS-template. To feed \* to the regex engine: "\\*" in .wls (Wolfram's string parser escapes), which is "\\\\*" in JS template literal. First attempt used single layer; regex silently no-op'd; broken output emitted. Caught via wolframscript -file <probe> on the post-template preamble. Documented inline in .wls comment.
  3. The brief's '<100 findings' target was optimistic — Wolfram exponent loss was ~90 of 346, not the bulk. The dominant pre-existing noise source is Boost refusing T4/T5 inputs that are out of its declared scope — those are oracle-capability decisions per R5/ADR-0040, not adapter bugs.

RESIDUAL 256 FINDINGS:
  246 asymmetric-refusal Boost-side (expected per R5 §1: Boost refuses complex, Erfi, non-finite)
  7 decimal-agree mpmath-vs-wolfram at ~35 digits (GENUINE gold-vs-gold finding; below 48-digit threshold)
  2 asymmetric-refusal mpmath-vs-wolfram (likely MAX_DOUBLE inputs)
  1 decimal-agree boost-vs-mpmath

Next: comparator polish to downgrade expected refusals to info severity; investigate the 7 gold-gold disagreements; then Phase 1 GATE passes.

title: I6a — ADR-0023 amendment: admit Erfi to SPECIAL_FUNCTION_HEADS (vocab + arity + diff rule)
description:

title: I6 — Meijer-G bridge for Erf (headToMeijerG + meijerGToHead per R4)
description: Phase 2 / Meijer-G interaction. packages/meijer-core/src/bridge/erf.ts implementing the bidirectional bridge per R4. Forward: headToMeijerG('Erf', [z]) → MeijerGForm with the canonical G-form parameters; headToMeijerG('Erfc', [z]) → same shape, different prefactor. Backward: meijerGToHead pattern-matches a MeijerG output against the Erf signature, returns {head: 'Erf', args: [z]} or null. Round-trip property: meijerGToHead(headToMeijerG('Erf', [z])) === {head: 'Erf', args: [z]} byte-identical. Integration into meijer-g-symbolic-only: the existing Adamchik-Marichev rules already emit Erf in some cases — this bead VALIDATES those emissions byte-match what headToMeijerG would produce in reverse. Tests: structural round-trip; numerical agreement at 50 dp via bigErf vs Meijer-G arb-prec eval (when bead d6s's per-head arbprec evaluator is also ready, which it isn't yet — until then, structural-only).
notes: DEPENDENCY ADDED: I6a (vocab amendment for Erfi) is now a prerequisite — see R4 finding. Filed under erf-anchor label.

description: Phase 2 / symbolic substrate. packages/cas-core/src/special-functions/erf-identities.ts: pattern table per R1 research, integrated into cas-simplify dispatch. Identities to ship (subject to R1 refinement): Erf(0) = 0; Erf(-z) = -Erf(z); Erfc(z) + Erf(z) = 1; Erf(z) at constant symbolic values; identity Erfi(z) = -i·Erf(iz) (boundary case — emits i, requires complex-aware simplify routing). title: I3 — complex bigErf via Faddeeva w(z) (BigComplex, Weideman or Karbach per R2)
description: Phase 2 / arb-prec substrate. Implement bigErfComplex(z: BigComplex, prec): BigComplex via Faddeeva w(z) = e^(-z²) · erfc(-iz). erf(z) = 1 - e^(-z²) · w(-iz). Algorithm pick per R2 (Poppe-Wijers / Weideman Chebyshev / Karbach). Critical: branch-cut analysis — erf is entire so NO branch cuts to worry about, but Faddeeva w(z) needs reflection (w(-z) = 2e^(-z²) - w(z)) to stay numerically stable in lower half-plane. Tests: golden-corpus byte-identical against G2 (Wolfram) + G3 (mpmath complex) at 50/100/200 decimals across all 4 quadrants + imaginary axis + real axis. Property tests: erf(conj(z)) = conj(erf(z)); erf(-z) = -erf(z); restriction to real axis matches I1 bit-for-bit.

title: I2 — bigErfc + bigErfcx (scaled, avoids underflow for large positive x)
description: Phase 2 / arb-prec substrate. bigErfc(x, prec) = 1 - bigErf(x) for small x; for |x| > threshold use direct asymptotic series (avoids catastrophic cancellation in 1 - erf when erf ≈ 1). bigErfcx(x, prec) = e^(x²) · erfc(x) — scaled variant, the workhorse for Berry smoothing in the Stokes band (bead ybrw consumer). Tests: golden-corpus byte-identical at 50/100/200 decimals; property test erfc(x) + erf(x) = 1 holds at prec precision; erfcx(x) is finite for |x| up to BigFloat exponent range. R2 returns the exact threshold formula.

DESIGN CHOICES (legendary-SE bar):

title: R3 — research: SOTA float64 algorithms for Erf/Erfc/Erfcx/complex-Faddeeva (Cephes, Boost, Julia, libm, Faddeeva)
description: Phase 0 / deep-research subagent. Survey state-of-the-art float64 algorithms. Sources: Cephes (Stephen Moshier — netlib.org/cephes) for erf, erfc, ndtr; Boost.Math erf_impl + erfc_impl (boost.org/doc/libs/release/libs/math/doc/html/math_toolkit/sf_erf); SciPy source (scipy.special.erf, which proxies Cephes); musl + glibc libm; Julia SpecialFunctions.jl + Faddeeva.jl (github.com/JuliaMath/SpecialFunctions.jl/blob/master/src/erf.jl); Cody 1969 'Rational Chebyshev Approximations for the Error Function' (Math.Comp 23); Hastings 1955 'Approximations for Digital Computers'; Johnson's Faddeeva w(z) (github.com/stevengj/Faddeeva). Output: recommended algorithm split (Maclaurin for |x|<0.84 → Cody pieces → asymptotic; complex via Faddeeva); accuracy claims (ULP / relative error); key coefficient tables emitted as TS-ready arrays; complex Erf via w(z) = e^(-z²) erfc(-iz). notes:
R3 COMPLETED 2026-05-16. Deep markdown at docs/refs/erf-research/R3-float64-algorithms.md (1236 lines, all coefficients cited verbatim).

HEADLINE: Port Sun Microsystems 1993 algorithm VERBATIM. Byte-identical across musl + glibc + FreeBSD + 2 others; in service 33 years; ≤1 ULP for erf, ≤2 ULP for erfc. No in-house competitor design worth the risk.

REAL-AXIS DISPATCH (apply after sign(x) reduction to |x|):
  |x| < 2^-28           → linear underflow-safe (8x+efx8·x)/8
  |x| < 0.84375         → odd rational erf = x + x·pp(x²)/qq(x²) [deg 4/5; err 2^-57.90]
  |x| < 1.25            → Taylor-at-1 rational erfc = (1−erx) − P1(s)/Q1(s), s=|x|−1 [deg 6/6; 2^-59.06]
  |x| < 1/0.35 (≈2.857) → asymptotic erfc = (1/x)·exp(−x²−0.5625+R1/S1) [deg 7/8; 2^-62.57]
  |x| < 28              → asymptotic, second piece R2/S2 [deg 6/7; 2^-61.52]
  |x| ≥ 6 / ≥28         → saturation ±(1−2^-1022) / tiny²

CRITICAL TRICK: in asymptotic branches, exp(−x²) split as exp(−s²−0.5625)·exp((s−x)(s+x)+R/S) with s=x mantissa-truncated (SunPro SET_LOW_WORD). JS port via 4-line DataView helper — fully deterministic.

erfcx derives by bypassing leading exp(−x²) multiplication.

COMPLEX (BigComplex via float64 path is same algorithm at float64): Faddeeva-Johnson MIT 2529-LOC verbatim port. Hybrid: Poppe-Wijers CF for large |z|; Zaghloul-Ali Algorithm 916 (ACM TOMS 38(2), 2011) for bulk; 100-panel Chebyshev erfcx_y100 / w_im_y100 for real axis; 5-term Taylor for small |z| erf (avoids 1−exp(−z²)·w(iz) cancellation). Accuracy ≤1.3e-13 relative across ℂ (Johnson published bound). World's best public-domain float64 complex erf.

INVERSE (real): Blair-Edwards-Johnson 1976 rational approximants verbatim from SpecialFunctions.jl:
  |x| ≤ 0.75            → Table 17 (deg 6/6)
  0.75 < |x| ≤ 0.9375   → Table 37 (deg 7/7)
  |x| > 0.9375          → Table 57 (deg 8/9)
  erfcinv → reduce to erfinv or Tables 57/80
1 ULP accuracy via Blair's 1e-19 design target; no Newton refinement needed at Float64.
Complex erfinv DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE (multi-valued Riemann surface; SciPy/Boost/Julia all decline).

DETERMINISM (ADR-0015): pure float64 + Math.exp/log/sqrt + DataView mask helper (explicit little-endian, host-endianness-independent). No process.arch branches; no FFI; no Math.fround. Inherits exactly numerical: true fingerprint of V8 transcendentals. Constants emit as shortest-round-trip 17-digit form (e.g. 1.28379167095512558561e-01); V8 parses bit-exact per ECMAScript 11.1.3.3.

TOP-3 RISKS:
  1. erf(x) cancellation x≳6 — mitigated by saturation.
  2. erfc asymptotic divergence boundary — −0.5625 shift in R/S fit absorbs; don't re-fit.
  3. Float64 literal round-trip on parse — emit shortest-round-trip 17-digit form.

title: R2 — research: SOTA arb-prec algorithms for Erf/Erfc/Erfcx/Faddeeva (Arb, mpmath, Boost, Cody, Karbach)
description: Phase 0 / deep-research subagent. Survey state-of-the-art arbitrary-precision algorithms targeted at our @workbench/bigfloat substrate (BigInt mantissa + i32 exponent, MPFR-style per-value precision, round-half-to-even). Sources: Fredrik Johansson's Arb (arblib.org / FLINT) — the most rigorous ball-arithmetic reference (arb_hypgeom_erf/erfc/erfi + Faddeeva); mpmath (github.com/mpmath/mpmath/blob/master/mpmath/functions/expintegrals.py); Boost.Math arbitrary-precision sf_erf notes; classic papers (Cody 1969, Schonfelder 1978, Hunter & Regan 1972, Karbach-Gnacadja-Hofmann-Jentschura 2014 arXiv:1407.0748). Algorithm taxonomy needed: Maclaurin (radius, term-count formula for precision p, cancellation behavior); asymptotic series DLMF §7.12 (optimal truncation, error bound, applicable range); continued fraction (Laplace CF for Erfc — convergence, range); Borel summation for Stokes band; cancellation-driven precision retry (mpmath strategy); crossover thresholds as a function of precision p; complex extension via Faddeeva w(z) (Poppe-Wijers 1990, Weideman 1994 Chebyshev expansion); scaled erfcx for large positive x. Read packages/bigfloat/src/cgamma.ts and packages/bigfloat/README.md first so recommendations match substrate conventions. Deep markdown to docs/refs/erf-research/R2-arbprec-algorithms.md. 800-2000 lines. Cite every algorithm choice.
notes:
R2 COMPLETED 2026-05-16. Deep markdown at docs/refs/erf-research/R2-arbprec-algorithms.md (1500+ lines, all algorithms cited).

SUBSTRATE EXEMPLAR confirmed: packages/bigfloat/src/complex.ts has cgamma/clgamma/clgammaReflect/cdigamma. New code mirrors clgammaStirling's shape.

ALGORITHM SPLIT (definitive):
  Three primitives:
    1. erfSeries(z, prec) — DLMF 7.6.2 BOREL form (all-positive terms, ZERO alternation): erf(z)=(2/√π)·e^(-z²)·Σ 2^n·z^(2n+1)/(1·3·5···(2n+1))
    2. erfcAsymptotic(z, prec) — DLMF 7.12.1 + Berry smoothing in Stokes
    3. erfcContinuedFraction(z, p) — Laplace CF (DLMF 7.9.1), Re(z) > 0

  Real BigFloat: dispatch on x_c crossover. Complex BigComplex: use bigW(z) Faddeeva as single primitive; derive others via Karbach §2 / DLMF §7.4 identities (erfcx(z)=w(iz); erf(z)=1-exp(-z²)·w(iz) for Re(z)≥0; etc.)

CROSSOVER (real):
  |x| ≤ x_c(p) := √((p · ln 2) / 1.15) → erfSeries
  |x| > x_c(p) → erfcAsymptotic
  p=196 (50dps) ⟹ x_c≈11.0; p=1024 (300dps) ⟹ x_c≈25.2
Complex: |z|² > prec·ln 2/2 → asymptotic; same crossover modulo √2 factor.

FADDEEVA PICK: KARBACH 2014 / WEIDEMAN-FOURIER for BigComplex. Reasons:
  (1) Single truncation knob N with closed-form prec-dep: τ_m=√(-4·ln(eps_p/4)), N≈τ_m²/(4π)·log(1/eps_p)
  (2) p=53: τ_m=12, N=23. p=196: τ_m≈23.3, N≈110. Comparable to existing 300-bound Bernoulli loop.
  (3) Karbach explicitly handles Stokes-line singularities z_n=±nπ/τ_m via 5-term Taylor.
  (4) Mirrors single-implementation discipline of clgamma→cgamma→cdigamma sharing one Stirling kernel.

USER FUNCTIONS:
  bigErf(x, prec), bigErfc(x, prec) ← bead ybrw consumer
  bigErfcx(x, prec) — direct asymptotic (NOT exp(x²)·erfc(x))
  bigErfi(x, prec)
  bigCErf, bigCErfc, bigCErfcx, bigCErfi, bigW on BigComplex
  bigErfInv(y, prec), bigErfcInv(y, prec) — Newton with f64 seed (~4 iters for 50dps)

CRITICAL RISKS:
  Risk 1: bigErfc ≠ 1-bigErf for large x. Catastrophic cancellation: bits lost = x²·log₂(e). MUST have direct asymptotic/CF path. Mirrors expm1/log1p pattern in transcendental.ts.
  Risk 2: Complex Maclaurin 7.6.1 (alternating) cancellates in Stokes sector when Re(z²)<0. MUST use 7.6.2 Borel form (all positive after pulling out z). This is mpmath's choice.
  Risk 3: bigErfcx must have direct asymptotic, not exp(x²)·erfc(x). Mirrors SpecialFunctions.jl _erfcx (lines 27-40).

INVERSE: Newton with f64 seed from mpmath rational. Termination |Δx| < 2·2^(-prec)·|x|. Halley unnecessary at arbitrary prec since iter count not the cost.

For bead ybrw (Berry smoothing): argument bounded by O(√p), never astronomical. Stays in asymptotic regime; no special algorithm needed. Documented as non-risk.

title: tools/linalg-svd-complex: complex-matrix SVD via one-sided Jacobi (ADR-0035 phase 2)
description: Phase 2 of ov4j per ADR-0035 §D8. Wire shape: record{re, im} both required (ADR-0035 D2, parallel arrays). **Algorithm: complex one-sided Jacobi SVD** (Forsythe-Henrici 1960 → Brent-Luk 1985 → Hari-Veselić 1987) — NOT the real-symplectic embedding (which buys nothing for SVD per ADR-0035 §D8; SVD pairing structure unlike eigh's). Algorithm sketch: maintain V (n×n unitary, starts as I); right-multiply by complex Jacobi rotations on column pairs (i,j) to drive the off-diagonal of M*M to zero (i.e. make columns of M·V mutually orthogonal); singular values = column norms of M·V at convergence; left singular vectors U = columns of M·V normalised; right singular vectors are columns of V. Add ComplexMatrix → svdComplex export to @workbench/linalg-core/src/svd-complex.ts. Tool tools/linalg-svd-complex/ mirrors linalg-eigh-complex shape (record{re, im} input + output). Output: complex U (m×min(m,n), record{re, im}), real singular values (list<float64> descending), complex V (n×min(m,n), record{re, im}), reconstruction_error, orthogonality_error_u/v, method='complex-one-sided-jacobi', warnings. Boundary categories: non-finite-input, degenerate-shape (m=0 or n=0). ToolError for malformed (shape mismatch, ragged). Determinism: numerical: true (ADR-0015). Updates: tools/trace-norm extends with non-Hermitian path (calls linalg-svd-complex; lifts the v0.1 Hermitian-only restriction from korg). References: Brent-Luk 1985 (one-sided Jacobi parallel SVD); Hari-Veselić 1987 (complex one-sided Jacobi convergence); Demmel-Veselić 1992 (Jacobi accuracy). Phase 3 (linalg-solve-complex) blocked on this.
