title: bigfloat: lgammaRealAbs / digamma real-argument reflection — same near-pole cancellation as oj5j
description:
Sibling of scientist-workbench-oj5j. The complex reflection paths clgammaReflect / cdigammaReflect were fixed (oj5j, worklog 117) by reducing z -> zeta = z - m before multiplying by pi, plus an adaptive working-precision bump by the measured cancellation depth. The REAL-argument reflection path in packages/bigfloat/src/special.ts carries the byte-identical latent bug: lgammaRealAbs computes piZ = mul(piW, z, work) then sin(piZ, work) at work = prec + 32, so for a real z epsilon-close to a non-positive integer pole it loses ~(-log10(eps) - 9) digits exactly as the complex path did. gamma() (real) inherits it via lgammaRealAbs. The real digamma() reflection is currently stubbed ('negative argument support deferred to v0.2') so digamma is only latently affected once that stub is filled.

Fix: port the oj5j reformulation to lgammaRealAbs (and to the digamma real path when it is implemented): m = round(z); zeta = z - m; sin(pi z) = (-1)^m sin(pi zeta); lossBits = max(0, magBits(z) - magBits(zeta)); work = prec + 32 + lossBits. For m = 0 the computation is byte-identical to the current code (zeta = z, lossBits = 0).

Acceptance: a near-pole real case (e.g. gamma(-1 - 1e-40) with z carried at high precision) delivers the full requested precision; existing special.ts tests still pass; check the meijer-core real-path goldens for intended drift.

Why separate from oj5j: different file (special.ts), different golden-churn surface (real gamma path), and oj5j's stated acceptance is the complex meijer-core estimator. Honest decomposition, not scope creep — flagged during the oj5j fix.
close_reason: Fixed: ported the oj5j reformulation to lgammaRealAbs (real-argument reflection); BUT additionally found gamma's sign detection had a different-shape failure mode of the same bug (sgn(sin(πz, work)) returns 0 near poles, gamma throws spurious 'pole' RangeError for inputs only near a pole). Replaced with the algebraic identity sgn(Γ(z)) = (-1)^m · sgn(ζ) — exact, sin-free, no precision loss, fewer lines. bigfloat 267 tests (was 257; +10 zhrm regression block). Mutation-proven: revert lgammaRealAbs reduction → 6/10 RED; revert gamma sign → spurious-throw test RED. Honest scope: digamma's negative-z reflection stub still has identical latent code but is gated behind an unconditional throw (v0.2-deferred); out of scope. Full bun run check green. Worklog 119.

title: cone-core/cone-solve: SCS termination test is looser than the §C-wire-form precision contract
description: Background: surfaced while fixing bead rgl8 (cone-solve achieved_precision over-claim) during the worklog-114 reconciliation. Once achieved_precision was corrected to the honest §C-wire-form max(r_p,r_d,r_c), a deeper incoherence appeared: cone-core's scsSolve decides 'optimal' from O'Donoghue 2016's §3.5 termination test — measured on the *embedded translated* problem in 2-norm, and gap-based (cᵀx+bᵀy, no xᵀs complementary-slackness term). That criterion is paper-faithful but LOOSER than the §C-wire-form residual the tool's precision contract is denominated in: the embedded test fires (residual ≤ precision in embedded form) while the recovered §C point's residual still exceeds precision. Measured embedded→§C amplification across the lp-netlib profile: ratio ranges 0.59 (afiro) to 3.08 (scsd1) — not a fixed factor. As a STOPGAP, rgl8 made tools/cone-solve re-label optimal→iter-cap when the recovered §C residual exceeds the request, so 'optimal' ⟹ achieved_precision ≤ precision holds (coherence guard). But that means cases that COULD reach the requested precision (with more iterations / a tighter internal tolerance) are honestly-but-pessimistically reported as iter-cap rather than driven to optimal. Proper fix options (a real design call, hence its own bead): (1) make cone-core's recoverPrimalDual §3.5 test optionally measure a caller-supplied consumer-form residual; (2) cone-core gains an xᵀs complementary-slackness term + ∞-norm-consistent denominators so its 'optimal' matches the wire contract; (3) cone-solve passes cone-core a principled tighter internal precision derived from a per-problem amplification estimate (not a fixed guess). Whichever: it touches cone-core's paper-faithful termination, has ADR-0036 interactions, and needs care + mutation-proofing of the 72-test substrate suite — do NOT rush it into rgl8. Acceptance: cone-solve's optimal-rate on bench/cone-solve/profile-lp-netlib.ts climbs (cases re-labelled iter-cap purely by the embedded/§C gap become genuine optimal); cone-core termination change mutation-proven; ADR addendum or new ADR if cone-core's termination semantics change.
notes: Relates: rgl8 (the over-claim fix that surfaced this; rgl8's coherence guard re-labels optimal→iter-cap as the stopgap), 2ivi (cone-solve — NOT blocked by this; cone-solve ships honest, this makes it better), ADR-0037 (the universal-tier discipline), ADR-0036. Measure via bench/cone-solve/profile-lp-netlib.ts optimal-rate.
close_reason: Fixed: cone-core's recoverPrimalDual + SCSOpts gain an optional convergenceTest?: (c: Candidate) => boolean hook (default absent = paper-faithful §3.5; supplied = sole arbiter of optimal). tools/cone-solve hands scsSolve a closure that recovers the §C point and returns kktResidualC ≤ precision, so the iteration is driven to the wire criterion directly — rgl8's coherence-guard re-label retired. Two rejected options (cone-core adopting ∞-norm/xᵀs is structurally impossible; per-problem amplification estimate is a Rule-2 bandaid) recorded in the ADR-0030 addendum. cone-core 99 tests (was 90), mutation-proven. Profiler optimal-rate 3/5 → 5/5 (blend + scsd1 now genuine optimal). Worklog 116. bun run check green 95/0.

title: cone-core v0.2: Type-I Anderson + Powell globalisation for the nonsmooth SCS tail
description: Background: cone-core v0.1 (bead k9mm, ADR-0036) shipped Type-II Anderson acceleration (AA-II). worklog 113 + the bench/cone-solve/profile-lp-netlib.ts universal-tier profile (ADR-0037) established the limit: AA-II collapses *smooth* fixed-point tails but the SCS map is *nonsmooth* (the cone projection has kinks), so on NETLIB-LP at the 1e-6 cone-solve contract the optimal-rate is ~5/21 within a 50000-iter budget — the rest honestly iter-cap. ADR-0036 §A and ADR-0037 §E both name the remedy: Type-I Anderson acceleration with Powell-type regularisation + Gram-Schmidt restart globalisation — the method Zhang-O'Donoghue-Boyd 2018 built specifically for the nonsmooth case (the whole point of that paper). This is the v0.2 algorithm lever that climbs the profile's optimal-rate; it is NOT a cone-solve v0.1 blocker (cone-solve ships on its seven-artefact contract per ADR-0037 §B). Fix: (1) stage docs/refs/zhang-odonoghue-boyd-2018-type-i-anderson.pdf (arXiv:1808.03971) and transcribe the Type-I update + Powell regularisation (eq 10-13) + GS restart rule (eq 14) to docs/ground-truth/convex/ — Law 1 + ADR-0030 §E, reference before code; (2) implement Type-I in packages/cone-core/src/anderson.ts (alongside, not replacing, AA-II — keep both selectable; AA-II stays the determinism cross-check baseline); (3) wire an SCSOpts selector; (4) mutation-prove the Powell regularisation + restart on the load-bearing invariants. Acceptance: Type-I implemented + mutation-proven; the profiler optimal-rate measurably climbs vs the AA-II baseline recorded in ADR-0037; ADR-0036's 'documented v0.2 move' realised; determinism contract (numerical: true) preserved.
notes: Relates: k9mm (AA-II, the v0.1 baseline this extends), 2ivi (cone-solve — NOT blocked by this per ADR-0037 §E), ADR-0036 §A (names this the v0.2 move), ADR-0037 §E (files it). Measure via bench/cone-solve/profile-lp-netlib.ts.

title: cone-core: SOC + PSD cone projections
description: Background: cone-core v0.1 (bead cp9k) shipped the LP-complete slice — NonNeg/Zero/Free cone projections + HSDE + SCS iteration — which closes the v0.1 LP bench gate. The second-order (SOC) and positive-semidefinite (PSD) cone projections were deferred because O'Donoghue 2016 (docs/refs/odonoghue-2016-scs.pdf) gives only the cone *definitions*, not the projection *formulas*; it defers those to Parikh-Boyd, Proximal Algorithms, FnT Optimization 1(3) 2014, §6.3 (ref [64]). Per CLAUDE.md Law 1 + ADR-0030 §E, that reference must be staged in docs/refs/ before the code is written. Fix: (1) stage parikh-boyd-2014-proximal-algorithms.pdf in docs/refs/ and add a docs/ground-truth/convex/ transcription of the SOC + PSD projection formulas; (2) implement the soc/psd cases of projectCone/inCone in packages/cone-core/src/cones.ts (currently throw ConeError naming this bead). SOC: the standard 3-case closed form for {(t,x): t>=||x||}. PSD: eigendecompose the svec'd symmetric matrix (linalg-core eigh), clamp negative eigenvalues to 0, re-vectorise — mind the strict-Mosek sqrt2 off-diagonal scaling (ADR-0030 open-q 4, the trap that bites every amateur SDP implementer). title: solver-ipm corpus tests throw instead of skip on missing corpus (convention divergence)
description:
Background: Commit ef3a56c de-hardcoded /home/tobias/... paths in three solver-ipm tests (afiro.test.ts, hsde-lp-afiro.test.ts, hsde-lp-brandy.test.ts) to use loadSuite() from corpus.ts. Good change in intent — but the missing-corpus handling diverges from the project convention. corpus.ts's own doc-comment codifies the rule: a corpus-dependent test is 'skipped with a clear reason — not silently green'. The sibling tests netlib.test.ts and lp-small.test.ts honour this with describe.skip(...) on suite===null. The three converted tests instead 'throw new Error(...)' inside the test body, which goes RED, not skip. On a corpus-less machine 'bun run check' would now FAIL on three tests where the convention is to skip. worklog 106 claims they 'match netlib.test.ts and lp-small.test.ts' — they match the resolver (loadSuite) but contradict the missing-corpus handling. The divergence is masked locally because the corpus is present (the gate's '7 skipped' are the siblings; the 3 converted tests pass) — a Rule 3 'verified on my machine' trap.

Fix: convert the three tests to the describe.skip(suite===null) pattern used by netlib.test.ts / lp-small.test.ts. OR — if throwing-is-louder is a deliberate decision — change netlib/lp-small to throw too AND update corpus.ts's doc-comment so the convention is stated consistently. Pick one; consistency either way.

Acceptance: all five corpus-dependent solver-ipm tests handle suite===null identically; corpus.ts doc-comment matches the chosen behaviour; 'bun run check' on a corpus-less environment behaves as the doc-comment promises.
close_reason: Converted afiro/hsde-lp-afiro/hsde-lp-brandy corpus tests from throw-on-missing-corpus to the describe.skip(suite===null) convention used by netlib.test.ts/lp-small.test.ts and codified in corpus.ts. Verified: corpus present -> 3 pass; WORKBENCH_CORPUS=/nonexistent -> 3 skip 0 fail (was 3 fail).

title: mosek-log-to-jsonl.ts never validated against a real Mosek log (fuur acceptance criterion 4 unmet)
description:
Background: Commit ef3a56c (bead fuur, HSDE Phase 5 Tier 0) shipped scripts/mosek-log-to-jsonl.ts. The bead's own acceptance criterion 4 was: 'scripts/mosek-log-to-jsonl.ts converts probe_sdo1.log to JSONL successfully' — i.e. against a REAL Mosek log named probe_sdo1.log. Instead the agent validated against temp/mosek-sample.log, a gitignored file hand-written to match the script's own doc-comment. That is tautological (the parser parses a file written to its own assumptions) and proves nothing about real Mosek output. Contrast the COPT sibling, whose comment states 'Verified against probe1.log on COPT 8.0.4 build 20260424'. Law 1 (open the canonical reference) was not met. Worse, ADR-0033 Decision 8 now asserts as settled fact that the script 'parses Mosek's ITE PFEAS DFEAS GFEAS PRSTATUS POBJ DOBJ MU TIME table' — confidence the evidence does not support. fuur was closed claiming 'Mosek parser shipped' with this acceptance criterion unmet.

Fix: (1) Obtain a real Mosek IPM log (probe_sdo1.log per fuur, or any real Mosek interior-point run). (2) Verify the actual column layout/spacing against the parser's toks.length===9 assumption and the NUM_RE/TIME_RE token shapes; fix the parser to match real output. (3) Commit a small real-log fixture and add a reproducible assertion (not a smoke test — Rule 7). (4) If the format cannot be verified now, soften ADR-0033 Decision 8 wording from 'parses' to 'intended to parse (format unverified)' until it is. (5) The strict toks.length!==9 currently fails closed/loud, which is the one mitigation — preserve that.

Acceptance: parser verified against a committed real Mosek log fixture with an assertion in the suite or a --test-style check; ADR-0033 wording matches the actual validation state.

title: tools/choi-iso: seven-artefact wrapper around qinfo.choi / deChoi
description:
Thin tool over @workbench/qinfo's Choi-Jamiolkowski isomorphism. Two modes (via discriminator). Mode 1 — channel→Choi: input record{channel: list<list<float64>>, dim_in: integer, dim_out: integer} where channel is the matrix representation of the superoperator in column-stacking convention; output record{J: list<list<float64>>}. Mode 2 — Choi→channel: input record{J: list<list<float64>>, dim_in: integer, dim_out: integer}; output record{channel: list<list<float64>>}.

Convention: column-stacking (textbook default; QuTiP / SymPy default). J(Φ) = (Φ ⊗ id)(|Ω⟩⟨Ω|) where |Ω⟩ = Σ_i |i⟩|i⟩ (unnormalised maximally entangled). 

Invariants: (1) round-trip choi(deChoi(J)) = J; (2) J(identity channel) = |Ω⟩⟨Ω| (maximally entangled projector, unnormalised); (3) linearity in channel; (4) Tr_2(J(Φ)) = I iff Φ is trace-preserving (TP test); (5) J(Φ) ⪰ 0 iff Φ is completely-positive (CP test). 

>=10 examples covering: identity channel; depolarising channel at various p; transpose 'channel' (non-CP, J has negative eigvals); amplitude damping; tensor product of channels; refusal cases (dim mismatch, non-square).

Part of the qinfo epic (hsxa); blocked by eq4a.
close_reason: Closed

title: tools/partial-transpose: seven-artefact wrapper around qinfo.partialTranspose
description:
Thin tool over @workbench/qinfo's partialTranspose. Input: record{M: list<list<float64>>, dims: list<integer>, transposeOn: list<integer>}. Output: record{M_pt: list<list<float64>>, warnings: list<string>} | tagged 'partial-transpose/{shape-mismatch,subsystem-out-of-range,non-square,dims-mismatch}'.

Invariants: (1) involution PT(PT(M))=M; (2) PT(A⊗B)=A⊗B^T when transposing the second factor; (3) PT on the WHOLE system equals transpose; (4) PPT entanglement witness — Bell state |Φ+⟩⟨Φ+| has min eigenvalue -1/2 after PT on one subsystem (the canonical worked example).

>=10 examples covering: small 2-qubit cases (Bell state reduction, product states); qutrit ⊗ qubit dims; transposing multiple subsystems simultaneously; refusal cases. Symbolic tier for rational inputs / numerical tier for float64.

Part of the qinfo epic (hsxa); blocked by eq4a.

title: sdp-solve: infeasibility detection broken — infp1/infp2/infd1/infd2 return status=optimal with huge ap
description:
Background: Surfaced by SDPLIB stress test (bead jb1x, 2026-05-12). The four explicitly-infeasible SDPLIB cases (infp1, infp2 primal-infeasible; infd1, infd2 dual-infeasible) return status=optimal with achieved_precision in the 1e+1 to 1e+5 range. Wire output claims optimality when the solver-internal state is reporting numerical convergence on an embedded problem after dual regularisation has shifted the constraint set; the wire-frame primal/dual residuals are huge.

Examples (case: status / iter / ap on the default --method=nt):
  infp1: optimal / 2 / 1.52e+5
  infp2: optimal / 2 / 1.13e+5
  infd1: optimal / 2 / 2.16e+4
  infd2: optimal / 2 / 1.05e+4

HSDE-NT does slightly better numerically (ap in 1-90 range) but still claims optimal. The HSDE path SHOULD use the τ-κ ρ-dichotomy to detect infeasibility (τ → 0 with κ > 0 signals primal infeasibility; the opposite signals dual infeasibility per ART03); evidently the termination check at the wire isnt mapping the HSDE status correctly back to status=infeasible/unbounded.

This is an honest-scope violation per CLAUDE.md Rule 8: the tool is producing a wrong-shaped answer (optimal record with primal/dual/slack fields) when the correct answer is status=infeasible (no x; dual is Farkas certificate) or status=unbounded (x is an unbounded ray).

Root-cause hypotheses (verify before fixing):
1. The NT-path convergence check looks at the internal compl/primalInf/dualInf relative to a regularised metric; when the regulariser absorbs the infeasibility, the inner residuals shrink and the convergence flag fires.
2. The HSDE-path Status.ts mapping likely treats certain SolverStatus values (primal-infeasible / dual-infeasible) as wire-optimal incorrectly. Read packages/solver-ipm/src/solver/Status.ts toWireStatus mapping; verify the HSDE solvers correctly emit primal-infeasible / dual-infeasible SolverStatus when τ → 0 / κ > 0.

Acceptance: (1) infp1/infp2 return status=infeasible with a Farkas certificate in the dual field. (2) infd1/infd2 return status=unbounded with an unbounded ray in the x field. (3) hsde-nt does both via the τ-κ ρ-dichotomy. (4) Add 4 cases to packages/solver-ipm/test/ (or tools/sdp-solve/goldens/) pinning the correct wire output. (5) bun run check green.

Filed for visibility; tractable on its own but interacts with the Phase 5 IR work (the IR fixes precision; this fixes infeasibility classification).
notes: Fixed across HSDE-NT + NT paths. (1) NtSdpSolver.ts: bestStatus='dual-feasible' gated on couldDualFeas (the flag was previously computed but voided). finalizeBestOr now returns best snapshot with fallback status when stamp didn't fire, so infeasible inputs return numerical-error not optimal. (2) HsdeNtSdpSolver.ts: checkHsdeTermination split — OPTIMAL keeps purified ρ-gate, INFEASIBILITY uses unpurified witness-ratio tests (Mosek hom_terminatelo shape). WITNESS_FLOOR=1e-6 + TAU_KAPPA_FLOOR=1e-8 + prstatus<-0.5 regime guard. HSDE-NT path no longer stamps bestStatus='dual-feasible' at all. (3) Test fixtures: packages/solver-ipm/test/sdp-infeasibility.test.ts — 4 hand-constructed SDPs (2 primal-infeas + 2 dual-infeas), 8 tests, all pass. (4) Doc: ADR-0033 §6/§7 updated explaining the design fix and the previous ADR draft was wrong. worklog 097 added.
close_reason: HSDE-NT correctly classifies primal-infeasible / dual-infeasible at iter=2 on the probes with τ≈1e-12, κ≈1. NT path no longer lies — returns honest numerical-error on infeasible inputs. 14 existing sdp-solve goldens unchanged. Acceptance gates met (1-3,5); (4) covered via packages/solver-ipm/test/ rather than tools/sdp-solve/goldens/ — package test has assertions on the actual witness conditions (b^T y > 0, ⟨C,X⟩ < 0) that wire goldens can't easily express. Wire goldens for these cases deferred.

title: SDPLIB stress test: launch tools/sdp-solve on filtered SDPLIB (m ≤ 500), both --method=nt and --method=hsde-nt
description:

Currently the corpus has 10 .dat-s files locally; full SDPLIB has ~92. The middle ~50 (m ≤ 500) are tractable on the current dense-Cholesky substrate; the upper quartile (maxG*, theta6, equalG51 with m ≈ 5000-6000) need sparse linalg first.

2. Filter by m ≤ 500 (number of constraints — line 1 of .dat-s after comments). Probably ~50 problems.
3. Write scripts/sdplib-stress.ts: glob .dat-s files, filter, loop. Per problem: convert to wire, invoke `bun tools/sdp-solve/tool.ts --method=<m>` via spawnBun with IPM_TRACE_JSONL=<traces/case-method.jsonl> and a 5-min per-problem timeout. Run both --method=nt (legacy) and --method=hsde-nt (Phase 3 new).
4. Tabulate {case, method, status, iter, achieved_precision, wall_ms, primalObj, dualObj} to scripts/sdplib-stress-results.csv.

(4) Coverage report: how many cases reach optimal at default tol, how many iter-cap, how many numerical-error, broken down by method. (5) An A/B comparison of NT vs HSDE-NT on cases where they disagree on status.

Not in scope: the upper-quartile m ≥ 1000 cases (need sparse-linalg work in solver-ipm). Will be flagged but skipped via the filter.

Scale ceiling at m·n ≈ 30k (33 timeouts on m≥250,n≥250 cases). Full notes in scripts/sdplib-stress-NOTES.md.

title: solver-ipm SDP convergence hardening (analog of LP brandy gap)
description:
@workbench/solver-ipm's SDP IPM stalls on hinf2 because the iterate (X, y, S) must stay strictly inside K × K* — when the problem geometry pushes iterates against the cone boundary, the primal step length αP collapses to 0 and progress stops. Mosek (1) and COPT analysis (2) confirm: the fix is HSDE (Homogeneous Self-Dual Embedding), not Ruiz scaling. HSDE re-embeds the iterate in K × K* × R+ × R+ with new homogenization scalars (τ, κ); τ can shrink to absorb boundary approach, eliminating the αP → 0 stall by construction.

Mosek reaches pres ≈ 5.4e-13 on hinf2 in 84 iters; our NT stalls at pres ≈ 3.8e-7. The non-HSDE solver cannot reach Mosek-class precision on this problem geometry no matter how it's tuned — this is structural.

(1) docs/HANDOFF_solver_ipm_hsde.md + ~/Dropbox/.../MOSEK-decomp/analysis/VERDICT.md identifies Mosek's algorithm as ART03 (Andersen-Roos-Terlaky 2003) HSDE with NT scaling + Mehrotra correctors.
(2) ~/Dropbox/.../COPT-decomp/analysis/PD_IPM_DEEP.md confirms COPT does NOT use HSDE (default path is standard infeasible-start Mehrotra); COPT serves as Mehrotra/regularization reference, not HSDE reference.

Bench grade: 5/6 today (control2/control3 fixed by 095's COPT-aligned termination + best-iterate). HSDE port lifts to 6/6 on hinf2, with stretch to tighter TOL_KKT on the full SDPLIB set.

PLAN (5 phases, decomposed as qmrv-hsde-0..4):
- Phase 0: ADR + HsdeIterate/HsdeStepLength scaffold (~1d)
- Phase 1: HsdeLpSolver (LP first; no NT scaling; reveals API shape) (~3-5d)
- Phase 2: HsdeNtSdpSolver — the hinf2 fix (~3-5d)
- Phase 3: Tool wiring + default to hsde-nt (~1d)
- Phase 4 (stretch): Tighten corpus TOL_KKT (~1d)

REFERENCES (downloaded to docs/refs/): Andersen 2009 (homolo.pdf, primary impl ref), Andersen-Roos-Terlaky 2003 (canonical HSDE paper), ECOS/Domahidi 2013 (clearest written treatment), SCS, Clarabel, Ye warmstart. ECOS source at /tmp/ecos-reference/ (read-only structural reference, GPL).
close_reason: HSDE Phase 5 landed across Tiers 0-4 (worklogs 106 / 110 / 128 / 129 / 130). qmrv's αP-collapse root cause was correctly diagnosed; the fix it proposed (HSDE per ART03 + Andersen 2009) is what landed. **Outcome:** corpus invariant count lifted 63→64 of 66; control2 + control3 now reach strict / soft optimal via Tier 1 IR + Tier 3 soft-success branch; hinf2 invariant count 7→8 (of 10) with optimality_gap flipping to pass via IR's 3-decade r_p improvement. The remaining 2 hinf2 invariants (primal_feasibility, complementary_slackness) are the float64 representation limit of r_p/τ purification (worklog 128 §'hinf2 diagnostic'), lifted cleanly by Phase 6 bigfloat (separate ADR per ADR-0033 Decision 9). 6/6 case-count is honestly a Phase 6 gate, not a Phase 5 unfinished line-item.

title: lp-solve golden 05 (unbounded) mismatch — pre-existing on main since worklog-090 ship
description:
The oracle phase of bun run check fails on tools/lp-solve/goldens/05-unbounded-min-x-with-no-upper-bound-on-x.golden.json (canonical bytes: expected 642, got 567). Discovered 2026-05-11 while landing the solver-ipm substrate; confirmed pre-existing by checking out main directly.

Either the golden was generated against an older version, or the unbounded path's dual-emission was changed late and the golden not regenerated.

So OPTION 1 (regenerate golden) is the correct fix. The fact that the tool currently emits the empty list suggests that's the intended behaviour.

ACCEPTANCE: bun run check passes on main; bun run goldens:check passes for lp-solve.

  git checkout main
  bun run check
  # — oracle: lp-solve (12 goldens) ... FAIL
close_reason: Golden 05 regenerated to match current tool convention. The tool emits the unbounded ray in 'x' (primal space) with dual=[] for unbounded problems. The current convention is the TS-expert-correct one: result.dual carries Lagrange multipliers when they exist, not phantom data; unbounded rays live in primal space. bun run check now passes oracle: lp-solve.

title: tools/lp-solve: add Mehrotra IPM lane (lp-solve-ipm)
description:
Third lane for tools/lp-solve. Mehrotra predictor-corrector primal-dual
interior-point method on the homogeneous self-dual embedding (HSDE).
Public wire schema unchanged (ADR-0030 §C/§D); dispatch via
--method=ipm or auto when m,n >= 100 (per ADR-0030 §B's original
dispatch rule).

WHY: polynomial-time complexity; competitive with simplex on
medium-large LPs (n~500+); naturally produces a central-path solution
that simplex's vertex output complements. Different output structure
than simplex (no vertex basis) but same wire shape.

ALGORITHM: Mehrotra 1992 predictor-corrector with HSDE embedding for
unified infeasibility detection (Ye-Todd-Mizuno 1994). Iterative
refinement on the KKT solve for precision <= 1e-12.

REFERENCES (per ADR-0030 §E):
  Mehrotra 1992 SIAM J. Optimisation; Wright Primal-Dual

title: tools/qp-solve: best-in-class QP specialist (Mehrotra IPM with Q-block in KKT)
description:
Phase 3 specialist for the convex-cone epic (eg9j) per ADR-0030 §B. Best-in-class convex QP.

ALGORITHM: Mehrotra predictor-corrector primal-dual interior-point method, extending lp-solve's IPM path with the Q matrix as the (1,1) block of the KKT system:
  [ Q + S X^{-1}   A^T ] [ Δx ] = [ -r_d ]
  [ A              0   ] [ Δy ]   [ -r_p ]
where r_d, r_p are dual and primal residuals, S/X are slack/primal diagonals. The complementarity update mirrors LP.

References: Nocedal-Wright Numerical Optimization Ch.16; Vanderbei Ch.16-18; Mehrotra 1992 (extension to quadratic objective).

REQUIREMENTS on Q: positive-semidefinite (validated within tolerance; tagged 'qp-solve/non-psd-Q' refusal otherwise — convex QP only in v0.1, non-convex is a separate epic).

ACCURACY CEILING: 1e-10.

OUTPUT EXTRA FIELDS (vs cone-solve): active_set (which inequality constraints are tight at the optimum, with their multipliers).

BENCH GATE: 120+/138 Maros-Mészáros-QP cases against Gurobi/Mosek/COPT at 1e-8 precision.

BLOCKED BY: cone-core substrate + benchmarks/qp-maros-meszaros corpus bench.

title: benchmarks/sdp-sdplib (corpus): SDPLIB collection + Mosek/COPT triple-witness adapters
description:
Phase 0 corpus bench for the convex-cone epic (eg9j) per ADR-0030 §F. Lives in scientist-workbench-corpus/benchmarks/sdp-sdplib/.

SDPLIB (Borchers 1999): ~90 problems covering Lovász θ function on graph instances, MAXCUT relaxations, control LMI feasibility, eigenvalue minimisation, truss design. The canonical SDP test set.

Adapter caveat: Gurobi does NOT support SDP (LP/QP/SOCP/MIQP only). Triple-witness reduces to Mosek + COPT pair for SDP. SDPT3 (academic, MATLAB-only) could be a third adapter if the user wants it — its accuracy ceiling at 1e-10 makes it the natural SDP gold standard. Defer that decision to bench-bring-up time.

Per-problem invariants:
  1. primal_feasibility (constraint linear functionals + PSD-ness of primal matrix)
  2. dual_feasibility (PSD-ness of dual slack matrix)
  3. complementary_slackness (tr(X S) close to zero)
  4. optimality_gap
  5. oracle_agreement (Mosek + COPT; or all three if SDPT3 added)

BLOCKS tools/sdp-solve (Phase 4 white-whale, deferred per ADR-0030 §G).
DOES NOT BLOCK tools/cone-solve (cone-solve's SDP path is graded by oracle-agreement at 1e-6 ceiling, which Mosek/COPT meet with margin).

title: [epic] linalg-{eigh,svd,solve}: complex-Hermitian / complex-matrix extension
description:
Current linalg-* tools take list<list<float64>> only — real arithmetic. General quantum states have complex off-diagonal phases; the user-side workaround is the real-symplectic embedding H = A+iB -> block-real-symmetric of size 2n × 2n (eigenvalues duplicated, dimension doubled).

Surface friction from D_W1 dogfood 2026-05-10: ALL n=1 examples were restricted to the real Bloch X-Z plane to dodge this. Any quantum-info workflow that touches imaginary-phase coherence runs into it immediately.

DESIGN OPTIONS (one to pick before implementation):

(a) EXTEND existing tools with optional record{re, im} input schema.
    Pros: agents reach for the same tool, schema-discriminated branch on input.
    Cons: doubles the refusal surface; output is now also record{re, im}, breaks current callers.

(b) PARALLEL tools: linalg-eigh-complex, linalg-svd-complex, linalg-solve-complex.
    Pros: cleanest schema; existing tools untouched; mirrors meijer-g-symbolic-only / meijer-g-asymptotic-only naming.
    Cons: doubles the registry catalog row count; agents need to pick.

(c) BRIDGE: @workbench/complex-linalg substrate that does the real-symplectic embedding internally and calls the real linalg-* under the hood.
    Pros: zero new tools; the bridge lives in a package and downstream callers (qinfo, future quantum-info code) use it transparently.
    Cons: not visible to registry-search; agents discover it only via the qinfo / quantum-info path.

Recommend (b) on balance — explicit tool surface for explicit complex-Hermitian operations, mirrors existing meijer-g-* fan-out. Decision in an ADR before implementation. Phase order: linalg-eigh-complex first (most-needed for quantum-info), then linalg-svd-complex, then linalg-solve-complex.

Discovered: D_W1 dogfood 2026-05-10.
notes: 2026-05-13: ADR-0035 (docs/adr/0035-complex-linalg-tier.md) resolves the 'Decision in an ADR before implementation' open point. Commit option (b) parallel *-complex tools; wire shape record{re, im} with im required; ComplexMatrix type in linalg-core; v0.1 algorithm is real-symplectic embedding reusing the existing real cyclic-Jacobi eigh. Phase order: linalg-eigh-complex first (unblocks korg trace-norm), then linalg-svd-complex, then linalg-solve-complex. Worklog shard 100 documents the iteration. Next session: file the three downstream beads as children of this epic.

title: tools/trace-norm: trace norm ||M||_1 via linalg-eigh (Hermitian) or linalg-svd (general)
description:
Thin tool over @workbench/qinfo's traceNorm. Input: record{M: list<list<float64>>, hermitian?: boolean}. Output: record{value: float64, method: string, warnings: list<string>} | tagged 'trace-norm/{non-square,non-finite-input}'.

Implementation: if hermitian=true (default if M is symmetric within tolerance), use linalg-eigh + sum |eig|; otherwise use linalg-svd + sum of singular values. Numerical tier (numerical: true ADR-0015) — bit-identical given platform fingerprint.

Invariants: triangle inequality ||A+B||_1 <= ||A||_1 + ||B||_1; ||cA||_1 = |c|·||A||_1; ||A||_1 >= |tr(A)|; ||A||_1 = sum|eig(A)| for Hermitian.

>=10 examples: identity (||I_n||_1 = n); rank-1; rho-sigma for orthogonal pure states (||·||_1 = 2); non-symmetric (uses svd path).

Part of the qinfo epic (hsxa); blocked by qinfo-substrate.

Next: trace-distance / fidelity / purity, each one composition over this tool's substrate.

title: packages/qinfo: substrate package (partialTrace, kron, traceNorm, traceDistance, fidelity, purity, embedRealSymplectic)
description:
Phase 1 / Phase 2 substrate for the qinfo epic (hsxa). One TypeScript package with cohesive deep export table — the cas-core / groebner pattern. Updated 2026-05-12 with two-principles re-scoping decisions (see worklog 098).

DESIGN (UPDATED)

Storage: flat row-major Float64Array internally (matches solver-ipm/linalg-* convention; cache-friendly on dense partial-trace at >5 qubits). Single Matrix type with mandatory re field + optional im field; functions branch on `if (M.im)` exactly once. Helpers Matrix.fromNested / .toNested for tests + tool boundaries.

Dims: arbitrary-dim subsystem lists (`dims: number[]`) not 2^n-qubit-only. partialTrace(rho, [4,3,2], traceOut) is what a TS expert reaches for before specialising to qubits.

Complex: index-only operations (kron, partialTrace, partialTranspose, vec/unvec, choi/deChoi) support complex from day 1 via the optional im field — these operations don't depend on linalg-eigh. Real-Hermitian-only restriction applies only to the eigh-routed ops (traceNorm/traceDistance/fidelity), which is why their tool wrappers ship in v0.2 (after the linalg-complex epic ov4j lands).

Endianness: qubit 0 = leftmost tensor factor (matches dogfood and reading-order |q_0⟩ ⊗ |q_1⟩ ⊗ …).

EXPORTS

INDEX-ONLY (complex-OK from day 1, v0.1):
- kron(A, B): Matrix — Kronecker product.
- partialTrace(M, dims, traceOut): Matrix — trace out one subsystem; sequential under the hood for traceOut: number[].
- partialTracePure(psi, dims, traceOut): Matrix — pure-state special case via SVD/Schmidt (O(d·rank) vs O(d²)). Useful for state vectors not full density matrices. Performance work; can land later.
- partialTranspose(M, dims, transposeOn): Matrix — index permutation.
- vec(M): Vector / unvec(v, rows, cols): Matrix — column-stacking.
- choi(channelMatrix, dim_in, dim_out): Matrix / deChoi(J, dim_in, dim_out): Matrix — Choi-Jamiolkowski iso, column-stacking convention.

EIGH-ROUTED (real-Hermitian for v0.1; complex deferred to ov4j; tool wrappers ship in v0.2):
- traceNorm(M, wb): Promise<number> — sum |eig|.
- traceDistance(rho, sigma, wb): Promise<number> — (1/2) ||rho-sigma||_1.
- fidelity(rho, sigma, wb): Promise<number> — Uhlmann F.
- purity(rho): number — pure JS, just tr(rho²).
- embedRealSymplectic(re, im): real-symmetric 2n×2n form for routing complex through real-only linalg-eigh.

NUMERICAL TIER

Index-only ops are bit-identical cross-platform forever (pure index manipulation on float64 — no transcendentals; arithmetic is exact when inputs are exact integers/rationals). Eigh-routed ops inherit `numerical: true` from linalg-eigh.

BLOCKS THE NEW SUB-BEADS

- qn98 (tensor-product) ─┐
- 4jux (partial-trace)   ├─ v0.1 tool beads
- yjs9 (partial-transpose)│ (new bead 2026-05-12)
- pk0c (choi-iso)        ─┘ (new bead 2026-05-12)
- korg (trace-norm)      ─┐
- k2xo (trace-distance)   ├─ v0.2 tool beads (blocked on ov4j)
- 2hxf (fidelity)         │
- 2czd (purity)          ─┘ (purity itself doesn't need eigh — could ship v0.1)

REFERENCE

temp/qwasserstein.ts (dogfood prototype) — has the primitive implementations to lift. Note: dogfood is qubit-only (2^n × 2^n); this substrate generalises to arbitrary dims and adds the complex-OK + index-permutation surface (partialTranspose, choi).
close_reason: v0.1 substrate + 2 tools ship in worklog 098 / ADR-0034. packages/qinfo with kron, partialTrace, partialTracePure, partialTranspose, vec/unvec, choi/deChoi; 56 substrate tests pass with mathematical invariants per Rule 7. tools/tensor-product (11 goldens) + tools/partial-trace (12 goldens). Typed barrel auto-extended. Three principle-led re-scopings vs eq4a's original spec: dims-generalised, flat Float64Array + optional im, complex from day 1 on index-only ops. ADR-0034 + worklog 098.

title: tools/meijer-g-float64: numerical: true sibling for fast complex evaluation (plotting/exploration)
description: A float64 sibling of tools/meijer-g (the arbprec hv0.10 dispatcher). Same cost-ascending dispatch (symbolic → Slater → contour → asymptotic → refuse), same I/O contract, same principal-branch convention, but runs Complex<number> (IEEE 754 doubles) end-to-end instead of BigComplex. Numerical tier per ADR-0015 — bit-identical given platform fingerprint. Use case: interactive exploration and modulus-phase plotting (the canonical 200×200 grid takes ~30–60s instead of 5–60 min in arbprec at precision=10 dps). MOTIVATION: 8-bit-per-channel image output has ~2.4 dps of visible precision; float64's 15–16 dps is vastly more than needed for plotting. The current arbprec stack's BigInt arithmetic is 10–100× slower than native floats; arbprec at precision=10 dps is still BigFloat-substrate-bound, not float64-substrate-bound. SCOPE: new package packages/meijer-core-float64 (or float64 namespace inside @workbench/meijer-core) providing the four lanes in float64. Slater Series 1/2: residue summation with Γ from cas-core's existing float64 evaluator + pFq direct power series in Complex<number>. Contour: G7K15 in Complex<number> — the existing BC driver in packages/quadrature ports cleanly (the BF/BC pair was designed with this in mind; see ADR-0022). Asymptotic: optimal-truncation in float64. Symbolic: unchanged (the symbolic lane returns AST regardless of substrate; only the numerical materialisation differs). Dispatcher: same cost-ascending logic, routes to float64 lanes. Wire tool: tools/meijer-g-float64 with the 'numerical' tier flag set true (NOT the 'arbprec' tier flag) per ADR-0015; standard --platform-fingerprint flag inherited; provenance carries the platform field per ADR-0015. ACCEPTANCE: 200×200 complex grid on a typical (m,n,p,q,z) box completes in ≤60s wall-clock; cross-validated against tools/meijer-g at precision=12 on overlap regions (rel ≤ 1e-10); bit-identical given platform fingerprint (ADR-0015 contract); 50+ tier-graded bench cases mirroring bench/meijer-g (smaller corpus appropriate for the lower-precision target); mutation-prove 5/5 RED. RELATED: hv0.10 closed (the arbprec dispatcher this sibling mirrors); ADR-0015 (numerical tier); ADR-0022 (BigComplex/Complex driver pattern in quadrature); the precedent pattern is bench/integrate-ode-ivp's float64 implementation alongside the arbprec one. NOT BLOCKED by anything; can land any time. Filing in response to user query about modulus-phase plotting (Wikipedia/DLMF style).
notes: ADR-0028 migration: per ADR-0028, the new bench for meijer-g-float64 must land directly in scientist-workbench-corpus/benchmarks/meijer-g-float64/ (NOT in workbench bench/). Precedent: scientist-workbench-corpus/benchmarks/integrate-ode-ivp/ (the float64 IVP bench). Acceptance: 50+ cases graded via bash scripts/bench-grade.sh meijer-g-float64. No blocking deps; can land any time.

title: bigfloat: cgamma precision-loss at small-argument poles (clgammaReflect cancellation)
description: Discovered during 7usr diagnosis. cgamma's reflection-formula path loses ~50 dps of working precision when called near integer poles: Γ(-1 - 2.32e-69) at workingBits=458 diverges from workingBits=800-bit answer at digit 12 of the fractional part. The cexp(iπz) - cexp(-iπz) step in clgammaReflect has catastrophic cancellation at small ε that the +96-bit Stirling margin doesn't absorb. Worked around in @workbench/meijer-core via the empirical precision estimator (worklog 085 / hv0.11.1) — achieved_precision is now honestly reported as 12-14 dps for half-integer-spaced 2-pole cases. A proper substrate fix would let achieved_precision rise to 30+ dps for those same cases. Affects: any caller of cgamma at near-integer-pole arguments. Touches packages/bigfloat/src/complex.ts::clgammaReflect. Acceptance: the empirical estimator's output rises from ~14 dps to ~30 dps on 2-pole half-integer-spaced bench tier-E cases; existing 245 bigfloat tests + 26 tanh-sinh tests still byte-identical.
close_reason: Fixed: clgammaReflect + cdigammaReflect reformulated to reduce z->zeta=z-m before multiplying by pi (localising the one unavoidable cancellation) plus adaptive work = prec+32+lossBits. m=0 region byte-identical. 12 regression tests added (bigfloat 245->257), mutation-proven. Bead's acceptance over-achieved: meijer-core empirical estimator on the 2-pole half-integer witness rose from ~14 dps to full 50 dps, verified honest vs mpmath@120 (>=54-digit agreement). Zero golden drift across 94 oracle phases. Real-argument sibling filed as zhrm. Worklog 117.

When this lands, the largestIntegerSpacedClusterSize gate becomes a no-op and the structured-refusal cases (tagged 'meijer-g/coalescence-needs-higher-order-residue') become numerical successes. title: meijer-g: symbolic-required path doesn't admit rational-real BigComplex parameters
description: tools/meijer-g/tool.ts::bigcomplexToSymbolicValue only converts integer-real BigComplex to int(n). Effect: request_mode='symbolic-required' cases with rational parameters refuse with meijer-g/symbolic-required-no-match even when a literal-rational rule would otherwise match. Bench v0.1 documents this with Tier-A symbolic-required cases using integer-only parameters; rational-symbolic tests can be added once bigcomplexToSymbolicValue widens to rational-real. Acceptance: bigcomplexToSymbolicValue recognises rational-real BigComplex (e.g. via bigfloatToRationalIfExact) and emits rat(p,q) Values; tA-sym-arctan-z1 (or similar rational-param symbolic case) passes with kind=symbolic.

title: meijergContour: cost-bound truncation cap for one-sided pole clusters at |z| ≥ 1
description: The contour layer's pickTruncation doubles T up to 20 times when the integrand tail does not fall below peak·2^-X. For m=0 ∨ n=0 inputs (one-sided Γ-pole cluster) at |z|≥1, the tail decays slower than the Stirling estimate predicts; pickTruncation exits with T≈4×10^7 and the quadrature driver iterates thousands of evaluations before timing out. Dispatcher's canUseContour predicate (ADR-0027 §2) shadows this. Fix: hard cost cap inside pickTruncation; surface a structured refusal cost-bound-truncation if tail still too large after 20 doublings. Acceptance: new refusal class returned within ~10 ms; canUseContour predicate stays as defence-in-depth; 3+ test cases exercise the path.

title: hypergeometric-pfq: analytic continuation for |z| ≥ 0.99
description: 2F1(1, 1; 2; -1) = log 2 is the famous Abel-summation identity at the boundary of the unit disc; the v0.1 tool refuses with non-convergent (Tier E case tE-2F1-z-neg1-boundary in bench/hypergeometric-pfq/). The reference algorithms (Bühring 1987 / Becken-Schmelcher 2000; cited in bench/hypergeometric-pfq/REFERENCES.md) use connection formulas that map z near 1 to 1−z near 0, bringing the case back into the well-conditioned direct-series regime. Acceptance: v0.2 tool admits |z| > 0.99 with p == q + 1 when an analytic-continuation path exists (24 Kummer transformations of 2F1; analogous transformations for higher pFq); bench's Tier E shrinks (cases move to Tier C); new 'Tier C2' added for |z| ∈ [0.99, ∞) reduced via continuation.
notes: ADR-0028 migration: bench at scientist-workbench-corpus/benchmarks/hypergeometric-pfq/ (workbench fa29dab / corpus 86001e5). Tier E refusal cases live in scientist-workbench-corpus/benchmarks/hypergeometric-pfq/golden/inputs.json. When analytic continuation lands, update inputs.json + expected.json to move cases from Tier E to Tier C2. Verify: bash scripts/bench-grade.sh hypergeometric-pfq.

title: compose: merge ADR-0020 --precision flag for arbprec tools
description: (Companion to bead lc1 — same standard-flag wiring gap, different code path.) @workbench/compose's runWorkbench validates partial flags against def.flags ?? {}, ignoring the standard arbprec precision flag merged in by runTool (see packages/contract/src/runner.ts::mergedFlags). Result: the typed barrel wb.hypergeometricPfq(input, { precision: 50n }) is rejected as 'unknown flag precision for this tool'. Bench (bench/hypergeometric-pfq/run-candidate.ts) currently bypasses compose by invoking executeToolDef directly; admissible per ADR-0012 (single-implementation discipline) but defeats the call-site ergonomics compose was created for. Fix: in packages/compose/src/run.ts::runWorkbench, the flagSchema used for validation must be the merged schema, not the bare def.flags. Either export mergedFlags from runner.ts or build an equivalent merge that honours def.arbprec === true ⇒ inject the standard precision slot (and def.numerical === true ⇒ standard flags from STANDARD_FLAGS). Acceptance: typed barrel call wb.hypergeometricPfq(input, { precision: 50n }) succeeds; bench's run-candidate.ts can revert to typed-barrel surface and the executeToolDef workaround is dropped; bun run check stays green; tools/hypergeometric-pfq/tool.test.ts continues passing. RELATED: lc1 fixes the parallel CLI gap in runner.ts; this bead fixes the compose gap. Both should land together to keep the byte-identical-contract from ADR-0012.
close_reason: lc1 + rn2 arbprec --precision flag wiring fixed in one session per ADR-0012 byte-identical contract. title: arbprec runner: --precision flag not threaded into tool fn (CLI vs in-process divergence)
description: The runner (packages/contract/src/runner.ts) parses --precision=N correctly for arbprec tools (it's added to mergedFlags for argv parsing) but does NOT inject the parsed value into toolFlagsTyped (the object passed to def.fn). At runner.ts lines 497-500, Object.keys(toolFlags) iterates only over tool-declared flags (def.flags); precision is added by mergedFlags for arbprec tools but lives in parsed.flags not in toolFlags. So every arbprec-tool's CLI invocation runs at the default precision = 50 dps regardless of the --precision flag. Affected: hypergeometric-pfq, meijer-g-slater-only, meijer-g-asymptotic-only — all share the same (flags as { precision?: bigint }).precision ?? 50n access pattern. In-process callers passing flags directly to def.fn work; CLI invocations don't. Fix: in runner.ts, after the existing loop, conditionally add precision to toolFlagsTyped for def.arbprec === true. title: hv0.9.4 — Symmetric |z| → 0 asymptotic
description: v0.1 ships the n-pole (right-pole, |z| → ∞) asymptotic. title: hv0.9.2 — Stokes-line connection coefficients
description: The v0.1 asymptotic refuses inputs within 2^{-workingBits/4} of |arg z| = π/2 − π/64 (the Stokes-line band). Crossing the line activates exponentially-small contributions from the E_{p,q}(z) exponential series (DLMF §16.11; Paris-Kaminski 2001 §2.3 Stokes-multiplier table). Implement the table for the (m, n, p, q) shapes that the bench battery probes; widen the principal-sector cap accordingly. References: Paris & Kaminski 2001 *Asymptotics and Mellin-Barnes Integrals* CUP §2.3; DLMF §16.11(iii) the regime-by-regime combinations table. Acceptance: Stokes-multiplier table covers at least p = q and p ≤ q − 2 regimes; cross-validation against mpmath / Wolfram on inputs sweeping across arg z = ±π/2.

title: bigfloat::div working-precision tied to numerator mantissa length (silent precision floor)
description: Substrate quirk diagnosed in worklog 077 / bead 6f8 closure. packages/bigfloat/src/arithmetic.ts:92 (the div implementation) computes workingBits = prec + 32, but the effective precision of the quotient is bounded by the *numerator's* mantissa bit-length when that's shorter than the divisor's. Concretely: dividing fromInt(1n) (53-bit default precision attribute) by a 200+-bit denominator at target prec=200 yields a quotient with only ~85 effective bits — the trailing 128 bits of the result mantissa are zero-padded by normalise. This is silent: no warning, no error, the result just quantises to ~26 dps regardless of requested prec. Bites tanh-sinh harder than G7K15 because tanh-sinh divides inside the integrand evaluation path. Worked example in packages/quadrature/src/tanh-sinh-bf.ts API docstring (around line 300). Workaround in scope of hv0.6: integrand contract documented requiring fromInt(N, prec) constructors. Proper fix: bump workingBits in div to max(numeratorBits, denominatorBits) + 32 (or similar), so the quotient inherits the larger mantissa's precision. Cross-validate against mpmath at high prec post-fix to confirm no regression. Lockstep doc updates: ADR-0020 may need amendment if the determinism contract's invariants are affected; bigfloat README needs a precision-attribute-vs-prec-flag clarification section. Acceptance: tanh-sinh test integrand can use fromInt(1n) (default-precision) without precision floor; existing 25 tanh-sinh tests still pass byte-identical (no regression on the principled integrand).
close_reason: bigfloat::div precision-floor substrate fix shipped. Old: workingBits = prec + 32 (ignored input bit-lengths). New: workingBits = prec + 32 + max(0, denBits - numBits) — differential compensation when divisor mantissa exceeds dividend. Quotient now hits exactly prec+32 honest bits regardless of input precision attributes. Byte-identical for every existing call site that respected the worklog-077 integrand contract. Tests: 7 new in arithmetic.test.ts + 1 new in tanh-sinh-bf.test.ts; bigfloat 245/245, tanh-sinh 26/26 all pass; bun run check 69/0/7. Mutation-prove 4 RED on revert; 4 RED on numerator-only-compensation alternative; 3 RED on nondeterminism perturbation. Worklog 084. mul/sqrt/powInt audited: no analogous precision-floor pattern.

title: poly-factor: henselLiftPair fails on palindromic input from alg-num inversion
description:
Calling inv on Root[x⁴ - 4x² + 1, k=3] (i.e. √(2+√3), a real root of a palindromic deg-4 polynomial) fails inside the substrate with 'henselLiftPair: precondition f ≡ g₀·h₀ (mod p) violated'. The same case is hit by case B-nested-05-inv-nested in bench/alg-num-arith.

Reproduction:
`echo '{"kind":"record","fields":{"a":{"kind":"expression","head":"Root","args":[{"kind":"expression","head":"Polynomial","args":[{"kind":"integer","value":"1"},{"kind":"integer","value":"0"},{"kind":"integer","value":"-4"},{"kind":"integer","value":"0"},{"kind":"integer","value":"1"}]},{"kind":"integer","value":"3"}]}}}' | bun tools/alg-num-arith/tool.ts --op=inv`

Likely root cause: algNumInv reverses the coefficient vector of a palindromic minpoly producing the SAME polynomial; the canonicalIntegerForm + factor pipeline then hits some Hensel-lift edge case. Worth checking whether the bug is in algNumInv's reciprocal-polynomial path (incorrectly handling the palindrome case where the reciprocal IS the original) or downstream in poly-factor's Hensel lift on a polynomial whose factors-mod-p don't lift cleanly. Workaround for the bench: case removed from v0.1 cases; reinstate when this bead lands. Worklog 066.
close_reason: Root cause was algNumInv's reverseCoefficients helper in packages/alg-num/src/arithmetic.ts: it preserved the input terms array's order while applying a degree-reversal map on each term, producing a low-to-high term array when cas-core's canonical invariant requires high-to-low. Downstream factorRatQ → henselLiftMany then read the terms in non-canonical order, breaking the f≡g₀·h₀(mod p) precondition. Fix (~3 LOC): append .reverse() after the .map. Regression test added in packages/alg-num/test/arithmetic.test.ts; bench/alg-num-arith case B-nested-05-inv-nested reinstated. 32/32 cases + 76/76 alg-num tests + 65/65 check phases all green. Worklog 067.

title: packages/alg-num: subresultant-based sum + product
description:
Arithmetic on two Roots `alpha` (minpoly f), `beta` (minpoly g):
- minpoly(alpha + beta) = squarefree(Res_y(f(y), g(x - y)))
- minpoly(alpha * beta) = squarefree(Res_y(y^deg(g) * f(x/y), g(y)))
Compute resultants via Brown-Traub subresultant PRS (already in cas-core's polyGcd). Identify the correct root k of the result using interval arithmetic on the input intervals.

Reference: Cohen GTM 138 §3.6.2 (resultants), Algorithm 3.6.1 (sum-of-roots minpoly).

title: packages/poly-factor: Mignotte bound + recombination
description:
Mignotte 1974 coefficient bound: any factor of f in Z[x] has coefficients bounded by M(f) = (n choose floor(n/2)) * ||f||_infinity * ... (the standard formula). Lift Hensel until p^k > 2*M(f). Recombination: try subsets of the p-adic factors of size 1, 2, ..., floor(r/2); a subset whose product (lifted to Z) divides f exactly is a true factor.

v1 ships classical Berlekamp-Zassenhaus (worst-case 2^r). van Hoeij (LLL-based knapsack) is deferred to v2 as a fallback when r > 8.

description:
Second slice of the ODE epic (parent: scientist-workbench-32z). Solves dy/dt = f(t, y), y(t0) = y0 for stiff systems where the explicit RKF45 path is forced to take infinitesimally small steps to maintain stability.

Stiffness arises whenever the system has widely separated time scales — Robertson chemistry kinetics (3 species, rates spanning 7 orders of magnitude), van der Pol at large mu (relaxation oscillations), HIRES (chemical reaction network), Oregonator (Belousov-Zhabotinsky reaction). Universal in chemistry kinetics, plasma physics, electrical engineering, slow-fast systems generally.

Algorithm choice: 5-stage Radau-IIA (the scipy 'Radau' algorithm; A-stable, L-stable, 5th-order; collocation at Radau points) OR BDF (variable-order backward differentiation, scipy 'BDF'). Radau-IIA is the cleaner choice for the path-finder — single algorithm, no order-selection logic, well-understood Newton iteration structure.

Per-step Newton iteration on the implicit equation requires a linear solve. Composes linalg-solve internally. If f's Jacobian is symbolic (computable via cas-diff over the closed vocabulary), use it; otherwise finite-difference Jacobian.

Wire input: matches integrate-ode-ivp plus options.method ('radau' default, 'bdf' alternative). Wire output: matches integrate-ode-ivp plus n_jacobian_evals, n_lu_decompositions.

Boundary tags: same three as integrate-ode-ivp plus 'integrate-ode-stiff/jacobian-singular' (Newton iteration's linear solve hit a singular Jacobian — system is structurally ill-posed at the encountered state).
design: Algorithm: Radau-IIA(5) per Hairer-Wanner Vol II §IV.8 (canonical reference), with simplified Newton iteration (use one Jacobian for several steps via PI step-size controller). Substrate: extend packages/ode-core/ from the path-finder. Symbolic Jacobian via cas-diff when f's components are in the closed vocabulary; finite-difference fallback otherwise (with a warning to that effect in the output). Bench tiers mirror integrate-ode-ivp but with NHW Vol II problems: B canonical (Robertson, van der Pol mu=1, harmonic oscillator), C stiffness sweep (van der Pol mu=1, 100, 1e4, 1e6), D conservation on quasi-conservative systems, E boundary (Jacobian singular at encountered y), I industrial (NHW Vol II catalog: HIRES, Oregonator, Pollu, etc.).
acceptance_criteria: bench/integrate-ode-stiff/ scaffold complete; SciPy reference (solve_ivp method='Radau') passes its own verifier; tools/integrate-ode-stiff/ ships seven artefacts; bun run check green; bench 100% pass on Robertson, HIRES, van der Pol mu=1e6, Oregonator stress regime
notes: Bench dossier staged 2026-05-05: 19 cases (A shape edges, B mild-stiff, C stiffness sweep vdP μ∈{100,1e3,1e4}, D NHW Vol II canonical Robertson/Oregonator/HIRES, E boundary degenerate-tspan/method-bdf/unknown-head/dim-mismatch, F tolerance discipline Robertson at rtol∈{1e-3,1e-6,1e-9}). Reference scipy Radau at rtol=1e-13 passes verifier 19/19. Verifier checks 9 invariants per success-path case including stiffness_handled (Radau must use Jacobian) and jacobian_consumed (analytic J actually consumed when provided). Tagged tags: degenerate-tspan, non-finite-during-eval, jacobian-singular, method-not-implemented (for options.method='bdf').

title: integrate-ode-ivp — non-stiff IVP via Dormand-Prince RKF45 (path-finder)
description:
First slice of the ODE epic (parent: scientist-workbench-32z). Path-finder for the tournament-protocol applied to time-stepping ODE solvers.

Solves dy/dt = f(t, y), y(t0) = y0 over t in [t0, tf] for non-stiff systems via Dormand-Prince 4(5) — explicit Runge-Kutta with embedded 4th-order error estimate, adaptive step-size via PI controller. The scipy.integrate.solve_ivp method='RK45' algorithm; matlab.ode45's algorithm. Workhorse of computational science for non-stiff problems.

Wire input: record{f: list<expression>, vars: list<symbol>, t_var: symbol, y0: list<float64>, t_span: record{t0: float64, tf: float64}, options?: record{rtol?, atol?, max_step?, t_eval?: list<float64>}}.

Wire output: record{
  trajectory: list<list<float64>>,    // (n_eval × n_components)
  t_values: list<float64>,             // (n_eval,)
  error_estimate: float64,             // sup-norm of last accepted local error / atol
  n_evals: integer,                    // function evals (RKF45 = 6 per accepted step + ~2 per rejected)
  n_steps_accepted: integer,
  n_steps_rejected: integer,
  converged: boolean,                  // true unless integration aborted
  status: string,                      // 'success' | 'max_step_exceeded' | 'tspan_exhausted'
  method: string,                      // 'dormand-prince-45'
  warnings: list<string>
}.

Boundary tags (ADR-0003):
- 'integrate-ode-ivp/non-finite-during-eval' — f returned NaN/Inf at some t (payload: t, y at point of failure)
- 'integrate-ode-ivp/degenerate-tspan' — tf == t0 (payload: tspan)
- ToolError for: dim mismatch (len(f) != len(y0) != len(vars)), unknown head in f, malformed options, true OOM
design: Algorithm: Dormand-Prince DOPRI5 with embedded 4(5) error estimate (Hairer-Norsett-Wanner Vol I §II.5), PI step-size controller (Gustafsson 1991). Substrate: new packages/ode-core/ (mirrors linalg-core / quadrature pattern; pure Float64Array, no FFI). Closed vocabulary for f matches cas-diff / integrate-1d (so cas-diff can auto-generate Jacobians for the future stiff slice). numerical: true (ADR-0015); no hard cap (ADR-0016) — uses assessNumericalScale('ode-rkf45', n_components, n_steps_estimate). Bench tiers: A shape edges (1D scalar, 2D Lotka-Volterra, 3D Lorenz), B canonical (NHW Vol I non-stiff suite — Lotka-Volterra, Brusselator, Kepler-2body, exponential decay, oscillator), C precision sweep (rtol = 1e-3 to 1e-12 on a single hard problem to probe error-control), D long-time conservation (Kepler-2body energy + angular momentum drift), E boundary (NaN in f, tspan backward, dim mismatch), I industrial (full NHW Vol I catalog where licensing permits). Reference: scipy.integrate.solve_ivp with method='RK45' and tight tolerance; cross-check at relaxed tolerance for the candidate.

title: ODE solver suite (integrate-ode-{ivp,stiff,symplectic}) — parent epic
description:
Highest-leverage missing tool for the conference-physics workflow (every field cited — physics, maths, chem, economics, biology — needs ODEs). Three slices, registered as child beads:

1. integrate-ode-ivp — non-stiff via Dormand-Prince RKF45 (the scipy.RK45 / matlab.ode45 standard). Path-finder for the protocol applied to ODE.
2. integrate-ode-stiff — implicit BDF or Radau-IIA for stiff systems (Robertson chemistry, van der Pol at large mu, etc.). Requires linalg-solve internally for the per-step Newton iteration.
3. integrate-ode-symplectic — structure-preserving Verlet / leapfrog / Yoshida-4 for Hamiltonian systems where energy conservation over long integrations matters (orbital mechanics, classical mech, MD).

Inherits all the numerical-tier discipline established in worklogs 043-047:
- numerical: true (ADR-0015), platform fingerprint in provenance
- no hard cap (ADR-0016): scale warnings via assessNumericalScale
- agent-honest output: trajectory + error_estimate + n_evals + converged + method + warnings, all as fields
- tournament-style bench (per-tool bench/integrate-ode-{slice}/ with PROMPT, DESCRIPTION, REFERENCES, golden/{generate,verify,verifier_protocol}, reference/, run-candidate.ts)
- invariant-based verifier (NOT byte-equality — tolerances derived from method's local truncation error + 100x safety)
- NIST/canonical corpora where they exist: Hairer-Norsett-Wanner Vol I (non-stiff) and Vol II (stiff) test-problem suites are the standard
- closed vocabulary for f(t, y) matches cas-diff / integrate-1d / optimize-lbfgs-projected so symbolic differentiation, Jacobian computation, etc. compose without scope translation

Open design questions for the path-finder to settle:
A. Substrate package: new @workbench/ode-core (matches linalg-core precedent) or extend @workbench/quadrature (already has the closed-vocabulary evaluator)? Recommendation: new package — different algorithm class, different storage idioms.
B. Output trajectory shape: dense (every internal step) or evaluated-at-requested-times (numpy.linspace(t0, tf, N))? Probably the latter as default with a flag for dense output (mirror scipy's t_eval).
C. Vector-valued f signature on the wire: list<expression> (one per component) is the natural fit for the closed vocabulary; alternative is a single record-valued expression.
D. Reverse integration (tf < t0) — accept and integrate backward, or boundary-tag? scipy accepts; recommend matching.
design: Reference oracle: scipy.integrate.solve_ivp with method='RK45' (non-stiff), 'BDF' or 'Radau' (stiff), and a Verlet implementation for symplectic. Bench tiers per slice: A shape/edge, B canonical (Lotka-Volterra, Brusselator, Lorenz, Kepler-2body, harmonic), C stress (high-stiffness, long-time integration), D conservation (energy/mass within stable bounds), E boundary (non-finite f, NaN in y0, etc.), I industrial (NHW Vol I/II catalog), J post-cap stress (large-N coupled systems via method-of-lines). Tolerances: invariant residual = local truncation error * step count * 100 safety, mirroring the linalg pattern.
acceptance_criteria: three child beads created with proper deps; integrate-ode-ivp shipped as path-finder; bench protocol proven extensible to time-stepping ODEs; bun run check green; bench(es) 100% pass
close_reason: All three children closed: scientist-workbench-l6p (path-finder DOPRI5), scientist-workbench-09g (stiff Radau-IIA), scientist-workbench-4gr (symplectic Verlet/Yoshida-4). Bench protocol proven extensible to time-stepping ODEs across three algorithm classes (explicit non-stiff, implicit stiff, structure-preserving). Worklogs 048/049/050 capture each slice.

title: Tier-1 vocabulary extension: inverse trig + hyperbolics + log-with-base
description:
## Background

Closed-vocabulary surface as of 2026-05-04 (commit f7e0b37):
`+ - * / ^ neg exp sin cos tan log sqrt abs` plus `pi`, `e`. Lives in
`packages/quadrature/src/eval-expr.ts:ADMITTED_HEADS` and
`packages/cas-core/src/diff.ts:DIFF_ADMITTED_HEADS` (matched
deliberately so cas-diff → integrate-1d → optimize composes without
vocabulary mismatches).

A TS expert reaches for `Math.atan`, `Math.tanh`, `Math.log2`
regularly. Their absence is the most-likely-to-bite friction in the
v0.1 surface for any agent doing routine analysis. Each is mechanical
to add (single-argument, maps directly to `Math.*`, has a closed-form
derivative in the existing vocab). Cost is roughly one afternoon for
the whole batch.

## Heads to add (tier 1)

| head | f(x) | f'(x) (in our vocab + new heads) | Math equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|
| `asin` | arcsin(x) | `1 / sqrt(1 - x²)` | `Math.asin` |
| `acos` | arccos(x) | `neg(1) / sqrt(1 - x²)` | `Math.acos` |
| `atan` | arctan(x) | `1 / (1 + x²)` | `Math.atan` |
| `sinh` | sinh(x) | `cosh(x)` | `Math.sinh` |
| `cosh` | cosh(x) | `sinh(x)` | `Math.cosh` |
| `tanh` | tanh(x) | `1 - tanh(x)^2` | `Math.tanh` |
| `asinh` | arcsinh(x) | `1 / sqrt(1 + x²)` | `Math.asinh` |
| `acosh` | arccosh(x) | `1 / sqrt(x² - 1)`  (defined for x ≥ 1) | `Math.acosh` |
| `atanh` | arctanh(x) | `1 / (1 - x²)`  (defined for |x| < 1) | `Math.atanh` |
| `log2` | log₂(x) | `1 / (x * log(2))` | `Math.log2` |
| `log10` | log₁₀(x) | `1 / (x * log(10))` | `Math.log10` |

All single-argument; chain rule wraps each as
`d(f(g(x)))/dx = f'(g(x)) · g'(x)`.

`tanh`'s derivative could be `1/cosh(x)^2` — equivalent — but the
`1 - tanh(x)^2` form is the standard textbook expression and avoids
introducing `cosh` evaluation when the original was `tanh`.

## Out of scope (deferred to tier-2)

- Multi-arg `log(base, x)` — variadic shape change, separate proposal.
- `atan2(y, x)` — multi-arg, partial-differentiation design call.
- `min`, `max` — non-smooth at the equality locus; cas-diff would have
  to refuse (or emit subdifferentials honestly).
- `floor`, `ceil`, `round`, `trunc`, `sign`, `mod` — non-smooth; eval
  could admit them but cas-diff should refuse. ADR-worthy: should the
  eval-vocab and diff-vocab diverge?
- Special functions (`gamma`, `erf`, `Bessel`, …) — require an actual
  numerical implementation, not just `Math.*` dispatch. Tier-3, file
  separately when motivated.

## Fix

For each head:

1. `packages/quadrature/src/eval-expr.ts`:
   - Append to `ADMITTED_HEADS`.
   - Add a `case "<head>": return Math.<head>(evalNumericExpr(args[0], env));`
     in the `expression` switch.
   - Update the file's documentation block (lines 22–34 list the
     vocabulary verbatim — keep it in lockstep).
2. `packages/cas-core/src/diff.ts`:
   - Append to `DIFF_ADMITTED_HEADS`.
   - Add a `case "<head>":` to `diffExpression` returning the chain-
     rule product (use `mkTimes`, `mkDiv`, `mkPower`, `mkNeg`, `expr`
     helpers and the existing smart constructors).
   - Update the file's documentation block (the rule-table comment
     near the top) so it lists the new rules verbatim.
3. `packages/cas-core/test/diff.test.ts`:
   - Add unit tests for each new head's structural derivative.
   - Add ≥1 FD-corpus probe per new head, with evaluation points
     in the function's natural domain (acosh: x > 1; atanh: |x| < 1;
     log2/log10: x > 0; etc.).
   - The coverage-sanity test will then assert all 24 admitted heads
     appear in the FD corpus — no silent drops.
4. `packages/quadrature/test/eval-expr.test.ts` (if it exists; if not,
   the diff FD-cross-check exercises the eval too):
   - One probe per new head verifying numeric agreement with `Math.*`.

## Documentation lockstep (Law 2)

- `tools/cas-diff/README.md`: extend the rule table.
- `tools/integrate-1d/README.md`: update the closed-vocabulary list.
- `tools/optimize-lbfgs-projected/README.md`: update the closed-vocab list.
- `README.md`: catalog rows for cas-diff, integrate-1d,
  optimize-lbfgs-projected mention the vocab — keep in sync.
- Worklog shard documenting the extension.

## Acceptance

- `bun run check` green: every phase passes including the cas-diff /
  integrate-1d / optimize-lbfgs-projected `--test` and oracle phases.
- `bun test packages/cas-core/test/diff.test.ts` adds ≥11 new tests
  (one per head); coverage-sanity test green with all 24 heads.
- 11 new heads all callable end-to-end through `wb.casDiff`,
  `wb.integrate1d`, `wb.optimizeLbfgsProjected`.
- Three tool READMEs + main README + worklog updated in lockstep.

title: tools/cas-diff: symbolic differentiation over the closed vocabulary
description:
## Background

The friction surfaced during the `min ∫ p(x,a) dx over a ∈ [-1,1]`
demo (scripts/demo-min-integral.ts): integrate-1d and
optimize-lbfgs-projected compose if you can pre-compute the
gradient as an expression — and the natural source of that
expression is symbolic differentiation. cas-simplify exists; the
sister cas-diff does not. Without cas-diff an agent must hand-derive
gradients (or fall back to finite differences, doubling integrate-1d
calls per outer iteration).

This is the cheapest, highest-leverage missing CAS tool given the
two-principles framing (TS-expert + agent-irresistibility).

## Design

### Vocabulary

Closed vocab matches integrate-1d / optimize-lbfgs-projected:
`+ − * / ^ neg exp sin cos tan log sqrt abs` plus constants `pi`, `e`,
plus integer / rational / float64 leaves and symbol variables. (Wider
than cas-simplify's vocab — cas-simplify excludes transcendentals.)

### Differentiation rules (over `var = wrt`):

- atoms: integer/rational/float64 → 0; pi/e → 0
- symbol s: 1 if s.name == wrt.name (and same namespace) else 0
- `+(...)` → `+(da, db, ...)`
- `-(a, b)` → `-(da, db)`; unary `-(a)` → `-(da)`
- `neg(a)` → `neg(da)`
- `*(a, b, ...)` → product rule (n-ary)
- `/(a, b)` → `(da*b - a*db) / b^2`
- `^(a, b)`:
  - b constant in wrt: `b * a^(b-1) * da`        (power rule)
  - a constant in wrt: `a^b * log(a) * db`        (exponential rule)
  - general:           `a^b * (db*log(a) + b*da/a)` (log-chain)
- `exp(a)` → `exp(a) * da`
- `log(a)` → `da / a`
- `sin(a)` → `cos(a) * da`
- `cos(a)` → `neg(sin(a)) * da`
- `tan(a)` → `da / cos(a)^2`
- `sqrt(a)` → `da / (2 * sqrt(a))`
- `abs(a)` → `a/abs(a) * da` (singular at 0; correct on R\{0})

### Boundary discipline

Any subterm head outside the rule table → top-level
`tagged "cas-diff/out-of-scope"` whose payload is the original
input. Binary yes/no for the agent (rather than embedded tagged
sub-nodes that the agent must walk).

### Smart constructors only

Drop `0+x`, `1*x`, `x*0=0`, `x^0=1`, `x^1=x`, `neg(0)=0`,
`neg(neg(x))=x`. No internal cas-simplify call — pipe through
cas-simplify externally if full reduction wanted. Decomposition
discipline (Rule 4 / one tool one operation).

### Library / tool split

- `packages/cas-core/src/diff.ts` — `differentiate(expr, wrt)`
  returning `{kind:"ok",value} | {kind:"out-of-scope",head}`.
- `tools/cas-diff/tool.ts` — wire wrapper, `numerical: false`,
  full provenance.

### Input / output schema

Input: `record { f: <expression>, var: <symbol> }` — `f` mirrors
integrate-1d's field name for cross-tool symmetry.

Output: `<expression>` (record-or-expression Value) on success, or
`tagged "cas-diff/out-of-scope": <original input>` on boundary.

Malformed input (var not a symbol, etc.) → `ToolError` (schema
validation).

## Acceptance

- `bun test packages/cas-core/test/diff.test.ts` green: rule-by-rule
  unit tests + numerical FD cross-check property tests + mutation
  comments naming ≥2 caught mutations.
- `bun tools/cas-diff/tool.ts --test` passes a corpus of ~20
  expressions, asserting numerical agreement (rel ≤ 1e-6) between
  symbolic diff and finite-difference at random points.
- `bun run goldens --tool cas-diff` writes goldens; oracle byte-stable.
- `bun run check` green.
- README + catalog row in main README + worklog shard.
- @workbench/compose typed barrel regenerated.

## Determinism tier

`numerical: false` (default symbolic tier) — output bit-identical
cross-platform forever. Same as cas-simplify. ADR-0015 doesn't apply.
close_reason: Closed

Includes the per-platform fingerprint format the provenance store carries.
