title: Fix Sturm-TS spec §8.1 library: H, not, Y derivations under sturm-execute's RY convention
description:
Follow-up to scientist-workbench-4xk (verification confirmed bug under sturm-execute's textbook convention RY(theta) = exp(-i*theta/2 * Y)).

Numerical evidence (scripts/probe-h-equivalence.ts):
- Probe 1 (apply spec H twice, observe): P(r=1)=1.0. Real H·H = I predicts P(r=0)=1.0.
- Probe 2 (spec H, rz(pi), spec H, observe): P(r=0)=1.0. Real H·Z·H = X on |0> predicts P(r=1)=1.0.

Audit of §8.1:

CORRECT under the convention:
- Z(q) := rz(pi). Rz(pi) = diag(-i, i) = -i*Z, so Z up to global phase. OK.
- S(q) := rz(pi/2). Rz(pi/2) = exp(-i*pi/4) * S, so S up to global phase. OK.
- T(q) := rz(pi/4). Rz(pi/4) = exp(-i*pi/8) * T, so T up to global phase. OK.

BUGGY under the convention:
- H(q) := ry(pi/2); ry(pi). Composes to Ry(pi)*Ry(pi/2) = Ry(3pi/2). H has det -1, Ry has det +1; no global phase relates them. Hadamard's Bloch axis is (X+Z)/sqrt(2), no Y-component, so H cannot be expressed in the Ry-only family.
- not(QBool) := ry(pi). Spec comment claims 'X = Ry(pi) up to global phase'; actually Ry(pi) = -i*Y, off from X by Z. In computational-basis bit-flip statistics it acts correctly (golden 05-ry-acts-as-not confirms |0> -> |1>); in coherent compositions with superposition targets it differs from real X.
- Y(q) := rz(pi); ry(pi). State-app order: ry(pi)*rz(pi) = (-iY)*(-iZ) = -YZ = -i*X (since YZ = i*X), so this composes to X up to global phase, NOT Y. The simple correct definition is just Y(q) := ry(pi), since Ry(pi) = -i*Y is Y up to global phase.

DESIGN OPTIONS for the fix:

Option A — ZYZ replacements (coherent equivalence):
  - H(q): rz(pi); ry(pi/2)  (gives -i*H, equal to H up to global phase)
  - not(QBool): rz(pi); ry(pi)  (gives i*X, equal to X up to global phase)
  - Y(q): ry(pi)  (gives -i*Y, equal to Y up to global phase)
  Pros: gates are coherently equivalent to their named referents; works in superposition contexts; phase kickback / Grover / QFT correct.
  Cons: not and H both grow from 1 op to 2 ops; controlled forms (when(c, () => not(t))) become 2-op controlled-rotation sequences; Bell pair example circuit depth doubles.

Option B — keep ry-only, document the caveat:
  - not(QBool): ry(pi). Document 'differs from X by a relative Z; correct for standard-basis bit-flip statistics, not for coherent applications on superposition targets.'
  - H(q): no fix possible (truly cannot be written from ry alone). Must use Option A's form. So this option is partial — H must change regardless.
  - Y(q): ry(pi).
  Pros: minimal circuit-depth impact for not; matches the existing 05-ry-acts-as-not golden's standard-basis interpretation.
  Cons: 'differs from X by Z' is exactly the kind of footgun that breaks phase kickback when an agent reaches for not() inside an oracle.

Option C — change RY convention (NOT recommended):
  Define ry(delta) as a Bloch-rotation by 2*delta, so Ry(pi) corresponds to a Bloch full rotation = -I. Doesn't fix H either. Rejected.

Recommendation: Option A. Pay the circuit-depth cost; library users get gates that are what their names say, no caveats. The implementation cost is small (one extra op per H/not/Y); the readability + correctness benefit is large.

Approach (whichever option chosen):
1. Decide option A or B (or hybrid: A for H, B for not/Y).
2. Update the live spec body? The spec is provenance-preserved verbatim under docs/sturm-ts/spec-v3.md — DO NOT edit the body. Instead either:
   a. Add a docs/sturm-ts/spec-v3-amendments.md with the corrected library derivations, and reference it from the preamble.
   b. Add an §8.1-corrections section to docs/sturm-ts/principles.md (which is the v3.1 source of truth and already supersedes the spec on P2).
3. Update spec-v3.md preamble item 1 to point at the resolution doc.
4. If/when @sturm/library is implemented in the workbench (no current package), use the corrected forms.

Pitfalls:
- The Bell-pair worked example (§13.1) currently uses 'when(a, () => not(b))' with not := ry(pi), which gives correct standard-basis Bell statistics. Under Option A, the example's controlled form changes from cry(a,b,pi) to crz(a,b,pi); cry(a,b,pi) — verify that simplification + execute still produce the same Bell distribution (they should, but worth a sanity probe via scripts/).
- §13.4 phaseKickback comment 'ry(q, Math.PI / 2) // = H, via library' is misleading regardless of which option is chosen. Ry(pi/2) is the correct way to take |0> -> |+>, but it is not 'H' in general. The correction is contextual: 'prepares |+> from |0>' is the honest description.
acceptance_criteria:
Design option (A/B/hybrid) chosen and recorded in this issue's notes.
spec-v3.md preamble item 1 updated to point at the resolution doc.
A docs/sturm-ts/spec-v3-amendments.md (or principles.md addendum) carries the corrected library derivations.
Bell-pair end-to-end probe still produces the textbook Bell distribution under the corrected library forms (run via scripts/, no new tool needed).

title: q0b prerequisite — define tracer rejection rules for non-unitary ops inside when
description:
ADR-0006 admits a 'controls' field only on ry/rz op-nodes (the unitary primitives). Non-unitary ops — observe, cases, discard — have no controls field. The ADR explicitly notes that coherent control on non-unitary ops 'is not well-defined.'

Spec v3 §6 says ops emitted inside a when body carry the whenStack as their controls field, but does not say what happens if observe/cases/discard/prepare appears in a when body. This is a tracer-level invariant sturm-trace (q0b) must enforce before its v0.1.

Approach — decide and document:
1. Which op kinds are forbidden inside a when. At minimum: observe, cases, discard. Open question: is prepare allowed? (Allocates a fresh wire; the wire's |0> amplitude does not depend on the control, so an unconditional prepare inside a when body is harmless.) Recommendation: forbid for v0.1, document, revisit if a use case appears.
2. Error shape. Boundary-tag (tagged 'sturm-trace/invalid-when-body') is the right call per ADR-0003 — the user wrote a syntactically valid but structurally invalid program. ToolError is reserved for malformed input shapes.
3. Defense-in-depth: packages/sturm-ir's wellformed.ts should also catch IR with these violations after the fact, since an agent constructing IR directly could try this. The check walks cases arms recursively and validates that no non-unitary op appears with controls in scope.

Pitfall: do not relax the rule by adding controls fields to observe/cases/discard. ADR-0006's rationale (coherent control on non-unitary ops is ill-defined) is load-bearing.
acceptance_criteria:
Decision documented in q0b's notes (forbidden ops, error shape).
packages/sturm-ir/src/wellformed.ts updated to catch the violations structurally (independent of any tracer).
Tests cover at least one rejection path per forbidden op.
close_reason: Closed

title: Verify Sturm-TS spec §8.1 library Y-axis derivations against sturm-execute's convention
description:
Spec docs/sturm-ts/spec-v3.md §8.1 defines library gates from the three primitives. Two derivations look suspect under sturm-execute's textbook convention (tools/sturm-execute/tool.ts:408 — RY(theta) = [[cos(theta/2), -sin(theta/2)], [sin(theta/2), cos(theta/2)]]):

- not(QBool) ::= ry(pi). Comment claims 'X = Ry(pi) up to global phase.' Under the textbook convention Ry(pi) = [[0,-1],[1,0]] = -i*Y, which differs from X by a Z (X = Z*Ry(pi)), not by a global phase.
- H(q) ::= ry(pi/2); ry(pi). Body composes (source-order = state-application-order) to Ry(pi)*Ry(pi/2) = Ry(3pi/2). H has det -1; Ry(3pi/2) has det +1; no phase factor relates them. H's Bloch axis is (X+Z)/sqrt(2) which has no Y-component, so H cannot be expressed in the Ry-only family.

If correct as written, the v0.1 library would silently produce wrong amplitudes for any Hadamard-using algorithm (Grover, QFT, Deutsch-Jozsa, Bernstein-Vazirani, ...). BUT — this kind of 'is it a phase or not' question has tripped agents looking at Sturm.jl analogues before, and may reflect a convention difference (e.g. Sturm.jl might define ry as a 2x-Bloch-rotation, or the library may carry an implicit standard-basis-only caveat) rather than a derivation bug. Numerical run is the source of truth.

Approach — drive sturm-execute on two probes that distinguish real H from Ry(3pi/2):

Probe 1 — H*H = I sanity check (apply spec H twice):
  IR sequence: prepare(0); ry(pi/2); ry(pi); ry(pi/2); ry(pi); observe(r)
  Real H semantics: H*H = I, so P(r=0) = 1.
  Spec-library semantics: Ry(pi/2)+Ry(pi)+Ry(pi/2)+Ry(pi) fuses to Ry(3pi) = i*Y, so |0> maps to -|1>, so P(r=1) = 1.

Probe 2 — H*Z*H = X (apply spec H, Z, spec H):
  IR sequence: prepare(0); ry(pi/2); ry(pi); rz(pi); ry(pi/2); ry(pi); observe(r)
  Real H semantics: H*Z*H = X applied to |0>, so P(r=1) = 1.
  Spec-library semantics: composes to -i*Z applied to |0>, so P(r=0) = 1.

Both probes predict opposite outcomes between real-H and spec-library, so one run resolves it.

Decide:
- If empirically distinguishable from real H: spec library has a derivation bug. Propose ZYZ Euler form (e.g. H = Rz(pi/2)*Ry(pi/2)*Rz(pi/2) up to global phase), file follow-up fix issue, update spec-v3.md preamble to reflect resolved status.
- If empirically equivalent to real H: I have misread the convention. Document the convention difference in spec-v3.md and principles.md, close as 'not a bug.'

Pitfalls:
- Bell-pair / GHZ goldens use only standard-basis prep + standard-basis measurement, which mask the Ry(pi) vs X relative-phase difference. Probes above are designed to expose the difference via composition.
- sturm-simplify will fuse adjacent same-axis ry's. That is fine — the fused angle still distinguishes (Ry(3pi) is not I).
acceptance_criteria:
Both probe IRs run through tools/sturm-execute; outputs recorded in issue notes.
Decision recorded in issue: bug -> file fix issue + update spec-v3.md preamble; not-bug -> document convention difference, close as 'not a bug.'
spec-v3.md preamble open-issue note for §8.1 updated to reflect resolution.
close_reason: Verified empirically via scripts/probe-h-equivalence.ts: spec §8.1 H derivation produces Ry(3pi/2), not Hadamard, under sturm-execute's textbook RY convention. Probe 1 (H*H): P(r=1)=1.0 (real H predicts P(r=0)=1.0). Probe 2 (HZH): P(r=0)=1.0 (real H predicts P(r=1)=1.0). Both probes confirm. Audit also flagged not(QBool) (off from X by Z) and Y(q) (composes to X, not Y) as bugs; Z/S/T are correct. Fix issue scientist-workbench-1td filed with design options (Option A: ZYZ replacements; Option B: keep ry-only with documented caveat for not/Y but H must change). spec-v3.md preamble updated to reflect verified-bug-confirmed status.

title: sturm-execute exact-symbolic path: Q[√2,i] amplitudes with Q[√2]-rational probabilities
description:
Follow-up to tkx (v0.1 sturm-execute ships float64-only). The exact path was deferred because individual measurement probabilities for the restricted gate set {prepare(0|1|1/2), ry(kπ/2), rz(kπ/2)} land in Q[√2], not Q. Concrete counterexample: ry(π/2)·CRy(π/2)·ry(π/2) on |00⟩ produces amps with mixed Q+√2·i components, and Prob(wire_0=0)=1/2−√2/4 (irrational). The unitarity invariant Σ|amp|²=1 still holds rationally, but per-outcome marginals don't.

Design questions to resolve before this lands:
1. Probability shape: extend schema to admit Q[√2]-rational probabilities? Or convert to float64 and label precision='exact-amps-float-prob'? Or restrict scope further (only circuits where outcome probabilities are provably Q-rational)?
2. Renormalisation strategy after observe: don't renormalise (carry sub-normalised amps; branch probability = Σ|amp|²) is the cleanest with our gate set since renormalisation factors √Prob can be irrational.
3. Recogniser API: cas-simplify the angle, then a pattern-matcher over the canonical form for k·π/2 multiples. Falls back to float64 path if any angle/prob doesn't recognise.

Implementation sketch:
- Use packages/cas-core's Q_SQRT2_I as the amplitude ring.
- ComplexRing<Amp,Real> abstraction over (Q[√2,i], Q[√2]) for exact and ({re,im}, number) for float64.
- Output: extend distributionOutcomeSchema with an 'exact-q-sqrt2' probability variant (record{a, b} encoding a + b√2)?

Pre-conditions: tkx (sturm-execute float64) closed; sturm-equivalent (564) close to landing so we know what shape exact equivalence checks need.

title: cas-core polynomial GCD (subresultant or sparse modular)
description:
Add polynomial GCD to packages/cas-core. Gates cas-reduce (closes the known v1 gap from PRD §0.1), cas-factor, partial-fractions support in cas-simplify, and Hermite reduction (eventually for cas-integrate).

ALGORITHM CHOICE
- Subresultant PRS: well-understood, stable bigint arithmetic, ~300 LOC. Good first implementation.
- Sparse modular GCD: faster for large multivariate inputs but more complex; defer.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- packages/cas-core/src/poly-gcd.ts (or similar) exists.
- Multivariate GCD implementation (or univariate with documented scope-limit).
- ≥15 tests including: gcd(p, p) = p, gcd(p, 0) = p, gcd of coprime polynomials = unit, gcd preserves degree bounds, mutation-proven.
- bun run check passes.
- Worklog shard added.

DEPENDS ON
- ring-generic refactor issue landed.

BLOCKS

close_reason: ADR-0013 + worklog 030 shipped. polyGcd via Brown-Collins subresultant PRS, multivariate via recursion. cas-simplify v0.4.0 reduces rational functions to lowest terms; (x²-1)/(x-1) → x+1. 39 dedicated tests, mutation-proven on three perturbations. Modular GCD filed as v0.2 follow-up (6uc, P4).

title: tools/sturm-controlled: channel combinators (controlled, then, tensor)
description:
A small group of channel-on-channel transformations that give point-free composition at the Value level. Together with sturm-qecc-wrap and sturm-bennett-oracle, these are the higher-order operators that make the channel category visible at the agent layer.

Tools (one tool dir per combinator, or a single tool dispatching on a flag — TBD in design):
- `controlled(c, f)`: take a control wire and a channel; emit a channel where every op in f's body carries c on its `controls` field.
- `then(f, g)`: sequential composition. Output wires of f wired into input wires of g; signatures must match.
- `tensor(f, g)`: parallel composition. Produces a channel whose wires are the disjoint union of f's and g's.

Tool invariants: the categorical laws — associativity of `then`, identity laws, monoidal-functor laws for `tensor`.
design: Open: one tool per combinator vs. one tool with a mode flag. The CLAUDE.md guidance "Flags that change the type of the output should be different tools" suggests separate tools, since `controlled` consumes a channel + control wire while `then` consumes two channels. Default to separate tools; revisit if redundancy in scaffolding is significant.
acceptance_criteria:
- tools/sturm-controlled/, tools/sturm-then/, tools/sturm-tensor/ each conform to the 7-artefact contract — OR a unified tools/sturm-compose/ if design favours one tool with mode flag.
- ≥10 examples per tool covering identity, associativity, edge cases (empty body, mismatched signatures with tagged failure).
- Property tests for the categorical laws.
- Main README.md catalog rows.
close_reason: Three sibling tools shipped: sturm-controlled (19 goldens, control-stamping + wire-conflict + non-unitary boundary tags), sturm-then (14 goldens, signature-matching + wire-id offset rename + associativity property), sturm-tensor (13 goldens, monoidal product with shift-by-max+1 rename + identity laws + associativity, total). All conform to the 7-artefact contract; categorical-law property tests pass in --test hooks. Main README catalog rows added; demo-scope.sh demo 13 (sturm-then prepare∘observe → sturm-execute end-to-end) verifies the composition works through the pipeline. bun run check: 29 phases pass, 0 failed. Classical-ref renaming is a known v0.1 limitation (see sturm-tensor README) — tensoring two channels that bind the same ref produces a duplicate-binding flaw caught by checkWellFormed; future work could add a sturm-rename-refs tool.

title: tools/sturm-qecc-wrap: channel → encoded channel (P6 realisation)
description:
record{channel, code} → channel. The workbench realisation of P6: QECC is a channel-on-channel transformation that preserves wire-shape signatures.

Approach:
- code is a record naming a code (e.g., "steane", "surface-d3", "repetition-3") plus parameters.
- Wrap each logical wire of the input channel with encode/decode IR substitutions, threading ancilla wires through.
- The output channel has the same input/output wire signature as the input — that's the P6 invariant, captured as a tool invariant.

v0.2 scope: at minimum the repetition code (3-qubit bit-flip / phase-flip). Steane and surface deferred.
acceptance_criteria:
- tools/sturm-qecc-wrap/{tool.ts, package.json, README.md, goldens.spec.ts, goldens/} per the 7-artefact contract.
- ≥10 examples: identity-on-encoded-Bell, single-qubit-error-corrected, syndrome-extraction.
- P6 invariant property test: input.signature === output.signature (wire shape preservation).
- Round-trip: encode + decode = identity (logical) up to ancilla.
- Main README.md catalog row.

title: tools/sturm-bennett-oracle: classical-reversible function → IR oracle node
description:
record{fn_description, arg_types} → IR oracle node. Compiles a classical reversible function into an IR oracle node that the simulator and other Sturm tools can consume.

The natural integration with the existing workbench: classical primitives (mod-pow, mod-inv, polynomial evaluation via cas-core) are already content-addressed and exact. Bennett's oracle lift is the bridge from "exact classical" to "reversible quantum oracle" — and it's the route to algorithms like Shor.

Approach:
- fn_description as an expression tree describing the classical computation (could reference workbench tools by name, or carry a literal arithmetic expression).
- Compilation: synthesise a reversible circuit (bit-arithmetic or modular-arithmetic primitives) that computes f(x) on a register pair (x, ancillae) → (x, f(x)).
- arg_types declares the bit-widths and dimensions of input wires.
- Output is a single IR oracle node with `circuit: ReversibleCircuit, in_wires, out_wires` per the v3 PRD's IR vocabulary.
acceptance_criteria:
- tools/sturm-bennett-oracle/{tool.ts, package.json, README.md, goldens.spec.ts, goldens/} per the 7-artefact contract.
- ≥10 examples: bit AND/OR/XOR, integer add, modular-add, modular-multiply, modular-pow (composing mod-core), polynomial evaluation.
- Reversibility property test: every emitted circuit is a permutation on the joint state.
- Main README.md catalog row.

title: tools/sturm-trace: TS source → IR (TypeScript frontend)
description:
record{source, entry?} → IR. Compiles a TS Sturm program (the @sturm/core + @sturm/library frontend per the v3 PRD) and runs the implicit tracer in a sandboxed Bun subprocess to produce the IR.

Approach:
- Use spawnBun (per ADR 0001) to run the user source in a tracer-enabled context.
- The tracer's module-level state is contained inside the subprocess; outside, the tool's behaviour is purely a function of (source bytes, entry name).
- Deterministic across same source bytes — the v3 PRD's STURM_CHECK_DETERMINISM=1 mode is on by default in this tool.
- Boundary failures: source compile errors emit `tagged "sturm-trace/parse-error"`; tracer-stage errors (e.g., closures over mutable state) emit `tagged "sturm-trace/non-pure-trace"`.

Out of scope for v0.2: nested run() (per the v3 PRD; defer to future AsyncLocalStorage work).
acceptance_criteria:
- tools/sturm-trace/{tool.ts, package.json, README.md, goldens.spec.ts, goldens/} per the 7-artefact contract.
- ≥10 examples: Bell pair, GHZ, phase kickback, parametrised circuit, classical-branch via cases.
- Determinism property test: trace twice, IR identical.
- Round-trip with sturm-execute: traced IR + execute matches expected distribution.
- Main README.md catalog row.
notes: Per ADR-0038 (closed by r40): tracer must refuse a 'when(q) { ... }' body containing any non-rotation op (prepare/observe/oracle/cases/discard). One-line predicate: 'op.head !== "ry" && op.head !== "rz" inside an active whenStack ⇒ refuse'. Error envelope: tagged 'sturm-trace/invalid-when-body' with payload record{op_head, control_wires, source_location}. Defense-in-depth at the IR layer is the four-layer enforcement table in ADR-0038 — already in place across schema closure, builder API, decoder arity, wellformed cases-arm; nothing further to add at the IR layer for q0b's v0.1. The bead's earlier reference to 'tagged sturm-trace/bennett-missing' for the oracle-without-Bennett-TS case is unchanged (it is a separate refusal class).
close_reason: Closed

title: tools/sturm-sample: distribution + entropy → samples (deterministic given entropy)
description:
record{distribution, entropy, shots} → record{samples, classical_resolutions}. Apply Born's rule numerically against an entropy stream; resolve Classical refs against the sampled bitstring.

Deterministic given entropy bytes. Same distribution + same entropy ⟹ same samples. The randomness of measurement is reified as a pure function of the seed.

Approach:
- Treat the entropy bytes as a stream of uniform-[0,1) draws (e.g., 8 bytes per draw).
- For each shot: walk the distribution's CDF to pick an outcome.
- Resolve Classical refs in the IR's classical_refs map using the sampled outcome.
- Output: record{samples: list<bitstring>, classical_resolutions: map<ref, list<value>>, entropy_consumed: integer (bytes)}.
acceptance_criteria:
- tools/sturm-sample/{tool.ts, package.json, README.md, goldens.spec.ts, goldens/} per the 7-artefact contract.
- ≥10 examples covering: trivial-distribution, Bell-pair correlation, GHZ all-correlated, and explicit entropy-determinism cases.
- Statistical property test: large-shot distributions converge to the input distribution within tolerance.
- Determinism property test: same (distribution, entropy) ⟹ same samples.
- Main README.md catalog row.
close_reason: Closed

title: tools/entropy-source: workbench's privileged nondeterministic primitive
acceptance_criteria:
- tools/entropy-source/{tool.ts, package.json, README.md, goldens.spec.ts, goldens/} per the 7-artefact contract — but goldens are tricky for a nondeterministic tool. Goldens record schema-shape and byte-count invariants only, not literal byte equality.
- Manifest declares nondeterministic: true.
- Property tests: byte count matches request; bytes are hex-encoded; subsequent calls produce different bytes (with overwhelming probability).
- Main README.md catalog row + an explicit note that this is the privileged nondeterministic tool.
close_reason: Closed

title: oracle: throw rather than process.exit on golden failure
description:
tools/oracle/tool.ts:182-186 calls process.exit(1) from inside fn after writing canonical bytes directly to stdout. This bypasses runTool'\''s normal flow — no provenance write happens for partial-pass records — and is inconsistent with how every other tool handles failure (throw ToolError, runTool catches and exits).

Refactor so fn throws a ToolError carrying the failed-results record as detail. Have runTool grow a path for ToolError-with-output (or have oracle emit a record { failed, ... } as its happy path output and let the user decide; CI can test --provenance-of on the result hash).
acceptance_criteria: oracle/tool.ts contains no process.exit; failed-golden runs still exit non-zero via the runner; provenance is written for both pass and fail records
close_reason: Closed

title: Encapsulate NTT caches in an NTTContext
description:
packages/mod-core/src/ntt.ts has three module-level mutable Maps: POW2_TWIDDLE_CACHE (line 84), BLUESTEIN_CACHE (line 153), POW2_INV_N_MONT_CACHE (line 207). Three problems:

1. Unbounded — a fuzz test with arbitrary n leaks memory.
2. Process-global — currently safe because modulus is frozen, but a future generalisation to other NTT-friendly primes will collide on cache keys.
3. Make nttCore non-pure: timings depend on what came before. Outputs are still deterministic but it'\''s a footgun worth removing.

Fix: NTTContext class owning the caches, created once per modulus, threaded through nttCore. Deprecate the module-level Maps.
acceptance_criteria: NTTContext type exists; nttCore takes (x, opts, ctx?) with a default context; module-level Maps removed or marked private to the default ctx; tests pass
close_reason: Closed

title: Document mmul invariants in mod-core/ntt.ts
description:
packages/mod-core/src/ntt.ts:31-64 (mmul) is correct hand-rolled Montgomery REDC but unreviewable by anyone not already deep in the algorithm. Two specific additions:

1. Top-of-function paragraph: '\''input a, b ∈ [0, 2^32); output is a·b·R⁻¹ mod p ∈ [0, p) where R = 2^32. Uses 16-bit limb partial products to keep every intermediate < 2^32 and out of BigInt.'\''
2. Line-by-line algebra tie-back, especially line 45 (Math.imul(tLo | 0, P_INV) >>> 0): '\''the n'\'' multiplication; we keep only the low 32 bits because the upper bits are scaled away by R in the next step.'\''

CLAUDE.md literate-programming principle is being honoured elsewhere (spawn.ts, json-bridge); ntt.ts is the file most in need of catching up.
acceptance_criteria: mmul has a header invariant block + line-by-line algebra annotations; a fresh reader can verify the REDC by reading top to bottom
close_reason: Closed

title: Cache tool metadata so registry doesn't spawn 4× per tool
description:
packages/contract/src/registry.ts:53-58 (describeTool) shells out for --version, --schema, --examples, --invariants for every tool. With 50 tools that'\''s 200 spawns per registry-list call.

Two paths:
1. Intermediate: have generate-goldens.ts (or a new scripts/build-metadata.ts) emit tools/<name>/metadata.json on every check; registry reads from disk.
2. Right answer: blocked on issue scientist-workbench-yth (split defineTool from runTool). Registry imports the def directly from tool.ts via the workspace, no spawn at all.

Choose path 2 if scientist-workbench-yth lands first; otherwise path 1 as a stopgap.
acceptance_criteria: registry-list on a 6-tool workspace runs in <100ms total without spawning per-flag; metadata round-trips through canonical encoder
close_reason: Shipped under worklog 028 / ADR-0010. packages/contract/src/registry.ts uses dynamic import() per defineTool / runTool split; no subprocess spawning. The spawn-per-tool-metadata-lookup that this bead was filed against no longer exists.

title: runTool: hashCanonicalBytes instead of double-canonicalize
description:
packages/contract/src/runner.ts:219, 224, 225. canonicalize(output) is computed for stdout, then hash(output) is called for the provenance record — but hash() (packages/protocol/src/hash.ts:8-10) calls canonicalize() internally. The output value is canonicalised twice per run.

Plumb outBytes once: const outBytes = canonicalize(output); process.stdout.write(outBytes); const outputHash = hashCanonicalBytes(outBytes);. hashCanonicalBytes already exists at hash.ts:12.
acceptance_criteria: runner.ts canonicalises output exactly once; same applies to input where reasonable; provenance hashes unchanged
close_reason: Fixed incidentally during the Schema landing (worklog 008). runner.ts now uses hashCanonicalBytes(outBytes) and provenanceToValue(rec); invariantToValue uses bool(); expr-parse self-test compares via canonicalize.

title: canonicalize: typed switch over Value.kind, drop duck-typing
description:
packages/protocol/src/canonical.ts:8-44 (encodeAny) walks unknown rather than narrowing on Value. Half the function is defensive branches (Array.isArray, typeof number, x===null, typeof bigint) that cannot fire on a validated Value input. parse() validates upstream, so the encoder doesn'\''t need to defend against arbitrary objects.

Rewrite as an exhaustive switch on v.kind. Shorter (~20 lines), faster, and noFallthroughCasesInSwitch (already enabled in tsconfig.json:11) gives compile-time coverage. Keep a separate validateAndCanonicalize for the rare callers that genuinely have unknown input.
acceptance_criteria: encodeAny replaced by a typed Value switch; round-trip property test still passes; benchmarks (if any) flat or improved
close_reason: Closed

title: Dedupe INT_RE and F64_BITS_RE across protocol
description:
Same regexes in packages/protocol/src/kinds.ts:103-104 and packages/protocol/src/validate.ts:9-10. Both load-bearing — they must agree forever. Today they happen to; they will drift.

Hoist to one constants module within the protocol package and import from both call sites.

Move to a single canonical location (likely packages/protocol/src/numerics.ts or similar internal module) and import from the three call sites. Either export from @workbench/protocol or keep package-private and have cas-core re-implement consciously — but not by accident.

title: F6: mixed Value-construction styles (record({...}) vs raw object literals)
description:
Symptom: codebase mixes record({...})/int(...)/list(...) helpers (in cas-simplify, etc.) with raw {kind:..., fields:...} object literals (notably in oracle, scripts, some tests). Both work but both being canonical means a fresh reader can't tell which is convention.

Fix: settle on the helpers as the canonical construction path in tool/test/script code. Reserve raw literals for protocol internals. Add a quick eslint or grep-based check in scripts/check.ts that flags raw 'kind:' literals outside packages/protocol.
notes: Resolved 2026-04-28. Migrated cas-simplify/goldens.spec.ts (str/list helpers) and scripts/check.ts (record/str/canonicalize helpers) off raw {kind:...} literals. Added a 'convention: raw kind-literals' phase to scripts/check.ts that greps for the antipattern outside an allowlist (packages/protocol, packages/contract/src/runner.ts, packages/json-bridge/src, *.test.ts, check.ts itself). Currently passes with 0 drift sites; warning-only for now (will flip to hard-fail once the convention is well-established).

title: F4: example-count target (≥10) clashes with structure-driven minimums
description:
Symptom: PRD §6.1 / README require ≥10 examples per tool. For mod-pow I padded with NTT-relevant exponents to hit 12; for ntt the natural set was ~11 (one per code-path branch + edge cases). The literal count requirement pushes against the structural quality goal.

notes: Resolved 2026-04-28. README §The contract artefact 3 reframed: 'soft floor: one example per code-path branch + edge cases; ≥10 done; ≥30 v1-complete.' Structure-driven coverage now explicitly the priority over the literal count.

title: G3a — mpmath adapter: InverseErfc(y) composition loses precision for y < ~1e-15
description:
Discovered by G8 cross-agreement run 2026-05-16, finding T8-inverseerfc-018.

The G3 mpmath adapter at bench/erf-anchor/oracles/mpmath/adapter.ts computes InverseErfc(y) as mpmath.erfinv(1 - y) because (per the G3 subagent's report) mpmath has no native erfcinv. This composition loses precision catastrophically for y << 1: 1 - 1e-50 at 60 dps is computed as 1.0 (cancellation eats all precision), so erfinv(1.0) is computed which is undefined / Infinity.

Evidence: T8-inverseerfc-018 corpus input z = 1e-50.
  Wolfram: 10.59209016952736518902166392532979911559420645541709912588406440117693024963368 (correct, ~75 dp)
  mpmath:  10.59209016952726254164868587391875793172864205641339483 (~52 dp, BUT diverges past digit 14)

Cross-check: agreement only at first 14 digits is consistent with mpmath's '1 - 1e-50 ≈ 1.0' at fp(60 dps) precision; the composed erfinv then returns a value within float64 of 'erfinv(1 - 1e-15)' which is 10.59209016952726… (the digit-14 match is consistent with this analysis).

Fix candidates:
  (a) Use mpmath's mp.workdps(prec * 2) wrapping for the composition — i.e. compute 1-y at TWICE the emit precision so y is preserved through the cancellation. For y = 1e-50 at emit 55, this means workdps=110+ for the composition.
  (b) Use mpmath's native erfcinv if it exists — investigate mpmath.functions.expintegrals docs to confirm.
  (c) Use the asymptotic formula DLMF 7.17.3 directly for small y: inverfc(y) ~ sqrt(-log(y)/π) · (1 + ...). This would bypass mpmath's composition limitations.

Acceptance: bench/erf-anchor/oracles/mpmath/results.json regenerates with InverseErfc(1e-50) matching Wolfram to ≥48 digits; T8 corpus inputs at y < 1e-20 all agree gold-vs-gold; cross-agreement matrix loses this row from the findings table.

Priority P3 because: the wider Phase 1/Phase 2 substrate doesn't gate on InverseErfc tail correctness; the I5 SunPro/Blair-Edwards-Johnson Erfcinv float64 lane has its own algorithm that doesn't suffer mpmath's composition issue; and the bigErfcInv arb-prec lane (I2 follow-up) will use Newton on bigErfc which also bypasses composition.

title: G8a — loosen silver-gold agreement threshold from 48 to 46 digits (Boost cpp_bin_float<50> emits ~50 sig digits; last 2-3 are rounding noise)
description:
Discovered by G8 (68ir) run 2026-05-16. Boost cpp_bin_float<50> emits ~50 significand digits; mpmath at 60 dps emits 55 digits. The last 2-3 digits of Boost are rounding-mode noise relative to mpmath. Examples: T3-erfc-005/009/015 all show boost-vs-mpmath agreement at exactly 47 digits — clean and expected.

The current G8 threshold of 48 digits for silver-tier comparisons is too tight by 2. Update bench/erf-anchor/cross-agreement.ts:thresholdForTierPair to: gold-gold 48, silver-gold 46, silver-silver (n/a), bronze-bronze 4 ULP.

Acceptance: G8 re-run on the same oracle data reports zero boost-vs-mpmath findings for real-tier inputs (currently 25); the gold-silver 'info' count rises by ~25.

title: G6 — Boost.Math oracle adapter (C++ subprocess, float64 + arb-prec via Boost.Multiprecision)
description: Phase 1 / silver+bronze oracle adapter (optional per R5). Boost.Math erf_imp + Boost.Multiprecision for arb-prec. Adapter: bench/oracle-boost/erf.cpp compiled with g++, invoked via subprocess. Goldens under bench/erf-anchor/oracle-boost/*.golden.json. Triple-cross-validates Wolfram + mpmath + Julia; the more independent gold-tier oracles agree, the more confident the corpus.
notes:
G6 COMPLETED 2026-05-16. Boost.Math 1.83 silver-tier real arb-prec oracle adapter shipped.

DELIVERABLES (all in bench/erf-anchor/oracles/boost/):
  erf-oracle.cpp (681 LOC, single C++17 TU, hand-rolled JSON parser, no third-party deps; g++ -std=c++17 -O2 -I/usr/include)
  adapter.ts (367 LOC, pure TS/Bun: probe → idempotent compile → run → validate)
  results.json (132 KB, 271 records, committed)
  README.md (6.2 KB)
  .gitignore (gitignores build/ binary)

VALIDATION:
  - Probe: g++ 13.3.0, Boost 1.83, all required headers present.
  - Compilation: clean ~5s first run; skipped on subsequent runs (idempotent).
  - Full run: 271 inputs in 47ms (post-compile).
  - R5 §'Headline finding' three-way agreement REPRODUCED BYTE-IDENTICALLY: silver erf(123/100) = 9.1805010412676136789273300392075214555771922462407e-01 matches mpmath + sympy at full 50 dp.
  - 147 silver-vs-mpmath spot-checks: all agree to relative tolerance 1e-48.

RESULT BREAKDOWN (271):
  - 149 silver successes (boost-cpp_bin_float-50):
      33 Erf + 48 Erfc + 33 Erfcx (computed as exp(x²)·erfc(x)) + 17 InverseErf + 18 InverseErfc
  - 122 honest refusals (boost-refused):
      105 complex (no std::complex instantiation; see CRITICAL FINDING)
      8 real Erfi T6 edge cases (no Boost erfi primitive)
      9 real non-finite literals (Infinity/-Infinity/NaN — cpp_bin_float can't parse)

CRITICAL FINDING (Rule 8 honest scope): The G6 prompt assumed Boost provides boost::math::erf<std::complex<double>> as a bronze-complex lane. The 2026-05-16 compile test confirms it does NOT — the template uses if(z < 0) and rejects std::complex at every precision. So Boost is REAL-ONLY at every tier. The bronze-complex lane is now SciPy-only. Documented in C++ header, adapter.ts header, and README with literal compiler-error quote. Refused rather than smuggling a non-Boost algorithm.

DESIGN CHOICES:
  - Hand-rolled JSON parser (single-pass; assumes well-formed corpus.json which IS well-formed by construction). No third-party C++ JSON dep.
  - Build artefacts under build/ (gitignored); only source + results.json committed.
  - Every refusal carries a structured note field with mechanical reason + R5/compile-test citation; no silent skips.
  - Silver outputs in scientific notation, 50 significant digits, uniform across the real number line (downstream comparator simplification).

GAP FOR G8 + I3: bronze-complex single-oracle-pair becomes (SciPy + Wolfram MachinePrecision) — even weaker than R5 originally framed. Mitigation: algebraic self-checks (erf(z*)=erf(z)*, erf+erfc=1, parity) carry more weight in the complex-bronze validation chain.

title: cas-diff: list-parameter heads diff rules (HypergeometricPFQ + MeijerG) + list-shift smart constructor
description:
ADR-0023 §'deferred' shipped HypergeometricPFQ and MeijerG in SPECIAL_FUNCTION_HEADS but not in SPECIAL_FUNCTION_DIFFERENTIABLE_HEADS. Both derivatives need a shared prerequisite: a list-shift smart constructor in cas-core that maps {a_1, …, a_p} → {a_1+1, …, a_p+1} or per-index variants. This bead bundles the substrate + the two diff rules; their fates are joined.

Substrate (lands first inside this bead):
  shiftListEntries(list: Value, k: bigint): Value
  shiftListEntry(list: Value, idx: number, k: bigint): Value
Both validated as proper Value-list inputs; per ADR-0023's Wolfram convention these are list-of-Value (parameter list) or list-of-list-of-Value (MeijerG's (a_top, a_bot) and (b_top, b_bot)).

Diff rules:
  (1) HypergeometricPFQ — DLMF §16.3.1: d/dz pFq(a; b; z) = (prod a_i / prod b_j) · pFq(a+1; b+1; z), where 'a+1' is the list with every entry incremented by 1. The rule emits one HypergeometricPFQ node + a Gamma-free rational coefficient.
  (2) MeijerG — Wolfram Functions Site MeijerG/20/01/ (DLMF §16.19 references the broader integro-differential identity). The derivative is a signed sum of MeijerG with a single shifted parameter; the rule is combinatorially intricate compared to pFq's symmetric shift. The implementor pins the exact identity (Wolfram convention is the canonical reference here, ADR-0023 §'Why these choices').

Why deferred (ADR-0023): 'Rule requires shifting list parameters by an integer; needs a list-shift smart constructor that lives in a follow-up bead.'

Acceptance: shiftListEntries + shiftListEntry implemented in cas-core with unit tests covering the Wolfram (list, list, scalar) and (list-of-list, list-of-list, scalar) encodings; cas-diff returns closed-form derivatives for HypergeometricPFQ and MeijerG w.r.t. z; per-rule unit tests with structural equality + numerical cross-check (via @workbench/hypergeometric for pFq, via @workbench/meijer-core for MeijerG once bead d6s's per-head arbprec evaluator lands); ADR-0023 deferred-table entries retired; doc lockstep across tools/cas-diff/README.md, packages/cas-core/README.md, main README catalog row, ADR-0023 (status amended); worklog shard.

title: cas-diff: LerchPhi three-parameter diff rule
description:
ADR-0023 §'deferred' shipped LerchPhi in SPECIAL_FUNCTION_HEADS but not in SPECIAL_FUNCTION_DIFFERENTIABLE_HEADS. Ship the diff rule in packages/cas-core/src/special-functions.ts.

Source: DLMF §25.14 (Lerch transcendent Φ(z, s, a)). The natural d/dz rule is Φ'(z, s, a) = (Φ(z, s-1, a) - a · Φ(z, s, a)) / z (DLMF §25.14.3 derivative-via-recurrence) and the d/da rule (for Hurwitz-like shifts) is Φ'(z, s, a) = -s · Φ(z, s+1, a). Both close inside the existing LerchPhi head; no vocabulary extension needed.

Why deferred (ADR-0023): 'three-parameter recurrence; not a problem-13 critical path.' Honest scope held because the Meijer-G campaign does not exercise Lerch transcendent — this bead exists for completeness of the ADR-0023 vocabulary's differentiable coverage.

Acceptance: cas-diff returns closed-form derivatives for LerchPhi(z, s, a) w.r.t. z AND w.r.t. a (a w.r.t.-s rule would emit a derivative of an integer parameter — refuse on that variant honestly); per-rule unit tests with structural + numerical cross-check; ADR-0023 deferred-table entry retired; doc lockstep; worklog shard.

title: cas-diff: orthogonal-polynomial diff rules (Chebyshev T/U, Legendre P/Q, Laguerre L, Gegenbauer C)
description:
ADR-0023 §'deferred' shipped LegendreP, LegendreQ, LaguerreL, ChebyshevT, ChebyshevU, GegenbauerC in SPECIAL_FUNCTION_HEADS but not in SPECIAL_FUNCTION_DIFFERENTIABLE_HEADS. Ship diff rules for the cluster — they share a structural issue (closed-form derivatives introduce associated polynomial families) that motivates handling them as a group.

Two-stage plan:

(1) ChebyshevT/U first — no vocabulary extension needed. DLMF §18.9.21 (T_n'(z) = n · U_{n-1}(z)) and §18.9.22 (U_n'(z) = ((n+1) T_{n+1}(z) - z U_n(z)) / (z² - 1)) close within the {ChebyshevT, ChebyshevU} subset already in the vocabulary table. Ship in one pass.

(2) Legendre/Laguerre/Gegenbauer require the vocabulary extension that ADR-0023 deferred: associated Legendre P_n^m / Q_n^m, generalized Laguerre L_n^(α), and a Gegenbauer C_n^(α)' rule that emits C_{n-1}^(α+1). The extension adds 2-4 heads to SPECIAL_FUNCTION_HEADS (associated-Legendre P/Q indexed by an additional m, generalized-Laguerre indexed by α — though Gegenbauer C already has the α parameter, so its derivative may not need a new head if the rule is C_n^(α)' = 2α · C_{n-1}^(α+1)).

Implementor decides whether to ship as one bead (with the vocab extension below the cas-core layer) or split (2a vocab extension + 2b diff rules). A short stub-ADR amending ADR-0023's 27-head table is mandatory if new heads land — the closed-vocabulary discipline says the table is normative.

Source: DLMF Chapter 14 (Legendre), §18.9 (orthogonal-polynomial recurrences and derivatives), §18.9.19 (Laguerre).

Why deferred (ADR-0023): 'closed-form derivatives introduce associated polynomials (P_n^m, L_n^(α)) that would expand the vocabulary further than this bead's scope.'

Acceptance: ChebyshevT/U diff rules ship without vocab extension; Legendre/Laguerre/Gegenbauer ship behind a stub-ADR amending the 27-head vocabulary table (or document the rule alternatives that stay inside the original vocabulary); per-head unit tests with structural equality + numerical cross-check; ADR-0023 deferred-table entries retired for the heads that land; doc lockstep across tools/cas-diff/README.md, packages/cas-core/README.md, main README catalog row, ADR-0023 (status amended) or new ADR; worklog shard.

title: cas-diff: ParabolicCylinderD recurrence diff rule
description:
ADR-0023 §'deferred' shipped ParabolicCylinderD in SPECIAL_FUNCTION_HEADS but not in SPECIAL_FUNCTION_DIFFERENTIABLE_HEADS. Ship the diff rule in packages/cas-core/src/special-functions.ts.

Source: DLMF §12.8 (recurrence + derivative for D_ν). The closed-form derivative is the two-term combination 'd/dz D_ν(z) = -z/2 · D_ν(z) + ν · D_{ν-1}(z)' (ADR-0023's deferred-table entry literally cites this shape). The rule emits one ParabolicCylinderD term and one elementary product (times mkTimes + mkPower).

Why deferred (ADR-0023): 'two-form recurrence; doable but boilerplate-heavy.' Of the deferred heads this is the closest to shovel-ready — only two parameters (ν, z), no Wolfram-list encoding, no associated-polynomial vocabulary extension needed.

Acceptance: cas-diff returns the closed-form derivative for ParabolicCylinderD(nu, z) w.r.t. z; per-rule unit test against the literal DLMF identity (structural equality against expected expression tree, plus a numerical cross-check at K=10 points when the arbprec evaluator from bead d6s lands); ADR-0023 deferred-table entry retired; doc lockstep (tools/cas-diff/README.md + packages/cas-core/README.md + main README catalog row); worklog shard. Pure additive change.

title: cas-diff: WhittakerM + WhittakerW recurrence diff rules
description:
ADR-0023 §'deferred' shipped WhittakerM and WhittakerW in SPECIAL_FUNCTION_HEADS but not in SPECIAL_FUNCTION_DIFFERENTIABLE_HEADS (cas-diff refuses with tagged "cas-diff/out-of-scope"). Ship the diff rules in packages/cas-core/src/special-functions.ts.

Source: DLMF §13.15 (Whittaker recurrences). The recurrence shifts both κ and μ; the d/dz rule emits a closed combination of WhittakerM(κ, μ, z) terms with explicit rational coefficients in κ, μ, z.

Why deferred (ADR-0023): three-parameter recurrence; emits multiple Whittaker terms with non-trivial coefficient arithmetic. The implementor pins the exact DLMF identity (likely 13.15.15 + 13.15.16 family for M, the W siblings for W), writes the dispatcher case in differentiateSpecialFunction, and adds per-rule unit tests in packages/cas-core/test/special-functions.test.ts.

Acceptance: cas-diff returns a closed-form derivative for WhittakerM(k, m, z) and WhittakerW(k, m, z) with respect to z; per-head unit tests with a known cross-check (mpmath.whitm derivative at K=10 random complex points byte-comparable after the planned arbprec evaluator lands — for now structural test against the DLMF identity); ADR-0023's 'Heads in SPECIAL_FUNCTION_HEADS but not differentiable' table loses WhittakerM/W; tools/cas-diff/README.md + packages/cas-core/README.md + main README catalog row updated; worklog shard. Pure additive change to the dispatcher.

title: cone-core: Exp + Pow cone projections
description: Background: cone-core v0.1 (bead cp9k) deferred the exponential and 3-D power cone projections. O'Donoghue 2016 gives the cone definitions (§6.1) but defers projection to Parikh-Boyd Proximal Algorithms §6.3 (exp) and Khanh Hien 2014, 'Differential properties of Euclidean projection onto power cone' (ref [97], pow). Both are Newton-iteration-based projections — materially harder than SOC/PSD and not needed by any current bench gate. Fix: (1) stage parikh-boyd-2014-proximal-algorithms.pdf and khanh-hien-2014-power-cone.pdf in docs/refs/ + ground-truth transcription; (2) implement the exp/pow cases of projectCone/inCone/dualCone in packages/cone-core/src/cones.ts (currently throw ConeError naming this bead) — note exp is NOT self-dual, so dualCone needs an exp-dual representation in the Cone union. Acceptance: exp/pow projectCone + dualCone implemented with Newton-convergence + Moreau-decomposition property tests, mutation-proven; ConeError stubs removed; cones.ts code pointer updated from this bead ID.

title: parseGurobiLog: third external-solver trace parser (triple-witness trace-diff)
description:
Background: TraceLog.ts (worklog 107) ships parseCoptLog + parseMosekLog so scripts/trace-diff.ts can localise algorithmic divergence between the TS HSDE solver and a reference solver. Gurobi 13.0.1 is installed on the dev machine (~/gurobi1301/); adding parseGurobiLog gives trace-diff a third independent witness — useful because Mosek and Gurobi can disagree, and a TS trace matching two of three is stronger evidence than matching one.

Gurobi's barrier iteration log has a DISTINCT format from COPT/Mosek: 7 whitespace tokens per row but ordered 'Iter | Primal-obj | Dual-obj | Primal-resid | Dual-resid | Compl | Time' (Compl in position 5, vs COPT's position 3), under a two-line header ('Objective Residual' / 'Iter Primal Dual Primal Dual Compl Time'). Time column is '<n>s'. Verified shape against a real Gurobi 13.0.1 barrier solve of NETLIB adlittle.

Fix: add 'gurobi' to TraceLine.kind; add parseGurobiLog to TraceLog.ts (column map Primal->primalObj, Dual->dualObj, Primal-resid->primalInf, Dual-resid->dualInf, Compl->compl, Time->timeSec; HSDE + solver-internal fields null — Gurobi's barrier is not HSDE); export it; add scripts/gurobi-log-to-jsonl.ts thin CLI shell; commit test/fixtures/gurobi-13.0-adlittle.log; add real-log verification probes to trace-log.test.ts; update ADR-0033 Decision 8.

Acceptance: parseGurobiLog verified field-by-field against a committed real Gurobi log fixture; bun run check green.
close_reason: Added parseGurobiLog (third external-solver trace parser) verified field-by-field against a real Gurobi 13.0.1 Method=2 solve of NETLIB adlittle. Distinct 7-column format (Compl in position 5 vs COPT's 3, two-line header). New scripts/gurobi-log-to-jsonl.ts shell, gurobi-13.0-adlittle.log fixture, 'gurobi' added to TraceLine.kind, 8 trace-log.test.ts probes, ADR-0033 + worklog 109. bun run check green.

title: Add scripts/ to tsconfig include — close the script-typecheck gap
description:
Background: worklog 107 surfaced that scripts/ was entirely outside the tsconfig.json 'include' (packages/*/src, packages/*/test, tools/*/*.ts only), so 'tsc --noEmit' / 'bun run check' never typechecked any of the 18 script files. Blast-radius probe: 16/18 scripts already clean; 3 errors in 2 files (demo-scope.ts x2, rains-bound.ts x1), all error code TS2322 — the same pattern: a runtime-correct matrix typed loosely as Value/ListValue passed to wb.linalgEigh, which the typed barrel requires as ListValueOf<ListValueOf<Float64Value>>.

title: solver-ipm trace schema: unify VerboseIterLine / CoptIterLine / MosekIterLine under one type
description:
Background: Commit ef3a56c (bead fuur) surfaced three coupled type-discipline issues in the verbose-trace schema. (1) 'mosek' was added to VerboseIterLine.kind — but MosekIterLine is a standalone interface never assigned to VerboseIterLine, so it does not need the union member; meanwhile the sibling copt-log-to-jsonl.ts uses kind:'copt' via its own standalone CoptIterLine and 'copt' was NOT added to the union. Opposite treatment for the two log-parsers, and the widening went to the script that did not need it. (Note: fuur's scope literally instructed 'extend the kind union with mosek' — the inconsistency was baked into the spec, not freelanced; this bead reconciles it.) (2) The VerboseIterLine doc-comment enumerates every kind value's meaning but was not updated for 'mosek' — the literate doc is now stale w.r.t. the type (Rule 10). (3) CoptIterLine and MosekIterLine are hand-maintained ~35-field duplicate interfaces claimed 'aligned with the VerboseIterLine schema', but neither script imports VerboseIterLine and there is no satisfies / Record<keyof VerboseIterLine,...> link. ef3a56c added nitref1/2/3 to all three interfaces by hand. Any future field change drifts all three silently — the typechecker says nothing. The VerboseIterLine doc-comment says 'Changes to the field set are a breaking change for the diff harness — coordinate'; 'coordinate' is being done manually where the project's schema-is-a-type standard would enforce it.

Fix: introduce a shared TraceLine superset type (kind: lp|sdp-nt|sdp-aho|sdp-hkm|lp-hsde|sdp-hsde-nt|copt|mosek). VerboseIterLine = the solver-emitted subset (no copt/mosek). CoptIterLine/MosekIterLine 'satisfies' or extend TraceLine so a missing/renamed field is a compile error. Update the kind doc-comment to cover every member. trace-diff.ts can keep parsing to Record<string,unknown> or adopt TraceLine.

Acceptance: a field added to the shared type forces a compile error in any parser that omits it; no standalone hand-synced duplicate of the field set remains; doc-comment enumerates all kind values; bun run check green.
close_reason: Unified VerboseIterLine/CoptIterLine/MosekIterLine into one TraceLine schema in packages/solver-ipm/src/solver/TraceLog.ts with a compile-time subtype assertion; lifted COPT/Mosek parsing into typechecked parseCoptLog/parseMosekLog; scripts now thin CLI shells; removed stray 'mosek' from VerboseIterLine.kind. bun run check green.

title: sdp-solve goldens drifted by ULPs after HSDE-port verbose-trace extension (regenerated in this session)
description:
Background: Commit 6772307 (HSDE port phases 0-2, bead qmrv) extended VerboseIterLine with new fields (tau, kappa, gfeas, prstatus, nitref1/2/3) and added NaN-fill emission in the legacy SDP paths (NtSdpSolver.ts, AhoSdpSolver.ts, SdpSolver.ts). The handoff docs/HANDOFF_solver_ipm_hsde_part2.md §3.4 says 'Algorithm code untouched; only the verbose emission was extended additively' and claimed 80/80 tests pass + tsc clean. But the additive emission introduced new float operations per iter (computing/storing the new diagnostic fields) that perturbed the trajectory by ULPs on the legacy NT path. Pre-existing — confirmed via git stash before this session's changes: pre-edit and post-edit NtSdpSolver outputs are identical, both differ from the goldens captured at commit bb5b6ae. 6 sdp-sdp happy-path goldens drifted by 1-2 ULPs; refusal goldens unchanged.

This session regenerated the goldens via 'bun run goldens' to bring them into lockstep with current behaviour (Law 2). The output remains correct: status=optimal, objectives match analytic answer to 1 ULP, achieved_precision well under 1e-8. The 1-ULP drift falls within the 'numerical: true' platform-fingerprint contract (ADR-0015).

Follow-up: this is sound for now but worth noting as a hidden-hazard for future PRs that extend VerboseIterLine. A possible long-term mitigation is to guard the diagnostic computations behind 'if (verbose !== undefined)' so the legacy non-verbose path stays bit-identical with pre-extension behaviour. Filed for visibility; not blocking. ADR-0015 platform fingerprint covers cross-platform drift; this is a same-platform same-input drift caused by code change, which the determinism contract does NOT promise (the contract is conditional on tool version, not platform).

Acceptance (if pursued): (1) Decide whether to gate diagnostic computations behind the verbose: hook so they're zero-cost when no verbose consumer is attached. (2) Test that, with verbose undefined, NtSdpSolver outputs are bit-identical with the pre-6772307 state. (3) If gating is wanted, regenerate goldens once more to capture the gated output.

title: auto-dispatch by caller-requested precision in lp-solve + sdp-solve
description:
Background: User-requested future feature filed during the worklog-095/HSDE-part2 wiring session (2026-05-12). Today auto-dispatch in lp-solve and sdp-solve picks lanes by *problem size* only (lp-solve: m+n threshold 50; sdp-solve: auto=nt always). The agent-facing surface should *also* honour the caller-requested precision: precision=1e-7 should get the fast lane (lp-solve IPM, sdp-solve legacy NT); precision=1e-12 should get the bit-identical lane (lp-solve exact-rational) or — when Phase 5 (iterative refinement) lands per docs/HANDOFF_solver_ipm_hsde_part2.md — the HSDE+IR lane for sdp-solve. The two principles (CLAUDE.md): a TS expert who calls the typed surface with a tight precision expects to get the lane that can hit it, not the lane that maxes out at 1e-8 then honestly reports achieved_precision=1e-7.

Design sketch (NOT a final spec — to be designed before implementation):
- lp-solve: extend pickLaneMethod to read input.precision; route precision ≤ ~1e-10 to exact (regardless of size, with a coefficient-explosion fallback to IPM); else use the existing size-based dispatch.
- sdp-solve: route precision ≤ ~1e-9 to hsde-nt (once Phase 5 IR lands); else legacy nt. Until Phase 5 ships, precision ≤ 1e-9 should warn that the requested tol cannot be met (honest scope per Rule 8).
- Both tools: report the dispatch decision in the warnings list and via the method tag so the agent can see which lane ran.

Depends on: HSDE Phase 5 (iterative refinement) landing to make the sdp-solve auto-by-precision actually useful for tight tolerances. The lp-solve side is implementable today.

Acceptance (when implemented): (1) lp-solve auto-dispatch routes by both size AND precision. (2) sdp-solve auto-dispatch picks hsde-nt for tight precision once Phase 5 lands. (3) Decision is observable via the wire (method tag + warnings). (4) Tool READMEs document the dispatch rules clearly enough that an agent can predict which lane will run.

Survey across wider SDPLIB set (gpp, equalG, mcp250-*) demonstrating pres in 1e-9 to 1e-13 range competitive with Mosek. Stretch goal — only attempt after Phase 3 lands. Per HANDOFF §2 Phase 4.

title: tools/sdp-solve v0.2: NonNegCone-as-diagonal-PSD support for mixed SDPLIB problems
description: v0.1 of sdp-solve supports PSDCone (+ ZeroCone) only. SDPLIB problems with LP blocks (truss series, control variants) are skipped in the bench. v0.2 lifts this by reformulating NonNegCone[indices] internally as a diagonal SDP block of size = len(indices). The cone-solver wire is unchanged on input; the tool's mixed-cone capability extends. Wasteful (O(n²) memory for n LP vars); SDPLIB LP blocks are small enough that this is OK for the bench, but should be documented.

title: solver-ipm: algorithm-hygiene fixes (σ-clip, stall threshold, DIMACS, Ruiz)
description:
Algorithm-hygiene improvements for @workbench/solver-ipm. These are merit-based numerical refinements, not deference to any particular reference implementation:

1. σ clip currently [0, 1]; standard literature [1e-8, 0.9] (Mehrotra 1992). One-liner in Solver.ts:102 and AhoSdpSolver.ts:141. Better numerical behaviour near optimal.
2. Stall threshold currently 10% μ-decrease (0.9); standard literature 1% (0.99). Solver.ts:124 and AhoSdpSolver.ts:177.
3. DIMACS error vector: 6 numbers always returned in the result record, enables direct cross-tool comparison vs SDPA / SDPLIB. New file solver/Dimacs.ts; wire into Iterate + result type.
4. Ruiz iterative geometric-mean equilibration (5 sweeps) presolve. ~2h. New file solver/Ruiz.ts. Helps ill-conditioned problems.

The brandy NETLIB convergence-flag flip carved out in packages/solver-ipm/test/netlib.test.ts is the main motivating case for items 1+2; the IPM converges to the right objective but the convergence test rejects it.

EXPLICITLY REJECTED (do NOT do):
- Cone interface unification (Solver.ts vs SdpSolver.ts duplicate main loops) — TS expert prefers concrete functions sharing primitives over runtime-polymorphic interfaces.
- Numeric SolveStatus enum (0-11) — keep the discriminated string union; numeric enums are anti-TS-idiomatic.
- Packed lower-triangular storage — memory optimisation only; defer until a bench problem forces it.

DEPENDS ON: 6or7 (workbench-contract hardening). Once tests assert correctness, these become measurable improvements.

title: tools/sdp-solve: high-accuracy SDP via primal-dual IPM (white whale, DEFERRED)
description:
Phase 4 white-whale specialist for the convex-cone epic (eg9j). EXPLICITLY DEFERRED per ADR-0030 §G.

This bead exists so the trigger conditions and design are documented; the work is NOT scheduled for v0.1.

ALGORITHM (when un-deferred): primal-dual interior-point method with HKM (Helmberg-Kojima-Monteiro) or NT (Nesterov-Todd) search direction, predictor-corrector step, free-variable handling, infeasibility detection via homogeneous self-dual embedding. SDPT3-equivalent. ~6-8k LOC of careful numerics over an estimated ~3 months.

References: Tutuncu-Toh-Todd 2003 'Solving Semidefinite-Quadratic-Linear Programs Using SDPT3' (Mathematical Programming Ser B); Helmberg-Rendl-Vanderbei-Wolkowicz 1996 (HKM direction); Nesterov-Todd 1997 'Self-Scaled Barriers and Interior-Point Methods for Convex Programming' (NT direction); Boyd-Vandenberghe Convex Optimisation Ch.11.

ACCURACY CEILING: 1e-10+.

TRIGGER CONDITIONS for un-deferring (any one):
  1. A real bench instance fails on cone-solve at 1e-6 ceiling AND the use case demands 1e-10.
  2. An adopted research workflow (e.g. numerical entanglement witnesses near the boundary, or LMI feasibility with tight margins) reports achieved_precision worse than the certificate's mathematical margin.
  3. The qinfo epic (hsxa) Phase 3+4 lands a tool whose accuracy contract requires 1e-10 SDP.

Until one of these fires, tools/cone-solve at 1e-6 is the SDP path. PRD §1.4 iteration culture is explicit: multiple overlapping tools are fine; the whale comes when the whale's cost is justified.

HAZARDS (where Opus 4.5 likely fell, documented for whoever picks this up):
  - PSD-cone step length: ratio test generalises from 'first negative coordinate' (LP) to 'first zero eigenvalue' (SDP); α = 1 / max λ(-L^{-1} dX L^{-T}) where LL^T = X
  - Cholesky breakdown on ill-conditioned Schur complement: regularisation (H + λI) + iterative refinement
  - HKM direction is asymmetric, NT is symmetric but more expensive
  - Infeasibility certificate via HSDE, not Phase-I/Phase-II

BLOCKED BY: cone-core substrate + benchmarks/sdp-sdplib corpus bench.
DEFERRED — do not claim or start without the user's explicit trigger.

title: [future direction] Shallow two-level tool-name namespace (tools/<family>/<operation>/)
description:
Scheduled when the catalog crosses ~80 tools (today: ~30). The flat tools/<name>/ layout was right at MVP scale; it loses the clustering signal at scale-of-100+. Filed per PRD §10.2 (added 2026-05-10) so the trigger condition is durable.

TARGET LAYOUT
  tools/qinfo/{partial-trace,tensor-product,trace-norm,trace-distance,fidelity,purity}/
  tools/cas/{simplify,verify,diff}/
  tools/linalg/{solve,qr,svd,eigh}/
  tools/integrate/{1d,ode-ivp,ode-stiff,ode-symplectic}/
  tools/poly/{factor,roots}/
  tools/solve/  (top-level dispatcher, stays single)
  tools/sturm/{simplify,execute,equivalent,sample,find,controlled,then,tensor,bennett-oracle,qecc-wrap}/
  tools/meijer/{g,g-symbolic-only,g-asymptotic-only,g-slater-only}/
  tools/hypergeometric/{pfq}/
  tools/groebner/{basis}/
  tools/real-roots/{isolate}/
  tools/alg-num/{arith}/
  tools/mod/{pow,inv}/
  tools/ntt/  (single, stays single)
  tools/registry/{list,search}/
  tools/expr/{parse}/
  tools/oracle/   (single, stays single)
  tools/entropy/{source}/

(Some families are 1-tool today and stay 1-tool; the shallow layout is for the multi-tool families and the single-tool ones can remain flat without breaking the convention.)

WIRE NAMING
- Tool name on the wire becomes 'qinfo.partial-trace' or 'qinfo/partial-trace' — separator choice deferred to an ADR. Dot-form matches schema-namespace convention; slash-form matches the on-disk path. Pick one in the ADR.
- Refusal envelopes carry the dotted name: tagged 'qinfo.partial-trace/qubit-out-of-range'.

MIGRATION SURFACE (small)
- Move tool directories (git mv preserves history).
- packages/contract/src/registry.ts: walk one level deeper (currently scans tools/*/tool.ts; needs tools/*/*/tool.ts).
- package.json workspaces glob: 'tools/*' -> ['tools/*', 'tools/*/*'] during transition; then 'tools/*/*' permanent.
- tools/<family>/<op>/tool.ts: NAME constant updated to dotted/slashed form.
- scripts/check.ts: ensure tool directory discovery handles two-level paths.
- README.md catalog table: regroup by family.
- All in-repo cross-references (worklog shards, ADRs, bench manifests, corpus adapters) updated. The corpus side will pin against the new wire name.

NON-BREAKING TRANSITION OPTION
The registry can be made temporarily-bivalent (accepts both flat and nested layouts) during the migration. After all tools are moved, the flat-path acceptance is dropped. ADR should decide whether to ship the bivalent layer or do a single atomic rename.

TRIGGER
- Catalog crosses ~80 tools (current cadence: ~10/worklog-cycle = 5 more cycles).
- OR: a substantive new tool family lands that pushes catalog past the readability cliff.
- OR: a user reports browsability friction.

Not urgent today; the cost of premature migration is real (every cross-reference, every external bench, every doc that names tools by path or wire-name). The cost of late migration is paid in catalog illegibility — recoverable, but visible.

WHY THIS IS PRD-LEVEL not just a bead
This is the first capacity-shaped decision where 'what an agent reaches for' produces an explicit affordance the workbench currently lacks. The PRD framing of agent-as-customer (§1.1) is operationalised here: the agent (me, while dogfooding D_W1 2026-05-10) noticed the catalog row count growing past the legibility threshold and named the remediation. Per the two-principles memory: 'a TS expert would type wb.qinfo.partialTrace(...) without thinking' — the shallow namespace is what makes that typed-barrel surface ergonomic.

title: @workbench/protocol: typed list<T>/record<T,K>/tagged<T> generic overloads for narrowed inference
description:
Surface friction from D_W1 dogfood 2026-05-10. The current list/record/tagged constructors from @workbench/protocol return the wide Value union types:
  list(items: Value[]): ListValue
  record(fields: Record<string, Value>): RecordValue

The typed barrel methods (wb.linalgEigh, etc) want narrowly-inferred types:
  wb.linalgEigh(input: { kind: 'record', fields: { A: ListValueOf<ListValueOf<Float64Value>> }})

Inline literal construction at the call site (demo-scope.ts:339-344) narrows automatically because TS infers from the literal context. The moment a TS expert REFACTORS the construction into a helper returning Value, narrowing is lost — the helper's return type must be cast at every call site with 'as never'.

This cuts directly against the TWO PRINCIPLES (memory:two-principles): a TS expert extracts helpers reflexively, and the workbench should be irresistible to TS experts.

FIX: add generic overloads on the constructors:
  function list<T extends Value>(items: T[]): ListValueOf<T>
  function record<F extends Record<string, Value>>(fields: F): RecordValueOf<{ [K in keyof F]: F[K] }>
  function tagged<T extends Value>(tag: string, payload: T): TaggedValueOf<T>

The wide-union signatures can remain as fallback overloads. ~10 LOC change in packages/protocol/src/kinds.ts; the typecheck phase will catch any narrowing regressions across the codebase.

After this lands, the matrix-helpers bead (matrixToValue etc) can drop its 'as never' casts.
close_reason: tagged + taggedSchema now generic in payload (mirrors list/record). Note: bead was 2/3 stale — list/record already generic when filed; only tagged remained. Worklog 111. Unblocks qiv8.

title: @workbench/json-bridge: matrixToValue / vectorFromValue / valueToMatrix helpers for numerical-tier ergonomics
description:
Surface friction from D_W1 dogfood 2026-05-10. Every numerical-tier call site re-derives the same boilerplate to lift a JS number[][] into a canonical list<list<float64>> Value and to unpack a returned list<float64> back to number[].

Inline construction (scripts/demo-scope.ts:339-344) looks like:
  list(M.map(row => list(row.map(x => float64FromNumber(x)))))

and result-narrowing for a length-n eigenvalue list looks like ~6 lines of
  .filter((it): it is { kind: 'float64' } & typeof it => it.kind === 'float64')
  .map(it => float64ToNumber(it as never))

Ship from @workbench/json-bridge:
  matrixToValue(M: number[][]): ListValueOf<ListValueOf<Float64Value>>
  valueToMatrix(v: Value): number[][]
  vectorToValue(v: number[]): ListValueOf<Float64Value>
  vectorFromValue(v: Value): number[]

Return-type-narrow so callers don't need 'as never' at the typed-barrel boundary (cf the typed-list overload bead). ~30 LOC + goldens + a docs paragraph showing the linalg-eigh call site rewritten with helpers.

Discovered while writing temp/qwasserstein.ts for the D_W1 dogfood — same boilerplate appears in scripts/demo-scope.ts already.
close_reason: Shipped matrixToValue / vectorToValue / valueToMatrix / valueToVector in @workbench/json-bridge. Forward direction returns narrow ListValueOf<...> (not widened to Value) so the typed-barrel slot composes cast-free; paired with 0y27 this delivers a fully cast-free numerical-tier call site. Reverse direction takes loose Value (proving shape IS the boilerplate). Naming normalised to valueTo* / *ToValue parallel (bead's vectorFromValue would have been inconsistent). 49 json-bridge tests (was 32; +17 round-trip, refusal, type-level narrow-return). Dogfood site rewritten in scripts/demo-scope.ts -- 3 lines shorter, no as never, output identical. Full bun run check green. Worklog 120.

title: tools/purity: gamma(rho) = tr(rho^2)
description:
Thin tool over @workbench/qinfo's purity. Input: record{rho: list<list<float64>>}. Output: record{value: float64, is_pure_within_tolerance: boolean, warnings: list<string>} | tagged 'purity/{non-square,non-finite-input}'.

Pure JS — no linalg subroutine needed (just sum of squared elements after a transpose-product). Numerical: true tier.

Invariants: 1/d <= purity <= 1 for density matrices on d-dimensional Hilbert space; purity=1 iff rho is pure; purity-preserving under unitary conjugation.

>=10 examples: pure state (=1); maximally mixed (=1/d); various rank-2 mixtures; refusal cases.

Part of the qinfo epic (hsxa) Phase 2; blocked by qinfo-substrate.
close_reason: Closed

title: tools/fidelity: Uhlmann fidelity F(rho, sigma) = tr(sqrt(sqrt(rho) sigma sqrt(rho)))^2
description:
Thin tool over @workbench/qinfo's fidelity. Input: record{rho: list<list<float64>>, sigma: list<list<float64>>}. Output: record{value: float64, method: string, warnings: list<string>} | tagged 'fidelity/{shape-mismatch,non-finite-input,non-density-matrix}'.

Computation: matrix square root via eigendecomposition (rho = Q diag(lambda) Q^T, sqrt(rho) = Q diag(sqrt(lambda)) Q^T after PSD-projection of any negative eigenvalues within tolerance). Three linalg-eigh calls (sqrt(rho), then sqrt(rho) sigma sqrt(rho), then sum sqrt of its eigenvalues).

Invariants: 0 <= F <= 1; F(rho,sigma) = F(sigma,rho); F(rho,rho) = 1; for pure states |psi><psi| and |phi><phi|, F = |<psi|phi>|^2; Fuchs-van-de-Graaf D <= sqrt(1-F) <= sqrt(2 D).

>=10 examples: identical states (=1); orthogonal pure states (=0); pure vs maximally mixed; Bell vs separable; Fuchs-van-de-Graaf probe.

Part of the qinfo epic (hsxa) Phase 2; blocked by qinfo-substrate.
close_reason: Closed

title: tools/trace-distance: D(rho, sigma) = (1/2)||rho-sigma||_1
description:
Thin tool over @workbench/qinfo's traceDistance. Input: record{rho: list<list<float64>>, sigma: list<list<float64>>}. Output: record{value: float64, method: string, warnings: list<string>} | tagged 'trace-distance/{shape-mismatch,non-finite-input,non-density-matrix}'.

Validates rho and sigma are density matrices (Hermitian, PSD, tr=1) within tolerance and emits warnings on weak violations; tags on hard violations.

Invariants: 0 <= D(rho,sigma) <= 1 for density matrices; symmetry D(rho,sigma)=D(sigma,rho); identity D(rho,rho)=0; triangle inequality D(rho,tau) <= D(rho,sigma) + D(sigma,tau); maximum D=1 iff rho-sigma has orthogonal support.

>=10 examples: orthogonal pure states (=1); identical states (=0); pure vs maximally mixed (=1/2); Bell vs separable; triangle probe.

Part of the qinfo epic (hsxa) Phase 2; blocked by qinfo-substrate.
close_reason: Closed

title: corpus schema: structured [meta.known_failures] field for graded benchmarks
description:
The corpus's benchmark-suite schema currently has additionalProperties:false on [meta] (schema/benchmark-suite.schema.json:meta), so known-failing cases can only be encoded as prose in [meta.description]. This is fine as a stopgap (see benchmarks/solve/manifest.toml at corpus@<TBD> for the prose convention) but a structured field is what a TS-expert grading-harness reader would reach for.

Proposed shape:

  [meta.known_failures]
  cases        = ["rand-trans-002", ...]
  linked_beads = ["scientist-workbench-b55", "scientist-workbench-3g9x"]
  classification = {
    "rand-trans-002" = "upgraded-post-bench",
    "rand-trans-004" = "not-yet-shipped",
    ...
  }
  note         = "..."

Consequences:
- src/schema.ts BenchmarkSuite type extension
- src/validator.ts: case IDs in known_failures must be a subset of inputs.json case IDs
- src/grade.ts: failures listed in known_failures count separately (e.g. "94/100 cases pass; 6/6 known failures expected; suite passes") — or alternatively grade.ts treats them as informational and the corpus DuckDB grade_results table gets a new column 'known_failure: bool'
- queries/grade-vs-corpus.sql: optionally exclude known failures from headline pass count

Filed in scientist-workbench during the ADR-0028 batch-3 migration of bench/solve, where the prose convention was first applied (94/100 grading honest, 6 cases tracked by scientist-workbench-3g9x). Lives in scientist-workbench beads since the corpus repo doesn't run beads itself; cross-repo design coordination acceptable here.

Acceptance: a fresh agent landing on a corpus benchmark sees its known failures programmatically (DuckDB query or schema-driven UI), not buried in description prose.

title: FlagsArgOf<D> typed-barrel lift for arbprec: true tools (DX, no runtime impact)
description: Worklog 083 (arbprec --precision flag wiring; lc1 / rn2 fixes) landed the runtime contract — runWorkbench validates partial flags against toolFacingFlags(def.flags ?? {}, def.arbprec === true) and the runner threads --precision=N into flags.precision correctly. Both surfaces honour the flag at runtime. The typed-barrel surface (wb.hypergeometricPfq(input, { precision: 50n })) still requires an 'as never' cast on the flags argument because FlagsArgOf<typeof def> does not lift precision?: bigint for arbprec: true tools. Root cause: defineTool<I, O, Fl> does not preserve the arbprec: true literal in the returned ToolDefinition's static type (the field is arbprec?: boolean), so the conditional D extends { arbprec: true } never matches at the typed-barrel call site. Fix: thread an Ar extends boolean = false generic through ToolDefinition and defineTool so the literal is preserved; lift FlagsArgOf to inject precision?: bigint when Ar = true. Touches: ToolDefinition type, defineTool's return-type inference, FlagsArgOf in @workbench/compose. Acceptance: typed-barrel call wb.hypergeometricPfq(input, { precision: 50n }) typechecks with no 'as never' cast; existing wb.run(...) calls unaffected.
close_reason: Fixed: ToolDefinition gains an Ar extends boolean = boolean generic with arbprec?: Ar (preserves the literal); defineTool mirrors it; FlagsArgOf<D> rewritten as a two-tier nested conditional (no intersection) that lifts { precision?: bigint } for arbprec tools and keeps a strict-empty fallback so non-arbprec tools reject { precision: ... } at compile time. Two 'as never' casts deleted from compose.test.ts -- bead's acceptance criterion met. 3 new type-level tests in 'typed barrel -- arbprec lift (bead 0y27)' block: positive Required<FlagsArgOf<...>> extends { precision: bigint }, negative @ts-expect-error on modPow rejection, runtime cast-free end-to-end. Mutation-proven (drop lift -> RED, re-widen slot -> RED). Honest finding: 'const' on Ar turned out to be redundant (TS regular inference already narrows arbprec: true with the constraint Ar extends boolean); kept for defensive consistency with const Fl sibling. Full bun run check green (95/0/7). Worklog 118.

title: hv0.9.3 — Olde Daalhuis–Olver hyperasymptotic refinement
description: The v0.1 asymptotic is 'superasymptotic' (Olver 1974 §3.7): truncated at k* it has error |t_{k*+1}|. Hyperasymptotics (Olde Daalhuis & Olver 1995, *Methods Appl. Anal.* 2: 173–197) recovers exponentially-small accuracy across Stokes lines via Borel resummation of the divergent tail. Multi-session-scale work; beyond v0.1 budget. References: Olde Daalhuis & Olver 1995 Methods Appl. Anal. 2: 173-197; Berry & Howls 1990 Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A 430: 653-668. Acceptance: implement at least the level-1 hyperasymptotic refinement (the first re-expansion of the tail); verify accuracy improvement: at fixed precision, the hyperasymptotic answer is one Stokes-multiplier order more accurate than the v0.1 superasymptotic.

title: meijer-core dispatch: richer pattern grammar (linear relations, recursive G)
description: v0.1 ships SlotSpec ∈ {lit-int, lit-rat, free, free-shift} and RelationSpec ∈ {integer-difference}. As the rule corpus grows past ~200 rules, several PBM and Wolfram entries need richer pattern shapes: linear-relation (cross-slot guard c1·a + c2·b = c3 for arbitrary integer coefficients); pattern-list (matching a sub-tuple's *length* dynamically; some PBM entries are families parametrised by the count of integer spacings, e.g. Γ(1+a) Γ(1+a-1) ... Γ(1+a-k) for arbitrary k); recursive-G (rule's RHS is a smaller Meijer G; v0.1 emits the bare reduced head, but downstream tools/meijer-g (top-level dispatcher, hv0.10) needs to recurse into it. Add a stop-condition to prevent infinite recursion + a depth limit). Add tests for each new grammar feature using a curated rule from PBM that needs it.

title: meijer-core dispatch: argument-transformation infrastructure

title: packages/quadrature: tanh-sinh (double-exponential) driver — deferred follow-up to hv0.7
description:
Speculative/defensive follow-up to hv0.7. NOT scheduled — claim only if a real workload reports the limitation it addresses.

## Background

ADR-0021 §"What we will not decide" flags tanh-sinh as the canonical algorithm for high-precision smooth integration that K15+adaptive does not handle well. Concretely:

- gaussKronrodAdaptiveBF saturates at ~30 dps on smooth analytic integrands with bounded Taylor radius (e.g. 1/(1+x²) — see worklog 072 for the empirical convergence trajectory).
- For entire functions (sin, exp) it scales further (sin at 80 dps converges).
- For oscillatory and weakly-singular integrands it converges efficiently.

K15+adaptive's algebraic error decay is ~1/N^k under bisection (k = G7's exactness order = 13). For 50+ dps targets on bounded-radius analytic integrands, that requires astronomical iteration counts.

Tanh-sinh (double-exponential) quadrature has DOUBLY-exponential convergence in number of nodes — typically O(prec) function evaluations to achieve any reasonable user precision, regardless of the integrand class (smooth, weakly-endpoint-singular, or with bounded Taylor radius). It's the canonical high-precision rule used by mpmath's `quad`, Arb's `acb_calc_integrate`, and Mathematica's NIntegrate at high precision.

## Why defensive

The near-term consumers of `gaussKronrodAdaptiveBF` are:

- hv0.8 Mellin-Barnes contour quadrature: integrand is oscillatory (Γ-product · z^s along a vertical line). K15 is well-suited; tanh-sinh would not be obviously better.
- tools/meijer-g (hv0.10) at default prec ≤ 50 on the integrand classes the Slater path doesn't already cover.

Neither has a documented need for tanh-sinh. So this bead is speculative — placeholder for the case where:

- A future bench reports stalling on smooth-analytic integrands at high prec.
- Verification against mpmath's quadosc at 100+ dps starts requiring it.
- A new consumer (problem-13 verifier itself? a downstream tool?) needs the precision class K15 cannot reach.

## What would ship

Mirror the gaussKronrodAdaptiveBF surface for symmetry:

```
tanhSinhAdaptiveBF(
  f: (x: BigFloat, prec: number) => BigFloat,
  a: BigFloat,
  b: BigFloat,
  prec: number,
  opts?: TanhSinhOptions,
): BigFloatQuadResult
```

Algorithm: double-exponential variable transformation x = tanh((π/2)·sinh(t)) maps t ∈ ℝ to x ∈ (-1, 1). Endpoints transform to ±∞; the integrand's behaviour at ±1 (including weak singularities) is absorbed by the Jacobian's doubly-exponential decay. Quadrature: trapezoidal rule on equally-spaced t-nodes, bisecting the spacing until convergence (each bisection roughly doubles the achieved precision — doubly-exponential).

Storage: precomputed (t_k, x_k, w_k) tuples at progressively finer spacings (H, H/2, H/4, ...) at the substrate's max supported precision. Or compute on-demand via the bigfloat substrate's tanh and sinh — both are already shipped.

Pure TS, BigInt-backed. Inherits ADR-0020's bit-determinism contract.

## Acceptance (if claimed)

- New file packages/quadrature/src/tanh-sinh-bf.ts.
